- Erasure never touches `reservations`, so a hold's `release_reason` and `notes` outlive Article 17. That is added to the open erasure decision.

**Review.** Three read-only lenses (correctness, tests, docs), two refuters per finding. Correctness found nothing. Confirmed (low) and fixed: the unit test did not prove the UPDATE names THIS hold — the read before it filters on the id too; now only the filters chained after the update count, as in the lead test — and this entry's "Confirm or Convert" (Convert is not live; its reason reaches the row). Refuted but cheap, also done: typed legacy reasons on confirmed / converted / expired in the renderer test, a positive anchor for the e2e dashboard check, and an exact e2e comment.

**Compatibility and deploy order.** No migration, no hosted step, not deploy-coupled: an old app renders a new payload as `Reservation {from} → {to}`, and a new app renders an old one the same. Evidence reports whose rows held a release reason recompute to a different content hash if regenerated; verification is by `pdf_sha256` (see T-event-typed-text-shape). Order: branch CI green → merge → deploy READY → probes.

## T-media-file-name-shape — a photo's events carry its id and the digest of its bytes, never its file name (2026-09-25; no migration)

**The leak** (operator: "fix the photo file name leak next"; BACKLOG "More event payloads carry typed text by value"). Inspected at `0b0a3ad` (`origin/main` when the work began), with a read-only scouting workflow (three readers and a critic).
- `uploadPropertyMedia` (`lib/actions/media.ts:167-174`) logged `media_uploaded` as `{ media_id, file: file.name, kind, watermarked }`. The name is whatever the uploader's machine called the file ("Andreou villa front.jpg"), and an ASSIGNED AGENT uploads too, not only admins and listing managers (`property_media_insert`, 0002/0100). The importer (`scripts/import/media.mts:254-261`) wrote `{ media_id, file: name, … }` the same way.
- `deleteMediaBulk` (`media.ts:447-493`) READ the name back out of the property's old `media_uploaded` events, with the ADMIN client (the lookup the 2026-07-16 audit added so "Photo deleted" named the photo), and copied it into the new `media_deleted`. The chain fed itself typed text, and would have kept doing so from old events after the writers stopped.
- `mediaUploadedFile` / `mediaDeletedFile` printed the name on the property's Activity tab and the admin feed. The evidence report excludes these two types (`MEDIA_NOISE`).
- **Hosted, read-only, counts only:** 35 `media_uploaded` events, all with a `file`; 29 of 35 `media_deleted` with one (copied forward); 0 `media_alt_set`. They stay (the chain cannot be edited) and are no longer printed.
- **RED first**, through the real actions and the real `logEvent` (`lib/actions/media-event-payload.test.ts`: a real sharp image named with a synthetic person and phone). 7 of 9 failed on `0b0a3ad`: the four upload cases because the payload carried the name and no digest; the three delete cases on `admin.from is not a function`, because the admin stand-in holds storage only, so the old events lookup could not run. The 2 controls — a rejected row and a refused delete — log nothing.

**What the timeline can honestly say.** `property_media` never stored a name: its columns are ids, generated UUID paths, `kind`, size, `alt`, `content_sha256` (0088). Storage never received one either (`binaryBody` is a nameless Blob). So there is no "current title" to join, and a deleted photo has no row at all. The lines are the fact — "Photo uploaded" / "Photo deleted" — as `media_cover_set` and `media_reordered` have always been.

**The fix.**
- `media_uploaded` = `{ media_id, kind, watermarked, content_sha256 }`. The digest is the ROW's own `content_sha256` — one computation, the same fact on the row and in the event — of the ORIGINAL bytes. It is a digest of an image, not of the removed text, and it keeps the trace the names gave: the 2026-09-07 cleanup used them to find six borrowed images across four listings, including photos already deleted, and `content_sha256` on the row covers only photos that still exist.
- `media_deleted` = `{ media_id, content_sha256?, bulk? }`, the digest read from the row the delete itself returns (the select now names the column). An imported photo whose digest was never backfilled gets no key, not a null. The admin events lookup is GONE; the admin client stays for storage removal only.
- The importer (`scripts/import/media.mts`) now hashes the original bytes once and writes the digest to the row AND the event — `{ media_id, watermarked, content_sha256, source: "import_script" }` — as the action does. Before, it computed none, so an imported photo's row stayed null until someone ran `backfill-hashes.mjs`, and a delete before that would have left no trace of which image it was.
- The lines print `mediaUploaded` / `mediaDeleted` for any payload, old or new, whoever wrote it — any staff member can insert an event with any payload (`events_insert`, 0071), so the renderer must not trust `file` at all. `mediaUploadedFile` / `mediaDeletedFile` are gone in EN, EL and RU, and `{file}` leaves `messages.test.ts`'s sample parameters.
- `lib/actions/media-deleted-keeps-the-name.test.ts` is DELETED. Its premise was the name's recovery; the new file pins the opposite, including that the system is never asked for events.

**Tests.**
- The writer test above: 9/9 after the fix — exact upload payloads for a photo and a floor plan, the event's digest equal to the row's, one event per file of a multi-file upload, the delete's exact payload with storage removal unchanged, the select naming `content_sha256`, a bulk delete (one photo without a digest), and the controls. Every inserted row is searched for the synthetic file name's words.
- `events.test.ts`: legacy upload, import and delete payloads WITH a file name render the bare lines; new payloads the same; malformed payloads do not throw; both go through the translator. The old test pinning "Photo deleted — images (4).jpg" now pins its absence.
- `tests/e2e/event-typed-text.spec.ts` gains a photo flow through the real Media tab: a sharp-made JPEG uploaded under a synthetic personal name, then deleted through the tile's own button. The stored payloads are exact, with the digest equal to the image's and the row's. The Activity tab shows one "Photo uploaded" and one "Photo deleted" with none of the name's words. Its teardown removes any stored objects (rows cascade with the property, files do not). The whole spec passes on desktop AND mobile (14/14).
- Mutation proofs (one exact replacement each, restored after): 8 of 8 killed. They cover the name restored or truncated under another key, the digest dropped, a null digest written, the admin events read restored, the select losing `content_sha256`, and each line printing a legacy name.

**Not changed here.**
- `media_alt_set`'s alt text: staff-written, PUBLISHED marketing copy, which T-updated-event-shape-only keeps by value on purpose — now a BACKLOG NOTE with the facts, including that it is missing from `MEDIA_NOISE`.
- The floor-plan wording: the lines say "Photo" for a floor plan too, as before.
- The scouts and the review found another identity-in-chain writer, in both row importers: `imported` carries a contact's name, or an owner's PHONE number (`properties.mts`: `name ?? phone`). It is on BACKLOG, with a VERIFY grep per importer.

**Review.** Four read-only lenses (correctness, security, tests, docs), two refuters per finding; nothing wrong with the fix itself. Confirmed and fixed:
- BACKLOG's importer item missed `properties.mts`'s owner name-or-phone, and its grep would have gone silent with it open;
- the delete tests could not catch the chain lookup coming back on the CALLER's client — the caller's fake now holds an old upload event WITH the name, and the test pins that `events` is never read;
- no test covered the importer's event — `scripts/import/entry-points.test.ts`'s PostgREST stand-in now records request bodies and serves a property, and a live run of `media.mts` over a sharp-made JPEG with a person's name pins the exact event body and the row's digest;
- the importer wrote no digest (one vote), which undercut the reason for adding one — it now hashes, as above.
Refuted but cheap, also done: the storage assertions name their bucket (renditions from `media`, the original from `documents`), and the e2e inserts an older upload event WITH the file name before reading the Activity tab, so its "no file name" check can fail.

**Compatibility and deploy order.** No migration, no hosted step, not deploy-coupled: an old app renders a new payload as the bare line (its `file` branch finds nothing), and a new app renders an old payload the same. The evidence report never included these two types, so no report hash moves. The public feed and portals read no events and carried no names. Order: branch CI green → merge → deploy READY → probes.

**Landing (2026-09-25 early morning).** On the operator's word ("merge, confirm the deploy, then check the live site"). Main had not moved (`88f0438`, the PR's base). PR #63 → main `0626680`, pinned to `39de646` (branch CI green on `021898a` and `39de646`). Vercel production `dpl_6pM9YPxLbaHVN2ZVtx4eYU25eB9Y` READY and aliased. CI on the merge commit green (run 36094716152: checks, rls, e2e). Verified read-only in the operator's Chrome: the test property with the most named photo events shows, on its Activity tab (latest 50 lines), 36 photo lines, all bare (13 "Photo uploaded", 17 "Photo deleted", 6 "Photos reordered"), none with a dash or a file name; the check reported counts and never printed a line's text. The request is on the new deployment in Vercel's logs (200), with no runtime errors and no new Sentry issue. `/login` 200 with the CSP nonce on 16 of 16 scripts; protected routes 307. Nothing on hosted. Remote branch deleted, worktree removed.

## T-escalation-recovery-reason-shape — an escalation recovery's event carries no typed reason (2026-09-25; migration 0115)

**The leak (verified against `f075f9b`).** `request_lead_escalation_recovery` (0111, the latest body; 0112 did not re-create it) wrote the admin-typed resend reason, up to 200 characters, into the `lead_escalation` / `recovery_requested` event as `'reason', v_reason`. The events table is append-only and hash-chained, so nothing written there can be erased or corrected (SEC-03). Nothing ever read it: there is no `lead_escalation` entry in `EVENT_LINES` and no lead timeline page, so the dialog's promise "Kept on the lead's timeline with your name" was never kept. The chain was the text's only home, and the TypeScript payload scan cannot see SQL. Reproduced on the local stack at 0114 by `supabase/tests/lead-escalation-recovery.test.ts`: a synthetic name, phone and address passed as `p_reason` landed in the lead's events (red), a resend without a reason was refused, and the retry event carried `reason: null`.

**Decision: drop the text, not move it.** The pattern in this series keeps descriptive text on its source record. Here there is no source record: the job row never held the reason, and nothing reads it. A new column would need its own erasure rule for text nobody reads, so the text is no longer collected at all. A required field that nothing keeps would tell the admin a falsehood. The audit fact stays whole in the event: the admin as actor, the time, `action`, `provider`, `job_id`, `key_serial`, `key_rotated`, and `previous_state` / `previous_category` / `previous_result`, which record why the worker had stopped. The friction that matters stays: the database still admits `resend` only when `retry` is unsafe, and Review & resend is a dialog that states the duplicate risk and needs an explicit confirmation.

**Migration 0115** (`escalation_recovery_reason_shape`) re-creates the function from 0111's text, generated by removal, with exactly three removals (a `diff` of the two bodies shows only them): the `'reason'` key, the refusal "A reason is required to resend under a new key.", and the `v_reason` variable with its 200-character cut. `p_reason` stays in the signature, accepted and ignored. Dropping it would change the arity, and the deployed code sends it on a resend, so it would fail CLOSED until the new code deployed. With the parameter kept, the apply is not deploy-coupled in either order. The return shape, security (SECURITY DEFINER, `search_path`) and grants are unchanged; the grants are re-stated anyway. Apply-time assertions: exactly one function by that name; the signature, SECURITY DEFINER and `search_path`; the body contains no `v_reason`, `'reason'` or `p_reason`, but still contains `recovery_requested`, `previous_result` and `key_rotated`; the ACLs; and the first refusal without a session. `database.types.ts` is unchanged (same arguments). The restore pin moves to 115.

**App.** `recoverLeadEscalation` no longer takes a `reason`; `z.object` strips the key that a browser loaded before this deploy still posts, so it never reaches the database. The Review & resend dialog loses the Reason box and says "The audit log records that you resent it, when, and why the worker stopped." There is no lead timeline, so the text does not say "timeline". Confirm is enabled unless a request is pending.

**Tests.** DB (`supabase/tests/lead-escalation-recovery.test.ts`, 15/15): the retry and resend events have no `reason` property; a resend with no reason is admitted; a `p_reason` from an old caller holding a synthetic name, phone and address appears nowhere in the lead's events or the job row. 3 of these were watched RED at 0114 and GREEN at 0115. Unit (`lib/actions/leads-recover-escalation.test.ts`): the RPC receives only `p_job_id` and `p_action`, even when a stale caller posts a reason (watched red first). E2E (`tests/e2e/lead-escalation-recovery.spec.ts`, desktop and mobile, 8/8 with setup): the dialog has no textbox and shows the audit-log sentence; opening it moves nothing; both events lack `reason`. Measured 2026-09-25: tsc 0 (`--incremental false`); eslint 0 on the whole tree; unit 2676/2676 across 206 files; `npm run build` exit 0; the full DB suite 364/370. The 6 reds are the known residue on this local stack (41/42/57, `enquiry-alert-sweep-runs` connect_error, `enquiry-alerts-cron`) plus `postgis-catalog-guard` "anon may not update", which passes alone both on untouched main and on this branch (a load flake).

**Hosted.** Read-only, counts only, 2026-09-25: hosted at 0114, **0** `recovery_requested` events, so no historical copy exists to decide about.

**Deploy order.** Either order is safe. Following the usual additive order: branch CI green → hosted 0115 (one `execute_sql` with the file's text, verified separately: prosrc digest = local, ACLs, ledger 115, advisors unchanged) → merge → deploy READY. An old app against 0115: its reason is ignored and a resend without one is now admitted. A new app against 0114: a resend is refused with the old sentence "A reason is required…" (fails CLOSED), and retry is unaffected. Rollback: revert the merge, then re-create 0111's body (the file's function text) if the old requirement must return.

**Landing (2026-09-25, late morning).** On the operator's word ("apply 0115 to hosted and merge #64"). Hosted first: its function body was 0111's (md5 `cf6f385c…`); 0115 applied in one `execute_sql` with the file's text, its assertions passed; verified separately: body md5 `bf6060c8…` = local, one overload, SECURITY DEFINER and `search_path` kept, ACL unchanged, ledger by hand at 115, advisors unchanged (2 ERR + 36 WARN, by design). Then PR #64 → main `8b3b313`, pinned to `e3ae0d3` (branch CI green: checks, rls, e2e; main unmoved). Vercel production `dpl_14cRt53tGch9WoTYL6o8yYQYcQZD` READY; CI on the merge commit green (run 36116353647: checks, rls, e2e); `/login` 200, protected routes 307, no runtime errors. Escalation stays paused, so no recovery was exercised in production; the behaviour is proven by the DB suite on CI's fresh database.

## T-viewing-feedback-shape — a viewing's feedback event carries its rating, never the buyer's words (2026-09-25; no migration)

**The leak** (operator: "fix the viewing feedback leak next"; BACKLOG "More event payloads carry typed text by value"). Inspected at `fff6f96` (`origin/main` when the work began), with a read-only mapping workflow (four readers and a completeness critic, which re-read the RLS and erasure claims against the migrations itself).
- `saveViewingFeedback` (`lib/actions/viewings.ts`) spread the whole feedback object, `{ rating, liked, disliked, comment }`, into the hash-chained `viewing_feedback` event on the PROPERTY. `liked` / `disliked` / `comment` are the buyer's words, typed by the agent, up to 2000 characters each, and they name people ("her husband Andreas wants a bigger garden"). The payload shape had not changed since T4.3 (`f82a68b`); it was the one writer the payload scan's `REVIEWED` map excused.
- The `viewing_feedback` line printed the comment (else `liked`) on three surfaces: the property's Activity tab (every role of the org), the admin dashboard's feed, and the commission evidence report when it is scoped to a property. That report lists EVERY viewing's feedback on the property, other buyers' included, and it is a dispute document made to leave the office (`docs/01_PROJECT_CONTEXT.md` 41/310). Its lines go into `reportContentHash` and into the stored PDF, which is not erasable by design.
- **A crash, found by the critic and proven RED:** the renderer is keyed by event type alone and any active org member may insert any payload (`events_insert`, 0071). `"★".repeat(rating)` with a forged `rating: 1e9` threw `RangeError: Invalid string length`, which would take the property page, the admin feed and evidence generation down for everyone.
- **Hosted, read-only, counts only:** 0 viewings, 0 `viewing_feedback` events. No historical copy exists.
- Name clash, kept apart throughout: the follow-up TASK kind `viewing_feedback` (the 48-hour nudge, SQL 0020…0078) reads `viewings.feedback` on the ROW and is unaffected.

**Verified, not assumed** (the mapping, re-checked by the critic): `viewings_select` and `properties_select` are both org-wide (0030:113-116, 150-153, not redefined since), so everyone who can see a property's Activity tab can read its viewings; the property page has NO other path to a past viewing's feedback (its viewings card lists scheduled ones only; the calendar has no property filter), so a bare line would have silently dropped the C7 acceptance; feedback is overwritten by every save and each save logs an event; erasure never touches `viewings.feedback`.

**The fix.**
- **Writer:** the payload is `{ viewing_id, reference, rating }`, built explicitly. `rating` is the form's 1–5 score (not typed text), `reference` the office's own property code, `viewing_id` the only link back to the row. The row keeps all four fields. The read, the admin-or-own guard, the completed-only rule and the proven UPDATE (zero rows → refused, nothing logged) are unchanged.
- **Renderer:** prints `Viewing feedback` plus the stars and nothing else, from ANY payload, old or new — and stars only for an integer 1–5, so a forged rating renders the bare line instead of throwing. `viewingFeedbackNote` / `viewingFeedbackStarsNote` are gone in EN/EL/RU; `{note}` left `messages.test.ts`.
- **Current context, not history.** `attachCurrentTitles` (`lib/services/event-context.ts`) also attaches `current_feedback`: the viewing's comment, else what was liked (the two the line used to print), read from `viewings.feedback` on the VIEWER's client in one batched, org-bounded, uuid-filtered query per page. It is labelled "current feedback: …" (`currentFeedback`, EN/EL/RU) and rendered after the line, never inside it. Only the NEWEST `viewing_feedback` event per viewing on the page carries it (by `occurred_at`), so an older save never shows today's wording beside it; only a `property` event; only when the viewing's `property_id` is the event's own property (a crafted event cannot pull one property's feedback onto another's timeline); never a fallback to any payload. The evidence report attaches nothing — its lines are the neutral ones.
- **Why a join here, when the lost-reason and release-reason fixes chose none:** those rows' text is shown elsewhere (the deal header, the leads inbox, "Earlier holds"); a viewing's feedback had no other surface on the property page, and C7 asks for it there. The mutable-row objection is met by labelling it current and attaching it to the newest save only. This reverses T4.3's "without the timeline query needing to join viewings": the join exists now, on the viewer's client, precisely so the words can leave the chain.
- **Payload scan:** `FORBIDDEN` gains `comment`, `liked` and `disliked` (whole `_` parts are matched, so `liked` would not have covered `disliked`); the `viewings.ts` `...feedback` exception is gone. The scan now refuses the words as literal keys too, which a spread-only rule would have let straight back in. It cannot see a renamed key, so the behavioural test below is the proof.

**Tests.** Every new test was watched RED on the old code first.
- `lib/actions/viewing-feedback-event-payload.test.ts` (new): the REAL action and the REAL `logEvent` over the fake transport. The row receives all four fields; ONE event with exactly `{ viewing_id, reference, rating }`; none of eight synthetic words (a name, a phone, an address, the opinions) anywhere in the inserted row; rating-only and admin saves; refused (0 rows) and failed updates, not-completed / not-yours / unreadable viewings and invalid input log nothing. RED at the old code: 4 of 8 (the payload carried six keys and all eight words).
- `lib/services/events.test.ts`: legacy payloads with the words (and a crafted one on a contact) render the bare line with stars; new payloads; `1e9`, `Infinity`, `2.5`, `0`, `-3`, `6`, a word and an object print no stars and never throw (`1e9` threw `RangeError` at the old code); the translator routes; `describeEventContext` labels current feedback.
- `lib/services/event-context.test.ts`: one viewings read on the viewer's client with the org filter; newest per viewing whatever the page order; no payload fallback for a missing row, null feedback or blank text; another property's viewing gets nothing; property events only; malformed ids never sent; a failed read logs a count and no words; tasks and viewings side by side.
- `lib/services/evidence.test.ts`: a property-scoped report with another buyer's legacy feedback prints only `Viewing feedback ★★★★` / `★★`, and never selects the feedback column.
- `supabase/tests/event-context.test.ts` (real database): admin, an agent who is not the viewing's agent, and a listing manager all read their own org's current feedback; the other org's admin reads only theirs; naming the other org buys nothing; an event naming another property's viewing gets nothing even for an admin.
- `tests/e2e/event-typed-text.spec.ts`: a completed viewing, an older-shape event WITH words inserted first, then the real form. The row holds all four fields, the event is exactly `{ viewing_id, reference, rating }`, the viewing page shows the words; the Activity tab shows the new line with `current feedback: <comment>` and the older line with its stars only; after "Update feedback" the newest line alone carries the NEW comment and the old one is nowhere; the admin feed shows the same, with no legacy words. RED at the old code (stash of the implementation): the stored payload carried three extra keys.

**Review** (an adversarial workflow over `6ed5c8e`: five lenses — logic, privacy, tests, i18n/UX, contract — each finding judged by three skeptics told to refute it, majority survives; then mutation proofs in a detached copy). No defect in the change itself; nine findings confirmed, all fixed here:
- **Letter case (2/3):** `z.guid()` admits an uppercase id, Postgres answers in lowercase, and the newest-per-viewing map was keyed by the raw string — a hand-made form post naming the viewing in uppercase made the OLDER save carry today's words (reproduced by two skeptics with a probe). `payloadId` now lowercases; the new test uses an id with hex LETTERS (a first version used an all-digit id, which `toUpperCase()` leaves alone, and passed on the old code too — caught by running it there).
- **Tests that could not fail (3/3 each):** the payload test's `.eq("id")` check matched the READ, not the UPDATE — now only filters chained after the update count; the evidence guard used non-uuid viewing ids, so no reader would ever have been asked — now real uuids and a scripted page of rows whose words the report would print, and wiring `attachCurrentTitles` into `assembleEvidence` was confirmed to turn it RED.
- **Stale record (3/3 each):** this entry and the BACKLOG strike did not exist yet; the `reportContentHash` docstring, `viewing-status-refused.test.ts` (its rationale and three test names said feedback was "published" to the timeline), and the caller comments in `event-timeline.tsx`, `admin-dashboard.tsx` and `entity-timeline.ts` named only a current title. All updated.
- **Erasure (2/3):** `viewings.feedback` is now the words' only home and erasure never touches it — recorded on the BACKLOG erasure-decision entry, not changed.
- **Rejected as this change's defect, recorded:** the `rescheduled` line crashes the same three surfaces on a forged `{ from: "x" }` (`formatDateTime` → `RangeError`). All three skeptics confirmed the crash and that it predates this change (`ebcfec5`) — a new BACKLOG item.
- **Mutation proofs:** 14 of 14 killed — the words back in the payload (explicit and as a spread), the renderer printing a comment, the old `isFinite && > 0` guard, attaching to every save, dropping the property match / the org filter / the property-only rule, a payload fallback, `liked` before `comment`, dropping the label, `disliked` out of FORBIDDEN, a missing Greek key, and reading viewings through the admin client.

**Measured** (the branch, local stack at 0115, 2026-09-25): tsc 0 (`--incremental false`); eslint 0 on the whole tree; unit 2710/2710 across 207 files; the database suite 370/375 — the 5 reds are the known residue on this stack (rls 41/42/57, `enquiry-alert-sweep-runs` connect_error, `enquiry-alerts-cron`), identical on `main`; `supabase/tests/event-context.test.ts` 11/11 (five new: every role of the org, the other org, naming the other org, another property's viewing); e2e 122/122 across nine specs touching viewings, feedback and the nudges (`event-typed-text`, `nudges`, `viewing-confirmation`, `viewing-reschedule`, `viewings-export`, `viewings-window`, `slip-pdf-hash`, `contact-merge`, `security`), desktop AND mobile; `npm run build` exit 0 and `check:static-routes` ok.

**Compatibility and deploy order.** No migration, nothing on hosted, not deploy-coupled: an old app renders a new payload as stars (its `comment` branch finds nothing); a new app renders an old payload as stars. A property-scoped evidence report generated BEFORE this change that included feedback words recomputes to a different `reportContentHash` (verification is by `pdf_sha256`, unaffected); hosted has 0 such events, so no such report exists. Order: branch CI green → merge → deploy READY → probes.

**Not changed here.**

## T-imported-identity-shape — an imported person is named on the row, never in the chain (2026-09-25; no migration)

**The leak** (operator: "fix the importer identity leak next"; BACKLOG "More event payloads carry typed text by value" — the last TypeScript writer on that list). Inspected at `a4a1f43`, with a read-only mapping workflow (writers, consumers, test harness, precedent; a completeness critic re-read the migrations, the harness and the configs itself).
- `scripts/import/contacts.mts` logged `imported` with `{ name }` — the row's first + last name, else its company name (exactly `contacts.display_name`) — through `logImported` (`scripts/import/_shared.mts`, which spreads the caller's keys into `{ source: "csv_import", … }`, actor null).
- `scripts/import/properties.mts` logged the OWNER contact it creates with `{ name: name ?? phone, as: "owner" }`. **Correction found by the critic:** the phone fallback cannot reach a real database — `contact_has_name` (0001) refuses a nameless owner insert before the event is written; it was a latent path (the stand-in enforces no CHECK). The live leak on that path is the owner's NAME.
- The `imported` line printed `reference ?? name`: the contact's Activity tab (anyone who can open the contact), the admin feed, and an admin's un-narrowed evidence report (`events_select` hides actor-null rows from everyone else). Identity in an append-only chain that neither erasure (which never edits events and keeps identity on the row) nor an Article 16 correction can reach — the T-merged-event-ids-only rule.
- **Hosted, read-only, counts only:** 0 `imported` events. No chain copy exists.

**The fix.**
- **Writers:** a contact import logs `{ source, batch }`; the owner contact `{ source, as: "owner", batch }` (`as` is the role that created it, which the row also holds). The mandate `{ source, property, batch }` and property `{ source, reference, batch, visibility, score, published_at? }` events are unchanged — `reference` is the office's own code, not a person. The local import report keeps the name (gitignored, never committed, never in the chain).
- **Renderer:** `imported` reads no `name` from any payload, old or new, and prints `importedRef` only for a PROPERTY — so neither a legacy name nor a crafted `reference` on a contact reaches a line. No current-name join: the event's entity IS the contact, whose page header names it; the evidence header names it from the row; the admin feed names no contact for any contact event. (T-merged-event-ids-only joined only because its event names a DIFFERENT contact; joins were declined wherever the text shows elsewhere.)
- **No runtime allowlist in `logImported`.** The critic showed why: it runs AFTER its row is committed, and a guard that throws there lands in the per-row catch — rows with no `imported` event (a public property among them) and a report that says "error". `scripts/**` is outside tsc and eslint, so a type narrowing would enforce nothing. The proof is behavioural.

**Tests.** Every new test was watched RED first.
- `scripts/import/entry-points.test.ts` (the REAL scripts, run as the operator runs them, against a request-recording PostgREST stand-in): a person row, a company-only row, and a property row with a named owner. Positive controls: the name and the E.164 number reach the `contacts` INSERT. The `imported` bodies are pinned exactly — contact `{ source, batch }`, owner `{ source, as: "owner", batch }`, mandate `{ source, property, batch }`, property keys `{ batch, reference, score, source, visibility }` — and no event body carries the name, the number (spaced or not), the e-mail or the company. Case-SENSITIVE distinctive words: the kept `as: "owner"`, the `zz-entry-…` batch and the ZZ references would trip a case-folded check. RED at the old code: 3 of 3.
- `lib/services/events.test.ts`: legacy contact / company / owner / owner-with-phone payloads read "Imported from CSV"; new shapes; a property prints its reference (even beside a legacy name); a property without one, a mandate, and a crafted `reference` on a contact read bare; no line carries the name or number; the translator routes. RED: 8 of 13.
- `lib/services/evidence.test.ts`: an admin's un-narrowed report over three imported events (legacy name, legacy owner phone, new) prints three bare lines. RED at the old code.

**Review** (an adversarial workflow over `07e7a8c`: writers-completeness, renderer-consumers and tests lenses, three skeptics per finding, majority survives; mutation proofs in a detached copy). No defect in the change. Two confirmed findings, both records, fixed here: this entry and the BACKLOG strike did not exist yet, and the `events.ts` header index did not name the rule or `imported`'s entity gate. Rejected 0/3 as pre-existing and already recorded: the default `batch` label is the CSV's file name and goes into every `imported` event — kept as a BACKLOG NOTE for the operator's call. **Mutation proofs: 8 of 8 killed** — the name back (contact, owner), a company key, a phone key, an extra key added inside `logImported` (killed by the exact-shape pins), the old `reference ?? name` line, the entity gate dropped, and `importedRef` dropped.

**Measured** (the branch, 2026-09-25): tsc 0 (`--incremental false`); eslint 0 on the whole tree; unit 2727/2727 across 207 files (the importer harness included: vitest runs `scripts/**`). No browser flow imports a CSV (the importers are CLI scripts), and no page's behaviour changed except the `imported` line, pinned by the renderer tests.

**Compatibility and deploy order.** No migration, nothing on hosted, not deploy-coupled. The scripts run from a checkout, so the operator's next import after merge writes the new shapes. An old app renders a new payload as "Imported from CSV" for a contact (as it would any payload without a name); a new app renders an old one the same. An evidence report regenerated over a legacy `imported` line with a name recomputes to a different `reportContentHash` (verification is by `pdf_sha256`); hosted has 0 such events.

**Not changed here** (each on BACKLOG): `record_key_movement` (0013) writes a key's typed HOLDER — an owner's name on a transfer — into key events (hosted: 2 events carry one); `archive-records.mts` writes the operator's typed `--reason` into `archived` (hosted: 7); a phone-only owner row's dry run promises an owner the live run refuses, after creating a missing area; the default `batch` label is the CSV's file name (a NOTE, the operator's call).

**Landing (2026-09-25, evening).** On the operator's word ("merge #66 and verify the deploy"). Main had not moved (`a4a1f43`, the PR's base). ## T-key-holder-shape — a key's movement event names the movement, never the holder (2026-09-25; migration 0116)

**The leak** (operator: "fix the key holder leak next"; BACKLOG, found by T-imported-identity-shape's scouting critic). Inspected at `0510047`, with a read-only mapping workflow (the SQL writer, consumers, callers and policy, precedent; a completeness critic re-read the migrations and the UI itself).
- `record_key_movement` (0013, never re-created; SECURITY DEFINER, `returns void`, authenticated-callable) logged every movement as `{ key_code, holder }`. `holder` was the TYPED name of an external holder on a checkout (a lawyer, a cleaner — nothing limits it to non-clients), the property OWNER's typed name on a transfer ("Owner name (optional)"), the same cached name copied again on a return or a loss, or a staff member's `full_name` by value. The pre-0013 app-side writer (T4.6, `78fd4c9`) wrote the same shape.
- The key lines printed it — "Key K12 checked out to …", "handed to owner (…)", "last with …" — on the property Activity tab (read as the system) and the admin feed.
- **Hosted, read-only, counts only:** 1 `key_checkout` and 1 `key_return` carry a holder; neither equals any staff member's name (typed); both written by 0013's RPC. The hosted function body is 0013's text exactly, with CRLF line endings (md5 `bf29a5e9…` = 0013's body with \r\n; LF md5 `15a8c83e…`).

**Verified, not assumed — why no new table.** The critic answered the one question that could have made this more than a removal: is the event the only custody record? No. `key_movements` gets one row per movement, written in the same transaction with the same name (0013's movement insert), and EVERY custody surface reads rows: the per-key History dialog (every role, on the register and the property page) and the /keys "Recent movements" list read `key_movements`; the register, the CSV export and the property page read `property_keys.current_holder_name`. The chain copy fed only a suffix on two event lines. Phase-1 spec (doc 02 §T4.6: every movement an event; holder and time recorded; the property page shows the holder) is still met: every movement still writes an event, the holder and time stay on the movement row, and the property page's holder comes from the cache.

**The fix.**
- **Migration 0116** re-creates the function from 0013's text with three changes and nothing else (a `diff` of the two bodies shows exactly them): a `v_movement_id` variable, `returning id into v_movement_id` on the movement insert, and the event payload `{ key_code, movement_id }` — the id is the fact, the row carries the name (the T-merged-event-ids-only idiom). Signature, defaults, `returns void`, SECURITY DEFINER, `search_path` and grants unchanged; re-stated. Apply-time assertions: one function by name; the signature, the void return, definer and search_path; no `'holder'` in the body, and the movement id both captured and logged; the ACLs; the first refusal without a session. Its header does not quote the removed line, so the BACKLOG VERIFY cannot hit a comment (the trap 0115's header set for its own VERIFY — fixed here by excluding SQL comment lines).
- **Renderer:** the four key lines read the code only — no `holder` from any payload, old, new or inserted by hand (`events_insert`, 0071, lets a member write any payload, which no body change can close). The six `*Holder` messages are gone in EN/EL/RU; `holder` left the parity test's sample values.
- **Kept byte-for-byte, recorded on BACKLOG:** no second-factor check in the function; a staff id matching no active profile NULLs the typed name (non-STRICT SELECT INTO); direct INSERT into `key_movements` and UPDATE of the holder cache bypass the RPC.

**Tests.** Watched RED first.
- `supabase/tests/key-movement-event-shape.test.ts` (new; the real RPC on real sessions): a checkout to an external holder, a return, a transfer to the owner then a loss, and a staff checkout. Positive controls: the typed name reaches the movement row and the holder cache (and survives a return onto the row, and a loss "for accountability"). Each event's payload is exactly `{ key_code, movement_id }` with `movement_id` = its row; a refused movement writes no row and no event; none of the typed names is in any of the run's key events. RED at 0115: 5 of 6 (the refusal control held).
- `lib/services/events.test.ts`: legacy payloads with a typed holder, the owner, a cached holder, a staff name, and a holder without a code read without a name; new payloads read the code. RED: 6 of 14.

**Review** (an adversarial workflow over `2a441c1`: SQL, consumers-and-UI and tests lenses, three skeptics per finding; no database touched). The SQL and tests lenses found no defect; one finding, confirmed 3/3 and fixed here: the `events.ts` header index of fields never printed did not name the key holder. **Mutation proofs** (the function re-created in a broken form on the LOCAL stack, the DB test run, 0116's exact text restored — prosrc digest `8d9dc7ba…` before and after): 4 of 4 killed — the holder back in the event (5 red), a `movement_id` naming another row (4), the row losing the holder's name (4), no movement id (4); the renderer's holder branch is pinned by the 6 RED renderer cases.

**Measured** (the branch, local stack at 0116, 2026-09-25): tsc 0 (`--incremental false`); eslint 0 on the whole tree; unit 2737/2737 across 207 files; the database suite 378/381 — the 3 reds are the known feed residue (rls 41/42/57), identical on `main`; `key-movement-event-shape.test.ts` 6/6 and RLS tests 13 and 18 (key history append-only; key events) green; e2e `keys-export` + `event-typed-text` 20/20 on desktop and mobile (no spec moves a key: the renderer tests carry the lines).

**Compatibility and deploy order.** Not deploy-coupled: same arity, `returns void`. An old app renders a new payload as "Key K12 checked out" (its holder branch finds nothing); a new app renders an old one the same. Hosted 0116 FIRST all the same — it stops new names reaching the chain soonest — then merge, deploy READY, probes. The evidence report has no key family, so no report hash moves.

**Not changed here** (BACKLOG): the three kept-as-is SQL behaviours above; the erasure decision now also covers `key_movements.holder_name` and `property_keys.current_holder_name` — a key's typed holder's only home, unlinked to any contact — and records backups as the real horizon; found on the way: four list exports write the raw URL query string into `exported` events, and a signed viewing slip's `signer_name` is in its event (hosted: 1, while its slip row is gone).

## T-rescheduled-line-crash — no crafted event can take a timeline page down (2026-09-25; no migration)

**The defect** (BACKLOG "A crafted `rescheduled` event crashes three pages", found by T-viewing-feedback-shape's review). Inspected at `a4a1f43`. Any active org member may insert any event — any type, any payload, any `occurred_at` (`events_insert`, 0071, checks only org and actor) — and the hash chain can never drop the row. `describeEvent` renders the property Activity tab, the admin dashboard feed and the commission evidence report, and it was unguarded. One event that breaks its line breaks those pages for everyone, for good. **Hosted, read-only, counts only:** 0 `rescheduled` events — nothing in production is broken today.

**What the sweep and the review found** (the first sweep, then an adversarial review — three lenses, three skeptics each, all nine findings confirmed):
- `rescheduled` (WF-1, `ebcfec5`) passed any non-blank `from` / `to` to `formatDateTime`: `Intl.DateTimeFormat#format(new Date("x"))` throws `RangeError`.
- **Not one line — a class.** The first sweep's battery held only primitives and plain objects, and on it `rescheduled` was the only offender. The review added what jsonb can also carry: an object with its OWN `toString` / `valueOf` (`{"toString":0}` — JSON.parse makes it an own data property, and `Number()` / `String()` then throw `TypeError`) and a deeply nested array (`String` recursion overflows the stack). Those broke **26 more lines** — every `Number(p.x)` count line, `asMoney`, `portalName`'s `String(p.portal)`, and `viewing_feedback`'s `Number(p.rating)` (so T-viewing-feedback-shape's "never throws" held only for its own battery). My first claim, "rescheduled was the only offender", was true only of the values I had chosen.
- **A prototype-named type** (`event_type: "constructor"`) resolved `EVENT_LINES["constructor"]` to `Object`, whose "line" is an OBJECT — no throw, so the new guard never saw it, and React failed rendering it. `__proto__`, `hasOwnProperty` and `valueOf` too; an `entity_type` of that name leaked a function's source into the prefix.
- **A crafted far-future `occurred_at`** (year 200000; Postgres allows it, and PostgREST returns text JavaScript cannot parse) threw in `formatDateTime` OUTSIDE `describeEvent` — the timeline, the key-movement list, the evidence preview and PDF.

**The fix.**
- `rescheduled` formats only a value that parses (`asDateText`), else "Viewing rescheduled".
- `asNumber` coerces only a number or a string; every `Number(p.x)` in `EVENT_LINES` (20 sites) and `asMoney` go through it; `portalName` takes a string or nothing. A crafted value reads as missing, which every line already handled.
- `describeEvent` renders only a type the registry OWNS (`Object.hasOwn`, the same for the entity-prefix map), requires the line to be a string, and a line that throws or returns anything else reads as the bare event type. The console line and a Sentry `captureMessage` carry tags only — the type if registered, else `"unregistered"` (an unregistered type is text anyone typed), and the error's NAME (a message can quote the payload). The guard is a last resort: the sweep fails for any registered line that reaches it.
- `formatDateTime` / `formatDate` read an unbuildable date as "—", as `formatNumber` / `formatArea` already read a non-finite number. Every place an event's time is shown goes through them.

**Tests.**
- `lib/services/event-lines-crafted-payload.test.ts` (new): every registered type (read from the source; a broken reader fails loudly) × every entity type × EN/EL/RU through the real translators, fed a Proxy payload whose every key reads one crafted jsonb value — 30 of them: words, an impossible date, "NaN"/"Infinity", a 100k string, extreme doubles, fractions, booleans, null, objects, arrays, the own-`toString` objects, a 5000-deep array, an absent value, and the strings "constructor" / "__proto__" / "toString" / "hasOwnProperty" — then 30 mixed rotations across keys, the discriminators (`kind` / `reason` / `action` … answer every literal the source compares them with, every other key a crafted value — the branches a uniform value never reaches), and an empty, null, array and string payload. It fails on a throw, a non-string, or a guard hit. Prototype-named event and entity types must read as a string with nothing of `Object.prototype` in it.
- `lib/services/events.test.ts`: `rescheduled` with words, a date beside a word, an impossible date, "NaN"/"Infinity", numbers and objects reads bare; two real dates still format; a translator that throws on one key makes that line read bare, leaves the next alone, and logs and reports `{ event_type, error }` with none of the payload; an unregistered type is reported as `"unregistered"`. The old `not.toThrow` tolerance test now also fails on a guard hit (the guard had made it unfalsifiable).
- `lib/utils/format.test.ts`: a word, an impossible date, "200000-01-01T00:00:00+00:00" (as PostgREST returns it) and an invalid Date read "—" in both formatters; a real timestamp still formats.
- RED at the old code throughout (14 at the first sweep; then 61 cases and 27 offending types on the extended sweep, and the formatter cases). **Mutation proofs: 8 of 8 killed** — the own-key lookup (4 red), the prefix own-key lookup (survived at first: the translator does not throw on `Object`, it prints "events.function Object() { [native code] }" — the prototype test now forbids that text, then 5 red), `asNumber` back to `Number` (57), `portalName` back to `String()` (34), the date check (6), the formatter check (4), the Sentry report (2), the raw type in the report (1).

**Measured** (the branch, 2026-09-25): tsc 0 (`--incremental false`); eslint 0 on the whole tree; unit 2855/2855 across 208 files (after rebasing onto `5cebdfc` — T-imported-identity-shape's and T-key-holder-shape's tests included, and the sweep over the new key lines); e2e 18/18 for `viewing-reschedule` + `event-typed-text` on desktop and mobile; a wider set of nine specs (those two, `keys-export`, `modules`, `csp`, `enquiry-contact-suggestions`, `mandate-lifecycle`, `performance`, `security`) 192/194 on desktop and mobile — the 2 reds are `modules` "Leads / Properties — loads clean" on MOBILE, a horizontal overflow (469 and 607 px in a 390 px viewport) that fails identically on untouched main `22287d9` (the known local-residue header overflow); `npm run build` exit 0 and `check:static-routes` ok.

**Compatibility and deploy order.** No migration, nothing on hosted, not deploy-coupled. Real payloads render exactly as before (a number or a numeric string is coerced as `Number` did; a boolean count, which no writer produces, now reads as missing rather than 1). A line that could not render now reads bare instead of failing the page; a date that could not be built reads "—". An evidence report could not be generated at all over such an event, so no stored report hash moves. Order: branch CI green → merge → deploy READY → probes.

**Not changed here** (on BACKLOG): the database still accepts a crafted `occurred_at` (the row now renders "—" but sorts first in "latest" lists — a CHECK or a stamping trigger needs a migration); `attachNotes` sends payload `note_id`s unchecked, so one malformed id blanks every note on a timeline (a degradation, not a crash).

**Landing (2026-09-25, night).** On the operator's word ("merge #67 and verify the deploy"). Main had moved twice since the branch was cut (the #66 landing docs, then #68 — which changed `events.ts`, its tests, the locales, BACKLOG and DECISIONS): rebased onto `5cebdfc`; the code applied cleanly, the two docs conflicts were both-sides appends and were kept in order; re-verified on the rebased tree (tsc 0, eslint 0, unit 2855/2855 — the sweep now covering #68's key lines); branch CI green on `a4241c6`. PR #67 → main `48a31cd`, pinned to `a4241c6`. Vercel production `dpl_Apxi5hkh3ueQDZLEMT4wkCsaoNRY` READY; CI on the merge commit green (run 36149107129: checks, rls, e2e). Verified in the operator's Chrome (counts only, no text read): the admin dashboard, the busiest property's Activity tab (50 lines: 36 photo, 2 key — as before), the busiest contact's Activity tab (13) and /keys render with no error boundary; every event time formats (the dashboard 10, the property 50, the contact 13; 0 read "—"); 0 lines fell into the guard (none reads as a bare lowercase type); the /keys em dashes are empty Holder cells of keys in the office. No runtime errors; no new Sentry issue in the two hours after the deploy (so no "[timeline] line failed" report). Hosted holds 0 rescheduled events — nothing crafted was created to exercise the guard.

## T-atomic-deal-close — closing a deal is one transaction; a competing or repeated close changes nothing (2026-09-25; migration 0117)

**The defect** (BACKLOG "`markDealLost` and `markDealWon` do not fold the open-status check into their UPDATE"; the brief asked for independent verification before any build). Inspected at `6366ef8` — the commit the previous audit examined; `main` had not moved. Mapped read-only first (six readers: the deals model and its policies, the events chain, every writer of closing state and any reopen path, the follow-ups and the UI, the test harnesses, the written rules). Both actions read `status = 'open'` on the caller's client, UPDATEd the row `.eq("id")` only, then wrote their events as separate requests through `logEvent`, which THROWS — after the update had committed. Nothing in the database stopped any of it: no CHECK ties status to its timestamps, `deals_update` (0100) restricts rows not columns, and no trigger guards a transition. No reopen or correction workflow for deals exists anywhere.

**Reproduced before anything changed — the real actions against the real stack.** `supabase/tests/deal-close-actions.test.ts` (new) runs the REAL `markDealWon` / `markDealLost` with supabase-js clients signed in at aal2, so every read and write goes through PostgREST, RLS, the triggers and the hash chain; only `revalidatePath` is stubbed. Interleaving is held by a gate on each client's fetch that HOLDS the action's first write until the test releases it — against `6366ef8` that write came after the status read, so "overlapping" meant exactly "both read the deal as open first". Never a sleep. Failure injection is real: a BEFORE INSERT trigger on `events` refusing one event type for one entity of the throwaway organisation, removed in `finally` (`trg_events_hash` untouched). At `6366ef8`, 10 of 11 red, each with the database's own evidence:
- two overlapping Lost requests: both "saved", **two `lost` events**;
- overlapping Won then Lost: the deal ended **lost, still carrying `won_at` and `final_value`**, one event of each kind; Lost then Won: **won, carrying `lost_at` and the Lost reason**;
- two overlapping override Wins: **two `won_override` and two `won`**, the later price standing;
- the `lost` event refused: the deal **stayed lost with no event** and the action threw; `won_override` or `won` refused: **won with no event**, or with `won_override` alone;
- two overlapping Wins on a listing with a live hold: **two `listing_status_check` prompts**;
- a follow-up event refused after the close: the action threw — an error page for a deal that WAS won;
- a sequential Won then Lost WAS refused ("Deal is already won") — the gap was the read-then-write, as BACKLOG said.
And the UI: the same outcome spec run against `6366ef8`'s app (the new spec copied into the main checkout for the run, then removed) was 4 of 4 red — among them, **the success toast never showed**: the page renders the Won/Lost dialogs only while the deal is open, the close revalidates it, and the effect that toasted ran in a component the refresh had already unmounted.
Classification: the action behaviour is confirmed with the real code on the real database; the database behaviour — no safeguard — against the actual schema; production occurrence is unknown (hosted holds test data only, and no production count was taken for this).

**The design was critiqued before it was built** (three adversarial lenses — PostgreSQL/RLS semantics, security and privacy, compatibility/UX/follow-ups — with rolled-back SQL experiments). What it changed: `FOR UPDATE` conflicts with the `FOR KEY SHARE` of every foreign-key check, so a close would block task and offer inserts on its deal and could deadlock the nightly nudge sweep through one — **`FOR NO KEY UPDATE`**; a guard freezing the reason for every role would pre-empt the open erasure decision — **it binds user sessions only**; letting a user session reopen let two PATCHes flip a closed deal with no event — **refused**; `numeric` admits NaN and it passes `>= 0` — **refused, typed or from the offer**; PostgreSQL's `\s` strips NEL and keeps the BOM, the opposite of JavaScript — **an explicit class, compared with `trim()` on every BMP code point: 0 mismatches**; an answer with no error code may have committed — **reported as unknown, never "nothing changed"**; `raiseLiveHoldCheck` swallowed its failures into a `0` that read as "no hold" — **a discriminated outcome**.

**The fix.**
- **Migration 0117 — `close_deal(p_deal_id, p_outcome, p_final_value, p_lost_reason, p_override) returns jsonb`**, SECURITY INVOKER, modelled on `move_deal_to_stage` (0067): `deals_update` / `deals_select` / `offers_select` / `events_insert` and `require_aal2` apply unchanged to a DIRECT call. Identity from the session only (`auth.uid()`, `mfa_satisfied()`, `current_org_id()`, `current_role_gnk()`); inputs validated as the form validates them, NULLs refusing; the role checked before any deal is read (no existence oracle: another agent's deal, another organisation's and a missing one all read "Deal not found"); the row locked `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` and its status checked UNDER the lock; both UPDATEs also conditional on `status = 'open'`; every event of the close in the same transaction, so a refused event rolls back the status, stage, timestamps, price, reason and the nudge supersession the status change fires. A deal already closed is untouched and answered `already_closed` (same outcome) or `conflict` (the other) — keyed on the row's status, never on "a terminal event exists": idempotency per open lifecycle. Rules kept: an accepted offer, or an admin's explicit override (`won_override` before `won`); `final_value` typed, else the offer's amount, else null; the type's is_won / is_lost stage (lowest `sort_order` — the schema allows several), else the stage kept; the reason on the row, never in an event. Additions: `won` names the justifying `offer_id` (an id — SEC-03 allows it); the offer is read in the deal's own organisation, newest first as the dialog prefills, `FOR SHARE`; a close clears the other outcome's columns. EXECUTE: authenticated only.
- **`deals_closed_guard`** (BEFORE UPDATE on `deals`): for a USER SESSION on a row ALREADY won or lost, refuses the other outcome, reopening, and any change to `won_at`, `lost_at`, `lost_reason`, `final_value`, `stage_id`, `stage_entered_at`. That covers the hosted-first window: the deployed actions' competing second UPDATE now fails before their `logEvent`. It does not bind service_role, postgres or definer bodies — the operator's correction path and a future reopen RPC's. Contact erasure writes on the admin's USER session (only notes and storage use the service role), so the pending decision on blanking `lost_reason` must put that step on the admin client or a definer function — pinned by a test, recorded on the erasure entry.
- **The actions** validate the form and call `close_deal`; they never throw. `closed` runs the Won follow-ups (the listing-status prompt, the live-hold ask, the health recompute) — only there, so a double submit, a retry or a competing close cannot raise them twice; each follow-up that fails AFTER the commit becomes a caveat on a success that says what is known (the reminder may not have been created — check by hand; or it was, and only its timeline line failed — tell an admin, the NOT_RECORDED_NOTICE convention), paged to Sentry by shape. `already_closed` is a saved state flagged `alreadyClosed`; `conflict` is an error naming the outcome that committed; a P0001 shows its own sentence; an error that proves a rollback (a SQLSTATE outside class 08, PGRST1xx–3xx, PGRST002/003) says nothing changed; anything else — no code, a gateway body, class 08, an unreadable answer — is UNKNOWN: the page is refreshed and the user is told, in the one text `unconfirmedCloseText` (`lib/validators/deals.ts`) shared with the dialog, to check the listing and any live hold if the deal now reads Won.
- **The dialogs** submit through a transition and toast from it (the review-and-link pattern), so a message outlives the refresh that unmounts them; everything that arrives with a refresh (`pageRefreshed`: a conflict, a repeat, an unknown answer) or with no answer at all stays until dismissed; `onSubmit`, not a form action, so a refusal does not wipe a typed reason; a refusal is cleared when the dialog closes.
- **Readers:** the deal page, the entity timeline and the admin feed break `occurred_at` ties by id — `won_override` and `won` now share one transaction time.

**Tests.** Watched RED first where a test could exist before the code.
- `supabase/tests/deal-close-actions.test.ts` (11) — the real actions on the real stack: the reproduction above, now green (the before/after evidence lines are in the PR). Its header says what the gate does and does not control against the RPC actions.
- `supabase/tests/deal-close.test.ts` (51) — the database: ordered races on two impersonated `pg` sessions (A closes and holds; B OBSERVED blocked on the row lock through `pg_stat_activity`; A commits or rolls back; B returns) for Lost/Lost, Won/Won with and without an offer, Won-then-Lost, Lost-then-Won and a rolled-back first close; a PostgREST race; repeats; the refused-event rollback for `lost`, `won_override` and `won`, nudge included; the rules by direct call (another deal's offer, another organisation's planted offer, a NaN amount, a typed price, zero); the reason trimmed as JavaScript trims and measured in UTF-16 units; the exact payloads, and not one word of the reason in ANY event the close wrote in ANY organisation, on the Lost path and on a Won after a maintenance reopen; the roles (listing manager, another agent, another organisation, aal1, deactivated, anon, service_role); the guard against the deployed `6366ef8` actions' exact requests, the user session refused (blanking the reason included), the maintenance path, a reopened deal's second lifecycle; the chain verifying.
- Unit: `deal-won-close.test.ts` (18, new), `deal-lost-event-payload.test.ts` (7, rewritten to the rpc-mock pattern — the reason leaves the action once, as `p_lost_reason`, and the action writes nothing itself), `followup-tasks.test.ts` (the discriminated outcomes), `entity-timeline.test.ts` (the tie-break).
- `tests/e2e/deal-close-outcomes.spec.ts` (5, new): the success toast, a colleague's close that committed first, a repeat, a follow-up failure after the commit (the caveat outlives sonner's 4 s and is dismissed by its button), and a Won whose request never comes back.
- **Mutation proofs:** SQL 11 of 12 killed — no status check or fold (13 red), no row lock (6), an event failure swallowed (2), the reason in the `lost` event (2), NaN from the offer (1), the other outcome's columns kept (1), locale trimming (1), the role check skipped (1), the guard allowing reopen (1), binding the maintenance roles (2), swapping outcomes (2); the one survivor — the offer read without its organisation predicate — is equivalent under RLS (`offers_select` already hides a foreign offer from an invoker call; the predicate is belt and braces). App 10 of 10 killed. Every mutant confirmed installed, every function restored to its digest.
- The apply-time SEC-03 tripwire read two of the three event inserts (a semicolon in a comment ended its match); it now strips comments and must read all three — fed the reviewers' leak (the row's earlier reason in the `won` payload) it refuses the migration, where the old regex stayed silent.

**Review** (an adversarial workflow over the full diff: SQL, actions, UI, tests, docs/compatibility lenses, two independent refuters per finding). 18 findings: 15 confirmed by both, 2 split, 1 refuted. All acted on: the dialog's own "could not confirm" text lacked the Won caveat in the one case the docs said it covered (a function killed after the commit), and the must-act toasts faded after 4 s — one shared text, persistent toasts, an e2e case; a refusal survived reopening the dialog (its clear-on-open branch could never run); the persistence assertion could not fail; the SEC-03 tripwire above; three written claims were false ("cannot deadlock" — a rarer task/chain-lock cycle predates 0117 and remains, now recorded; "erasure runs on the admin client" — it runs on the user session; the offers entry's mechanism); two VERIFY greps could never report fixed; the action-test header overclaimed what its gate controls. The refuted one (database text in console breadcrumbs) was applied as hardening to the new line only.

**Measured** (the branch, local stack at 0117, 2026-09-25): tsc 0 (`--incremental false`); eslint 0 on the whole tree; unit 2876/2876 across 209 files; the database suite 440/443 — the 3 reds are rls 41/42/57, identical on untouched `6366ef8` against the same database (the known local feed residue); `deal-close.test.ts` + `deal-close-actions.test.ts` 62/62; e2e desktop 15/15 (`deal-close`, `deal-close-outcomes`, `event-typed-text`, setup); `npm run build` exit 0 and `check:static-routes` ok. On MOBILE the specs whose deal has an offer fail at the dialog's button — exactly as `deal-close.spec` fails on untouched `6366ef8`: the deal page overflows a phone once it lists an offer (BACKLOG, new; CI runs desktop only).

**Compatibility and deploy order.** Additive: a function and a trigger; no enum, no column, no changed signature. **Hosted 0117 FIRST, then merge** (the working agreement). In the window the DEPLOYED app still closes an open deal exactly as before (its PATCH is legal — pinned with its exact requests), while its race cases are refused by the guard (the loser's dialog shows "Deal is already won — it cannot be marked lost"; nothing overwritten, no second terminal event); what it keeps until the deploy is the non-atomic event write. The NEW app against a database WITHOUT 0117 fails closed: PGRST202 → "Could not close the deal — nothing was changed", paged. No `release-compat-contracts` entry: that harness is the enquiry door's, and 0117 changes no function the deployed app calls.
**Rollback.** Revert the app first (merge a revert, confirm the deploy) — safe on its own: the old actions work against 0117 and the guard keeps their races refused; only atomicity returns to the old shape. Only then, if ever, drop the objects — through a FORWARD migration that also removes the two `verify-restore.sql` grants rows and moves the migrations pin, never by hand. Dropping them while the new app is deployed makes every close answer PGRST202 (fails closed: no deal can be closed). Dropping them reopens the original race for the old actions. No data migration either way: rows and payloads written by `close_deal` have the old shapes (plus `offer_id`).

**Not changed here** (BACKLOG): a direct write can still close an OPEN deal without `close_deal` (deploy-coupled, code first); the Won reminders are at-most-once; NaN is a legal price in three columns; `move_deal_to_stage` still takes FOR UPDATE; the rare task/chain-lock cycle between a close and the nudge sweep; the deal-nudge supersession writes across organisations; offers stay editable on a closed deal; the dashboard's "won this month" lost `final_value` in 0093; on a phone a deal with an offer cannot be closed from its page; a superseded deal nudge renders the generic line.
