## T-deal-close-db-boundary — a deal reaches won or lost only through `close_deal` (2026-09-26; migration 0118)

**The gap** (BACKLOG "A direct write can still close an OPEN deal without `close_deal`", left open by 0117 on purpose because refusing it was deploy-coupled; the brief asked for independent verification first). Inspected: gnk-crm `main` = `3a72498` (= the deployed `aa01ef8` plus docs), gnk-web `main` = `b158f37` (it has no writer of deals; its only hit is a test asserting it holds no service key). No open pull request on either repository; the three stale remote branches on gnk-crm do not touch deals. Mapped read-only first (five readers: every app and script writer of `deals`, the database layer — policies, grants, triggers, every SQL writer —, the test harness, the written rules and pins; then a completeness critic).

**Reproduced before anything changed** — the local stack at 0117, real PostgREST, an aal2 agent and an aal2 admin on a throwaway organisation (script outside the repository, cleaned up):
| attempt | result at 0117 |
|---|---|
| PATCH an open deal with no accepted offer to `{status: won, won_at}` | 200 — won, no event; `close_deal` then answers `already_closed` and the 0117 guard refuses any user-session correction |
| PATCH to `{status: lost}` with no reason / with `lost_reason: 'x'` | 200 — lost, no reason (or one letter), no event |
| PATCH closing details onto a deal that stays open (`won_at`, `lost_reason`, `final_value`) or into its Won / Lost stage | 200 each (the kanban's RPC refuses the stage move; a PATCH did not) |
| POST a deal born won or lost, or open with closing details, or open in the Won stage | 201 each |
| UPSERT (`on_conflict=id`, merge) an existing open deal to won; a new id born won | 200 / 201 |
| controls: `close_deal` Won with an accepted offer, Lost with a reason; an agent's Won without an offer | closed / closed / refused |
| a deal already won: PATCH to lost or open, upsert to open or lost | refused (0117's guard) |
Two adjacent facts from the same run, recorded rather than fixed here: the same session can POST hand-written `won` / `lost` events (`events_insert` checks only organisation and actor), and `deals_insert` does not bind `agent_id` / `created_by` to the caller.

**The dependency, confirmed and not assumed.** Production `gnk-crm.vercel.app` is `dpl_7BFFpRnoN9cDzuk2XquP7A9Yn7FL` at `aa01ef8` (Vercel API, alias read 2026-09-25); `aa01ef8:lib/actions/deals.ts` closes only through `rpc("close_deal")` (its only other deal write after a Won is the health recompute); the merge commit's CI was fully green (run 36176646388: checks, rls, e2e). Hosted (read-only `execute_sql`): ledger at 0117 (117 rows, non-filename versions 0), `close_deal` md5 `cb70a918…` and the guard `7ee172ae…` as recorded, owner `postgres` (BYPASSRLS, not superuser), pg_graphql not installed, `authenticated` cannot create in `public`; ONE deal, lost, with `lost_at`, a reason, its Lost stage and its `lost` event; no open deal with a closing detail or a terminal stage, no closed deal without its event, no Won without an offer or an override. Nothing needs repair and nothing was repaired.

**Options compared.**
| option | benefit | effort | permission-regression risk | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| a transaction-local flag `close_deal` sets and the guard reads (BACKLOG's first suggestion) | keeps the invoker body | small | `set_config` is executable by PUBLIC; a custom setting outlives the statement (and reads `''`, not NULL, on a pooled connection afterwards — measured) — a freely settable flag is not authorisation | rejected |
| column privileges (revoke UPDATE / INSERT on status and the closing columns) + a definer `close_deal` | engine-enforced | medium: the TABLE grant must go first, every later column needs a grant, hosted's default grants differ from local (HANDOFF §4.2) | high; and a privilege cannot say "a non-terminal stage of your own organisation", so a trigger is needed anyway | rejected |
| a deferred constraint trigger checking at commit that a terminal event exists in the transaction | keeps the invoker body | medium | low, but the rules live in two places and "close_deal ran" becomes an inference from side effects (and events are user-insertable) | rejected |
| **`close_deal` SECURITY DEFINER + the guard keyed on the ROLE the statement runs as** | the role comes from the signed JWT; the maintenance path and definer bodies stay unbound, as 0117 and the erasure decision require | small: one function re-created, one trigger function widened | the definer loses RLS — mitigated by restating `deals_update` explicitly, re-reading the caller under the lock, a differential test and apply-time assertions | **chosen** |

**The fix — migration 0118.**
- **`close_deal` becomes SECURITY DEFINER** (owner postgres, `search_path = public, pg_temp`, every relation schema-qualified; EXECUTE authenticated only, as before). Its body is 0117's with what RLS used to supply restated: the lock query carries `deals_update`'s USING clause (an admin of the organisation, or an agent who is the deal's `agent_id` or `created_by`; its WITH CHECK holds whenever USING does — a close changes neither organisation nor owner); **step 4b re-reads the caller under the lock** — aal2, organisation, role, ownership — because 0117's RLS re-read the profile at every statement after the lock, so an admin demoted (or an agent deactivated) while the close waited must still be refused (measured: without 4b the demoted admin's override Won committed); 0117's "defensive" `exists (...)` probe is removed, because as postgres it would have told another agent's deal apart from a missing id — every deal the caller may not close reads "Deal not found", and the two unreachable "You do not have permission to close this deal" sentences read the same. Rules, payloads, answers, grants and the signature are unchanged, so no `release-compat-contracts` entry and no type regeneration.
- **`deals_closed_guard`** fires BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE (`search_path = public, pg_temp`, `public.deal_stages` qualified) and, for a user session (`current_user` authenticated / anon), refuses on an OPEN row any change of `status`, any change to `won_at` / `lost_at` / `lost_reason` / `final_value` (a CHANGE, compared with OLD — a maintenance reopen leaves the previous lifecycle's values on the row, and an ordinary edit carries them), and a move to a stage that is not a non-terminal stage of the deal's own organisation; on INSERT a deal that is not open, carries a closing detail, or starts in such a stage. The closed-row rules are 0117's text. service_role, postgres and definer bodies are not bound — the correction path, a maintenance reopen, and now `close_deal`.
- **Apply-time assertions:** definer + owner + search_path; the restated predicate in the lock query; the re-read under the lock; no existence oracle; both UPDATEs folded on `status = 'open'`; the SEC-03 tripwire (no event insert names the reason); grants; the guard an invoker with `pg_temp` last; the trigger bound BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE FOR EACH ROW; **no SECURITY DEFINER function other than `close_deal` writes `deals`** (the guard exempts definer bodies, so any other would be a second door); a no-session probe. Measured by the mutation runs: they refuse every `close_deal` mutant tried (M7–M11, M16–M19b, M22).

**Tests.** Watched RED first: with the final files, 54 of the 123 tests in the two database files fail against 0117's exact bodies (installed from 0117's own text, md5 = hosted) — every one a 0118 test or the definer flag; the differential persona test PASSES there, which is itself the evidence that the restatement matches 0117's RLS. (A first draft's "cannot switch to a maintenance role" test was a harness mistake and was removed: `SET ROLE` checks the login role, and the harness logs in as postgres.) `supabase/tests/deal-close.test.ts`:
- the KNOWN GAP test flipped into a regression (refused; row and chain byte-identical); the pre-`aa01ef8` app's exact PATCHes (Won and Lost) refused with nothing written;
- a PATCH matrix, agent and admin (to won with a full payload, to lost with no / a one-letter reason, each closing detail alone, into the Won / Lost stage, into another organisation's Won and open stages), a bulk PATCH refused as a whole;
- an INSERT matrix, agent and admin (born won / lost, open with each closing detail, open in a terminal or foreign stage) and the ordinary insert (convertLead's shape);
- UPSERT: onto an open deal (the INSERT arm refuses before the conflict is resolved), onto a closed deal (stage move refused; an explicit reopen refused), a new id born won, an ordinary merge;
- forged context: `request.jwt.claims` claiming service_role, three made-up session flags, `set_config` over REST (PGRST202), and — labelled as the assumption the guard stands on — a token the project did not sign (401 before any SQL);
- a direct PATCH queued behind a held close (commit: meets the closed row; rollback: the open-row rule);
- a DIFFERENTIAL persona test: `close_deal` succeeds exactly where a PostgREST PATCH of an ordinary column succeeds, each refusal pinned to its rule — the deal's agent created by an admin (the `agent_id` arm alone), the creator who is not the agent (the `created_by` arm alone), an admin; not another agent ("Deal not found"), a listing manager ("You do not have permission to close deals."), another organisation's admin, another organisation's user named as the deal's agent, an aal1 session ("Second factor required."), anon (42501), a deactivated account ("Account deactivated.");
- the caller re-read under the lock: an admin demoted, and an agent deactivated, while their close waits — refused, nothing written, then the control succeeds;
- the definer's owner and search_path; the catalogue tripwire (only `public.close_deal` among definer functions writes deals); the maintenance path.
Every 0117 test (races in both orders, repeats, the refused-event rollback incl. the nudge, the rules, inputs, roles) now runs against the definer body unchanged. `deal-close-actions.test.ts` adds the REAL `convertLead`, `updateDealSection`, `logDealContact` and `moveDealToStage` — the app's user-session writers of deals — still succeeding, and the kanban still refusing a Won stage.

**Mutation proofs** (a harness that refuses to install unless the database matches a recorded fingerprint, installs by exact string edit, confirms the mutant installed, runs the two files, and restores to the fingerprint in `finally`). First round, 16: 15 killed; M5 (the guard's stage lookup without its organisation predicate) survived and is EQUIVALENT — the guard runs as the caller, `deal_stages_select` already hides other organisations' stages, and a rolled-back probe refused the same writes. Second round, after the review fixes: M17 (step 4b removed), M18 (the `agent_id` arm dropped), M19a (a precedence slip in the lock query alone — EQUIVALENT: step 4b's organisation check still refuses), M19b (the slip plus 4b's organisation check removed), M20 (the INSERT arm's `lost_at` check removed — the survivor of the first round's extra M12b, now covered), M22 (4b keeps the stale role): M17 (step 4b removed — killed by the two lock-wait tests), M18 (the `agent_id` arm dropped — killed by the differential test), M19b (the slip plus 4b's organisation check removed — killed by "another organisation's user named as the deal's agent"), M20 (the INSERT arm's `lost_at` check removed — the first round's extra survivor M12b, now killed) and M22 (4b keeping the stale role — killed by the demotion test) killed; M19a (the precedence slip in the lock query alone) survived and is EQUIVALENT: step 4b's organisation check refuses what the slipped query admits. The migration's own DO block refused every `close_deal` mutant of both rounds (M7–M11, M16–M19b, M22); it does not read the guard's body, and the tests are that proof (M1–M6, M12–M15, M20 killed by them). A planted SECURITY DEFINER function writing deals is refused by both the tripwire test and the DO block.. Every mutant was confirmed installed and every restore returned to the fingerprint.

**Review** (an adversarial workflow: four lenses — the definer restatement, a bypass hunt, rollout and written claims, test quality — with two independent refuters per finding). Acted on: the profile re-read under the lock (the mechanism was reproduced by both refuters; they judged it "not a defect", this record judges it a parity gap the brief names and closes it); `pg_temp` last and the guard's unqualified `deal_stages` (a raw SQL session could shadow it — no PostgREST caller can); the differential test never isolated the `agent_id` arm and pinned no refusal reason; no INSERT carried `lost_at` alone and no INSERT ran as admin; no upsert reopened; a direct PATCH queued behind a close was untested; three written claims overstated ("messages unchanged", "every refusal after the role check", "no other deal write"); the advisor +1 was unpredicted; the rollback recipe and the application floor were unwritten. Confirmed and recorded, not changed here (pre-existing): `created_at` / `stage_entered_at` / `deal_type` are writable by a direct PATCH (reports read them); an admin may flip a stage's `is_won` / `is_lost` with open deals in it; a chosen-id POST tells whether another organisation's deal id exists (the generic RLS + ON CONFLICT answer). Refuted: nothing reached the goal — no path to won / lost without `close_deal` was found.

**Measured** (the branch, local stack at 0118): tsc 0 (`--incremental false`); eslint 0 on the whole tree; unit 2876/2876 across 209 files; the database suite 501/504 — the 3 reds are rls 41/42/57, the public-feed residue on this machine's database (the feed's first 50 rows are residue listings), identical when `main`'s own test file runs against the same database; `deal-close.test.ts` + `deal-close-actions.test.ts` 123/123 (54 of them red against 0117's exact bodies); Playwright desktop 28/28 (`deal-close`, `deal-close-outcomes`, `event-typed-text`, `nudges`, `happy-path`, `deals-export`, setup); `npm run build` exit 0 and `check:static-routes` ok; the restore pack's `close_deal` grants row (true/false/true/false), the guard's (all false) and migrations 118 pass on the local stack. Branch pushed and PR [KALAITSIDIS/gnk-crm#70](https://github.com/KALAITSIDIS/gnk-crm/pull/70) opened; its CI is the fresh-database arbiter.

**Compatibility and deploy order.** Additive for the deployed application: no signature, return shape or enum changes. `aa01ef8` against 0118: closes through `close_deal` exactly as before (same answers, same messages the dialogs show), every other writer of deals it has is untouched (the real actions above). **Deploy order: hosted 0118 is a database-only change — apply it with the app at `aa01ef8` or later, then merge this branch (it carries no application code).** Visible to a DIRECT PostgREST caller only: a refused deal INSERT answers 400 / P0001 from the guard (it runs before the RLS WITH CHECK) where 0117 answered 403 / 42501; nothing in the app keys on either. Advisors: `close_deal` joins the by-design `authenticated_security_definer_function_executable` WARNs — expect 2 ERR + 37 WARN after the apply (36 at 0117).
- **The application rollback floor moves:** against a database at 0118, **no application older than `aa01ef8` can close a deal** — its `markDealWon` / `markDealLost` PATCH is refused before their event writes, so nothing is written and the dialog shows the database's sentence ("Deal is open — it is marked won only from the deal page (close_deal)"). A Vercel instant rollback past `aa01ef8` therefore fails CLOSED for closing and leaves everything else working. Stale browser tabs run no old code: a server action executes on the deployment that serves it.
- **Hosted apply recipe:** ONE `execute_sql` with the file's exact text (the DO block must run with it; `create or replace` keeps ACLs, the file restates them), then, separately: both bodies' md5 against local (`md5(replace(prosrc, chr(13), ''))`), `prosecdef` / owner / `proconfig`, ACLs (`close_deal` authenticated only; the guard body nobody), the trigger BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE, the ledger row 0118 by hand, `non_filename_versions` 0, aal2 gaps 0, partition health 0, the chain verifies, advisors 2 ERR + 37 WARN, and an anon PostgREST call to `close_deal` → 42501. The DO block needs the functions owned by `postgres` — measured on hosted for 0117's two.
- **Existing data:** 0118 adds no constraint and validates no existing row (the guard judges a write, NEW against OLD). Nothing to check before applying beyond the invariants above.

**Rollback.** Through a FORWARD migration, never by hand: re-create 0117's `close_deal` (invoker) AND 0117's guard body AND the BEFORE-UPDATE-only trigger **in one transaction** (0117's file text is a complete body for it), move the `verify-restore.sql` pins (`close_deal` secdef false; migrations +1), and revert the 0118 tests. **Never make `close_deal` an invoker while 0118's guard body is installed**: its own UPDATE would run as `authenticated` and every close would be refused. Guarantees lost on rollback: a user session can again PATCH / POST / UPSERT an open deal to won or lost with no rule and no event, park closing details or a terminal / foreign stage on an open deal, and insert a deal born closed. Kept: 0117's atomic close, its answers, the closed-row guard, the SEC-03 payloads. No data migration either way: every row closed at 0118 is valid at 0117.

**Not changed here** (BACKLOG): the accepted offer `close_deal` requires is whatever `offers.status` says, and offers have no database boundary (a user session may POST an offer already accepted or re-point an accepted offer's `deal_id` within the organisation — no new authority over the Won rule, since an agent may record and accept an offer on their own deal in the app, but the offer's own event and single-accepted check are skipped); hand-written terminal events; `deals_insert` does not bind `agent_id` / `created_by`; `deal_type` / `created_at` / `stage_entered_at` writable, and a closed deal's `expected_value` / `agent_id` editable (a product decision — reports read them); an admin may flip a stage's terminal flags; `verify-restore.sql` does not pin `forbid_srs_api_writes` (0099). No offer, reservation or listing status is changed by a close; the Won reminders stay app-side.

## T-task-deal-org-isolation — a task belongs to the organisation of the deal it names, and a deal's reminder supersession stays inside that organisation (2026-09-26; migration 0119)

**The gap** (BACKLOG "The deal nudge supersession writes across organisations", found by T-atomic-deal-close's design critique; the brief asked for independent verification first). Inspected: gnk-crm `main` = `79f3b3e` (PR #70's landing docs on top of `365c44d`), gnk-web `main` = `b158f37` (it has no writer of tasks or deals). No open pull request on either repository. Mapped read-only first (six readers: every writer of `tasks` in the app, the scripts and the SQL sweeps; every PostgREST embed between tasks and deals; every SQL join of tasks to deals; the test harness; the pins and records; the delete and maintenance paths — then the design). What they established: `tasks.deal_id` (0001) references `deals(id)` alone and `tasks_insert` / `tasks_update` (0030 / 0032) check only the caller's organisation, so nothing ties a task to its deal's tenant; `trg_supersede_deal_nudges` (0025, SECURITY DEFINER) matches the deal's open `deal_no_contact` tasks by `deal_id` alone and writes each `superseded` event with the TASK's `org_id` and `auth.uid()` as actor; the nightly sweep's step 3 (`create_followup_nudges`, 0078) has the same join; every legitimate writer that sets `deal_id` (quickAddTask after an RLS read of the deal, the Won follow-ups from `close_deal`'s answer, the sweep's own insert) takes `org_id` from the same row it read the deal from — except `transitionReservation`, which copies `reservations.deal_id`, itself accepted from the form without an RLS re-read (BACKLOG); nothing in the app, the scripts or the SQL ever changes a task's or a deal's `org_id`; no PostgREST select embeds deals from tasks or tasks from deals, and nothing names `tasks_deal_id_fkey` but the generated types.

**Reproduced before anything changed** — the local stack at 0118 (ledger 118, trigger md5 `081ca764…` = hosted), real PostgREST, aal2 sessions of two throwaway organisations A and B, the new test file run RED (10 of 16):
| attempt at 0118 | result |
|---|---|
| B's agent / B's admin INSERT a task of B naming A's deal (a reminder, an ordinary task) | 201 — the row exists |
| B PATCHes one of B's tasks (with or without a deal of its own) onto A's deal; B's admin the same | 200 — re-pointed |
| B UPSERTs onto an existing task of B, and as a new id | 200 / 201 |
| the service role moves a task's `org_id` to B while it names A's deal | 200 — `tasks.org_id` and `deals.org_id` no longer agree |
| B INSERTs naming a REAL A deal id vs a MISSING id | 201 vs 23503 — an existence oracle on deal ids, through tasks |
| A's agent closes the deal through `close_deal` | B's task marked done, `done_at` set (the `superseded` event goes into B's chain with A's user as actor — the trigger writes `t.org_id`) |
| A's agent logs contact (`last_contact_at`, the trigger's other branch) | the same |
| controls: B cannot read A's deal; A's own reminders (the agent's and a colleague's) complete with the right event and actor; a deal-less task; deletion NO ACTION | as expected, unchanged |
Hosted (read-only `execute_sql`, 2026-09-26): ledger 0118 (118 rows), **0 tasks**, 1 deal, 1 organisation, 0 mismatches, `tasks_deal_id_fkey` = 0001's, the trigger's body = 0025's. Nothing to repair, nothing repaired, no mutation run against production.

**Options compared.**
| option | benefit | cost / risk | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| the organisation predicate in the trigger alone (BACKLOG's first line) | one function re-created | the invalid RELATIONSHIP is still creatable (INSERT/PATCH/UPSERT still 2xx), the oracle stays, the sweep's step 3 still completes it nightly, every future reader of `tasks.deal_id` must remember the predicate | rejected on its own |
| a `tasks_insert` / `tasks_update` policy clause (`exists (select 1 from deals where id = deal_id and org_id = current_org_id())`) | no schema change | binds user sessions only — service_role, definer bodies and pg_cron are not held by RLS; two subselects on every task write; a policy cannot follow a later change of the DEAL's org | rejected |
| a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger on tasks checking the deal's organisation | catches every writer | a second mechanism for what the engine has first-class; judged at write time only; not visible to PostgREST or the types | rejected |
| the composite key ADDED beside the single-column one (0101's shape) | no DROP | two relationships between tasks and deals — the first `deals(...)` embed from tasks answers PGRST201 (measured by mutant M3) | rejected |
| **the predicate PLUS `(org_id, deal_id) → deals (org_id, id)` REPLACING the single-column key (0088's shape), NO ACTION kept** | the relationship is a fact the database checks for every writer, the oracle through tasks closes, one relationship, the pair subsumes the single column, the trigger's contract is legible in its text | a unique key on deals and one index; the types regenerate; a NOT VALID path is needed only if mismatches exist (none do) | **chosen** |

**The fix — migration 0119.**
- **Preflight** counts tasks whose `org_id` differs from their deal's and ABORTS the whole file (one transaction) naming the count and the listing query — nothing deleted, reassigned or repaired, and this file never adds the constraint NOT VALID. If a hosted database ever holds such rows the operator decides: repair through the app, or a separate migration adding the constraint NOT VALID and validating it after the repair — and until it is validated, the sweep's step 3 needs the same predicate (BACKLOG NOTE).
- **`deals_org_id_id_key` UNIQUE (org_id, id)**, the referenced side (implied by the primary key; exists so a referencing table can name the pair — offers, viewings, reservations and `leads.converted_deal_id` can use it later).
- **`tasks_org_deal_fkey` FOREIGN KEY (org_id, deal_id) REFERENCES deals (org_id, id)**, replacing `tasks_deal_id_fkey`; ON DELETE and ON UPDATE NO ACTION exactly as 0001's key (a deal with tasks cannot be deleted — the one app delete, `convertLead`'s compensating rollback, deletes a seconds-old deal no task can name; 0088's CASCADE was NOT copied); MATCH SIMPLE, so a task with no deal is not checked; `org_id` is NOT NULL, so every task with a deal is. `tasks_org_deal_idx` (org_id, deal_id) WHERE deal_id IS NOT NULL is the referencing side (the referential check on a deal's delete or key change, and the trigger's own lookup — 0020's partial nudge index serves only `kind = 'deal_no_contact'`). `set local lock_timeout = '5s'` (0113's lesson) first in the file, ahead of the preflight and the ALTERs: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on deals and tasks, give up and re-apply rather than queue behind a close or a sweep. Run twice by mistake, the file aborts at `deals_org_id_id_key` (42P07) and changes nothing.
- **`trg_supersede_deal_nudges`** re-created from 0025's text with one predicate, `and t.org_id = new.org_id`, in the UPDATE's WHERE; header (`security definer set search_path = public`), body, ACL (the revoke restated — HANDOFF §4.3), the trigger and its WHEN clause otherwise 0025's. It completes the DEAL's organisation's reminders and writes into THAT organisation's chain, attributed to the closer — whom `close_deal` (0118) and `deals_update` (0100) have already placed in that organisation. A same-organisation reminder assigned to ANOTHER staff member completes exactly as before: the predicate reads organisations, never assignees. With the key validated the predicate cannot fail to hold; it is defence in depth for the row the key could not have stopped (planted before 0119 and constrained NOT VALID, or written past the constraint with replication-role privileges), and the test proves it does that.
- **Apply-time assertions:** exactly one foreign key from tasks to deals, named, over (org_id, deal_id) → (org_id, id), VALIDATED, NO ACTION both ways, MATCH SIMPLE; `tasks_deal_id_fkey` gone; the unique key and the index present; the trigger body — comments stripped — scopes its UPDATE to the deal's organisation, is a definer with 0025's search_path, callable by neither anon nor authenticated; the trigger still AFTER UPDATE FOR EACH ROW WITH a WHEN clause; and the constraint EXERCISED once (0088's probe): two organisations, A's stage and deal, A's task on it and a deal-less task accepted, B's task naming A's deal refused — the foreign-key violation is what unwinds the sub-block's own inserts. On hosted the probe runs as `postgres` (not superuser there): `deals_closed_guard` exempts it, and every column it writes is one the tables require. Measured by the mutation runs: the block refuses every mutant tried (below).

**Tests.** Watched RED first: 10 of the 16 tests in `supabase/tests/task-deal-org-isolation.test.ts` fail against 0118's exact catalogue (the table above is that run), 16/16 at 0119. Two kinds of caller, as in `deal-close.test.ts`: supabase-js through PostgREST — how the app writes tasks and closes deals — and one `pg` session as postgres for fixtures, verification and cleanup, which also PLANTS the row the constraint now refuses (`session_replication_role = replica` for that one insert, which bypasses the referential check the way a NOT VALID constraint or a restore would; postgres is superuser on the local stack, in CI too). Two throwaway organisations, five users enrolled sequentially, everything deleted at the end as postgres — every task of BOTH organisations before any deal, because the planted rows name the other organisation's deal:
- the premise: B's admin and agent read nothing of A's deal; A's agent reads it;
- **cross-organisation writes refused without partial changes (23503):** INSERT as B's agent (a reminder) and B's admin (an ordinary task), and no row landed; UPDATE of a deal-less task, of a task on B's own deal, as agent and admin — the row keeps its `deal_id`; UPSERT onto an existing task (merge) and as a new id — nothing written; a task's `org_id` moved away from its deal's — by a user session (42501, `tasks_update`'s WITH CHECK) and by the SERVICE ROLE (23503: a key binds the maintenance role, unlike 0118's role-keyed guard); a real A deal id and a missing one answer the same code and message — the oracle through tasks is closed (`reservations.deal_id` keeps one — BACKLOG);
- **same-organisation links, deal-less tasks, embeds, maintenance:** A's agent and admin link and re-point tasks within A, clear a link, insert without a deal; PostgREST resolves `deals(...)` from tasks and `tasks(...)` from deals (no PGRST201 — the one-relationship claim, measured); the nightly sweep still mints a reminder in the deal's own organisation (its insert meets the new key); a deal with tasks still cannot be deleted (NO ACTION) and a task can, then the deal;
- **closing or contacting A's deal leaves B untouched:** with A's reminder for the deal's agent, one for ANOTHER staff member, an ordinary task on the deal, B's PLANTED reminder naming A's deal and B's own reminder on B's deal — `close_deal` completes A's two reminders with one `superseded` event each (`entity_type` task, actor = the closer, payload `{ kind, deal_id, reason: 'deal_closed' }`), leaves the ordinary task open, B's planted task and B's own reminder untouched (`is_done` false, `done_at` null), writes nothing into B's chain and nothing outside A, both chains verifying; `last_contact_at` (what `logDealContact` writes) does the same with `reason: 'deal_contacted'`;
- **a refused event during the close rolls the reminders back too** (a BEFORE INSERT trigger on events refuses the `lost` event): the close answers the injected failure, the deal stays open, A's reminders stay open, no event survives, B untouched — and the retry closes and completes them, B still untouched;
- **the deal-close protections stand:** B's admin and agent get "Deal not found" from `close_deal`; A's agent's direct PATCH to won is refused by 0118's guard; the planted row gives B no read of the deal;
- **the catalogue:** the key's columns, validation, actions; `tasks_deal_id_fkey` absent; `deals_org_id_id_key`; the index; the trigger body's predicate, definer flag, search_path, ACL; the trigger definition byte-for-byte 0025's.
Every existing test that plants a reminder does so in the deal's own organisation (rls test 27, `deal-close.test.ts`), so the database suite runs unchanged.

**Mutation proofs** (a harness that refuses to start unless the database carries 0119's fingerprint — trigger md5 `2020a0ee…`, the composite key present, the old one absent — installs each mutant by exact catalogue change, confirms it installed, runs the file, then runs the migration's own DO block against the mutant, and restores in `finally` to the fingerprint). M1 0025's trigger body reinstalled (no predicate): 4 tests fail — the close, the contact branch, the refused-event retry, the catalogue — and the DO block aborts "does not scope its UPDATE". M2 the single-column key reinstalled instead of the composite: 6 fail — INSERT, UPDATE, UPSERT, the org move, the oracle, the catalogue — DO block aborts. M3 the single-column key KEPT beside the composite (0101's shape): the embed test fails with PGRST201 and the catalogue test; DO block aborts "found 2". M4 ON DELETE CASCADE (0088's clause): the deletion test and the catalogue test fail; DO block aborts. Control: the DO block passes on the restored catalogue; the fingerprint matched before and after every mutant.

**Review.** An adversarial workflow over the first commit (four lenses — migration correctness and hosted-apply safety, a bypass hunt, test quality, written claims and rollout — with two independent refuters per finding; 36 agents): 16 raw findings, 3 confirmed, 13 refuted. **No defect in the change and no bypass:** every writer of `tasks.deal_id` was walked and none is refused by the key; no path to a cross-organisation task, a cross-organisation supersession or a cross-organisation chain write was found after 0119. Confirmed and fixed in `3031f18`: the rollback recipe said the restore pin moves *back* — a forward rollback is one more ledger row, so it moves forward (0118's record said the same); the three "nothing else was written" scans read the whole `events` table, which the local stack's own crons (lead-sla every ten minutes, the nightly sweeps) write into on their own schedule — now scoped to the two throwaway organisations; the BACKLOG NOTE on the sweep named only a NOT VALID constraint, not a replica-mode restore of a backup that held a mismatch, and only step 3, not step 1's idempotence join. Refuted but adopted anyway as wording: `lock_timeout` first in the file (0113's placement); the cron window in pg_cron's clock (UTC); the test header's exact RED count (ten: the five "B cannot", the first three "leaves B untouched", the two catalogue tests — the protections test pins 0118 and was green); what is proven about the local postgres role; "no existence oracle" scoped to tasks (`reservations.deal_id` keeps one — BACKLOG); the two BACKLOG VERIFY lines that could not discriminate; the performance advisor's INFO rows; a replay's 42P07. Refuted and left: nothing. Also acted on from the review: a restore-pack invariant row that counts task/deal organisation mismatches, because a replica-mode restore loads rows past every constraint.

**Measured** (the branch, local stack at 0119): `tsc --noEmit --incremental false` 0; eslint 0; unit 2874/2876 across 209 files with the two misses being 5 s timeouts under the concurrent database run (`due-at-is-a-cyprus-day`, `env-names-documented`) — 15/15 when run alone; the database suite 517/520 across 34 files — the 3 reds are rls 41/42/57, the public-feed residue on this machine's database (the feed's first 50 rows are residue listings), the same three the last two records name, green on CI's fresh database; the new file 16/16 (10 red at 0118); `verify-restore.test.ts` 4/4 after the pin moved (118 → 119); `npm run build` exit 0 and `check:static-routes` ok; Playwright desktop 12/12 through the worktree's own dev server (`deal-close`, `deal-close-outcomes`, `nudges`, `entity-tasks`, plus the setup login — the one "won follow-up failed" server line is `deal-close-outcomes`' own injected event refusal), 3.5 min. Branch pushed and PR [KALAITSIDIS/gnk-crm#71](https://github.com/KALAITSIDIS/gnk-crm/pull/71) opened; branch CI on the first commit `af6b348` GREEN (run 36223983365: checks, rls, e2e — the fresh-database apply of 0119 and the new file on it); the review follow-up `3031f18` GREEN too (run 36224931437: checks, rls, e2e — the fresh-database apply of the final migration text); the restore-pack invariant row and these records follow it.

**Compatibility and deploy order.** ADDITIVE for the deployed application (`79f3b3e`'s code = `aa01ef8`): every task it writes takes `org_id` from the row it read the deal from, so no request it sends is refused by the new key; no function signature, return shape, grant or enum changes — no `release-compat-contracts` entry (HANDOFF §3's rule is about functions the app calls). `database.types.ts` regenerates: the tasks Relationships entry `tasks_deal_id_fkey` over `deal_id` becomes `tasks_org_deal_fkey` over `(org_id, deal_id)`; nothing in TypeScript names either, nothing embeds across the relationship. **Deploy order: hosted 0119 first, then merge** — the branch carries no application code beyond the generated types. Visible to a DIRECT PostgREST caller only: a task naming a deal of another organisation now answers 409 / 23503 instead of 2xx, and a missing deal id the same; `transitionReservation` of a hold whose `deal_id` was posted as a foreign deal logs the refused prompt and raises none (BACKLOG). Advisors: no ACL moves, so the security advisor's 2 ERR + 37 WARN is expected unchanged after the apply; the performance advisor's INFO rows will move (+1 unused index for `tasks_org_deal_idx` and `deals_org_id_id_key`'s; a partial index may read as an unindexed foreign key) — record the INFO counts before and after.
- **Hosted apply recipe:** ONE `execute_sql` with the file's exact text (its preflight, DO block and probe must run with it; `set local lock_timeout = '5s'` is inside — apply outside 03:00–04:00 UTC, pg_cron's clock (06:00–07:00 Cyprus in summer), and simply re-run on a timeout), then separately: `pg_get_constraintdef` of `tasks_org_deal_fkey` = `FOREIGN KEY (org_id, deal_id) REFERENCES deals(org_id, id)` with `convalidated`, `deals_org_id_id_key`, `tasks_org_deal_idx`, `tasks_deal_id_fkey` gone; the trigger body md5 `2020a0ee…` = local (`md5(replace(prosrc, chr(13), ''))`), `prosecdef`, `search_path=public`, ACL as before (nobody over PostgREST); `pg_get_triggerdef` of `deals_supersede_nudges` unchanged; the ledger row 0119 by hand, `non_filename_versions` 0; `rls_aal2_coverage` 0, the chain verifies; advisors 2 ERR + 37 WARN; an anon PostgREST POST of a task → 42501 as before.
- **Existing data:** the preflight is the check. Hosted holds 0 tasks today, so the constraint validates trivially; if that changes before the apply, the file's abort names the count and the listing query, and the staged path above applies.
- **Rollback floor:** none moves — the application does not depend on 0119.

## T-task-viewing-org-isolation — a task belongs to the organisation of the viewing it names, and a viewing's feedback-reminder supersession stays inside that organisation (2026-09-26; migration 0120)

**The gap** (BACKLOG "Every other `tasks.*` link is org-blind", `viewing_id` first — the exact twin of T-task-deal-org-isolation, found by that change's scouting). Inspected: gnk-crm `main` = `f645274` (0119's landing records on top of the merge `a1b846e`), no open pull request. `tasks.viewing_id` (0020) references `viewings(id)` alone; `tasks_insert` / `tasks_update` check only the caller's organisation; `viewings_select` is organisation-scoped, so B cannot read A's viewing; `trg_supersede_viewing_nudges` (0020, SECURITY DEFINER, never redefined — md5 `57d304f3…` on both local and hosted) matches the viewing's open `viewing_feedback` tasks by `viewing_id` alone and writes each `superseded` event with the TASK's `org_id` and `auth.uid()`; its trigger fires AFTER UPDATE when `feedback` or `status` changes — `saveViewingFeedback` (`update({ feedback })`) and `updateViewingStatus` (`update({ status })`, a compare-and-set on `scheduled`), both on the user session. The only legitimate writers of `tasks.viewing_id` are the nightly sweep's arms 2 and 2b (0078), which take `org_id` and `viewing_id` from the same viewings row; the application writes no task with a viewing. No role can delete a viewing (no DELETE grant, no policy). Mapped read-only first by four readers (every writer of `tasks.viewing_id` and of `viewings.feedback` / `status`; every embed and join between tasks and viewings; every fixture and the test harness; every delete path, pin and record): no PostgREST select embeds across the relationship, nothing names `tasks_viewing_id_fkey` but the generated types, and no fixture links a task to another organisation's viewing. They also found the sweep's reminder-creation guards (arms 2 / 2b, `not exists … t.viewing_id = d.id`) organisation-blind — a planted row would suppress a legitimate one-shot reminder — which the validated key closes too (BACKLOG NOTE), and an inferred twin gap on `viewing_slips` (BACKLOG).

**Reproduced before anything changed** — the local stack at 0119, real PostgREST, aal2 sessions of two throwaway organisations, the new test file run RED: exactly the ten tests marked "RED at 0119" failed and the six controls passed.
| attempt at 0119 | result |
|---|---|
| B's agent / admin INSERT a task of B naming A's viewing (a reminder, an ordinary task) | accepted |
| B PATCHes a task of B (with or without a viewing of its own) onto A's viewing; B's admin the same | accepted |
| B UPSERTs onto an existing task, and as a new id | accepted |
| the service role moves a task's `org_id` to B while it names A's viewing | accepted |

| A's agent saves feedback (the action's exact write) | B's planted reminder marked done; the `superseded` event goes into B's chain with A's agent as actor |
| A's agent cancels a scheduled viewing (the action's exact write) | the same, through the trigger's status branch |

**The fix — migration 0120**, 0119's decision applied to viewings (the options were compared there: the predicate alone, an RLS clause, a tasks trigger, a second key beside the first — all rejected for the same reasons):
- **Preflight** aborts the whole file over any task whose organisation differs from its viewing's, naming the count and the listing query; never NOT VALID by this file.
- **`viewings_org_id_id_key` UNIQUE (org_id, id)**, the referenced side; **`tasks_org_viewing_fkey` (org_id, viewing_id) → viewings (org_id, id)** REPLACING `tasks_viewing_id_fkey` — one relationship, so PostgREST embeds stay unambiguous; NO ACTION both ways as 0020's key; MATCH SIMPLE, so a task without a viewing is unchanged; **`tasks_org_viewing_idx`** the referencing side. `set local lock_timeout = '5s'` first.

The probe names an existing profile as the viewing's agent and skips with a notice on a database that has none (never the case on hosted or CI).

## T-task-mandate-org-isolation — a task belongs to the organisation of the mandate it names, and the key-recall and renewal sweeps raise and complete only that organisation's reminders (2026-09-28; migration 0121)

**The gap** (BACKLOG "Every other `tasks.*` link is org-blind" — `mandate_id`, the twin T-task-viewing-org-isolation's review named NEXT; brought as an external audit finding against `702c70f`, reproduced in an isolated PostgreSQL fixture). Inspected: gnk-crm `main` = `702c70f` (0120's landing records on top of the merge `d9e5c3e`), gnk-web `main` = `b158f37` (no writer of tasks or mandates); no open pull request on either. `tasks.mandate_id` (0006) references `mandates(id)` alone; `tasks_insert` / `tasks_update` check only the caller's organisation; `mandates_select` is organisation-scoped, so B cannot read A's mandate. The only writers of `tasks.mandate_id` are `expire_mandates` step 2 (0053, cron as postgres) and `raise_key_recall_tasks` (0091, SECURITY DEFINER, service_role only — called by `setMandateStatus` on a termination through the service-role client with the acting admin as `p_actor`, and by `expire_mandates` step 4 with no arguments); both take `org_id` and `mandate_id` from the same mandates row; the application writes none (`quickAddTask` has no mandate field; `supersedeRenewalTasks` only completes, under the admin's RLS). Both functions matched tasks to mandates by `mandate_id` alone at FOUR sites: the key-recall duplicate guard and self-heal, and the renewal guard (step 2) and renewal self-heal (step 3) — the audit named the first two; a read-only mapping workflow (five readers + a completeness critic) found the renewal pair and confirmed nothing else in the database or the code reads or writes the link (no view, rule, policy or trigger; no PostgREST embed across it in the app; only the generated types and doc 03 name the constraint).

**Reproduced before anything changed** — the local stack at 0120, real PostgREST, aal2 sessions of two throwaway organisations; the new test file run RED (exactly the 13 tests marked "RED at 0120" failed, the 14 controls passed), and a scratch script that planted every row through the API and recorded each effect:
| attempt at 0120 | result |
|---|---|
| B's admin / agent read A's mandate | `[]` |
| B's agent INSERTs a `key_recall` task of B naming A's mandate; B's admin PATCHes a task of B onto it; UPSERTs one | 201 / 200 (1 row) / 201 |
| B names a REAL A mandate id vs a MISSING one | accepted vs 409 / 23503 — an existence oracle on mandate ids, through tasks |
| a legitimate ended mandate with a key held, no foreign row (`setMandateStatus`'s call) | 1 raised (the baseline) |
| the same with B's `key_recall` row on it | **0 raised, no event** — A's "Return keys" reminder suppressed |
| A's keys go back; the edit-time call (service role, `p_actor` = A's admin) | **B's task completed; a `superseded` event in B's chain with A's admin as actor** (B cannot even read that profile) |
| the nightly `expire_mandates()` as pg_cron runs it (as postgres; rolled back) | A's recall suppressed by a planted row; a planted row on a key-less A mandate completed (actor null); A's renewal reminder suppressed; **of three B renewal rows dated on guessed days, the two wrong ones were completed — B learned A's expiry date** |
Hosted (read-only `execute_sql`, 2026-09-28 13:17Z): ledger 0120 (120 rows, non-filename versions 0), 1 organisation, 2 profiles, 4 mandates (none ended), **0 tasks**, 0 mismatches, 0 dangling mandate ids, 2 property keys, `tasks_mandate_id_fkey` = 0006's, both bodies md5 = local (`06d5423a…` 0091, `fc80663f…` 0053), ACLs as local, 0 other active backends. Nothing to repair, nothing repaired, no mutation run against production.

**The design, compared.** (1) The four predicates alone close the reproduced effects but leave the invalid relationship creatable and the existence oracle open, and every future reader of the link would have to remember the predicate. (2) An RLS clause on tasks binds user sessions only — not the service role or the definer bodies that actually write these rows. (3) A trigger on tasks re-reading the mandate duplicates a foreign key, badly. (4) A composite key BESIDE the single-column one gives PostgREST two relationships (PGRST201 — measured on 0119 and again here as mutant M5). **Chosen: 0119's two layers** — the composite key REPLACES the single-column one (a fact about rows, binding every writer), and the four predicates stay as defence in depth for a row the key could not stop (one kept past a NOT VALID constraint after an approved repair, or loaded by a replica-mode restore) and as each function's contract in its own text. The predicates relate each task to ITS OWN parent row's organisation — never `current_org_id()`: both functions legitimately serve every organisation in one run, and a session-scoped filter would shrink the nightly job to one organisation, or to none under the cron's session.

**The fix — migration 0121:**
- **Preflight** aborts the whole file over any task whose organisation differs from its mandate's, naming the count and the listing query; never NOT VALID by this file. Proven: with one row planted past the key (replica role) inside a rolled-back transaction, the file stopped at the preflight ("0121 aborted: 1 task(s) …") and nothing changed.
- **`mandates_org_id_id_key` UNIQUE (org_id, id)**, the referenced side; **`tasks_org_mandate_fkey` (org_id, mandate_id) → mandates (org_id, id)** REPLACING `tasks_mandate_id_fkey` — NO ACTION both ways as 0006's key (a mandate with tasks still cannot be deleted, nor — through properties → mandates ON DELETE CASCADE — its property; no user session can delete a mandate at all), with one new effect the review made explicit: the update rule now also covers `mandates.org_id`, so a mandate with tasks cannot move to another organisation (as 0119 / 0120 did for deals and viewings; no application path writes it); MATCH SIMPLE (a task without a mandate is unchanged); **`tasks_org_mandate_idx`** the referencing side (0006's `tasks_mandate_idx` kept: lookups by mandate id alone). `set local lock_timeout = '5s'` first, then a guard that aborts unless it took effect (the file must run as ONE transaction, or a failed assertion would not undo the DDL before it). PostgREST keeps one relationship, and the `mandates_safe` view (every UI mandate read, doc 04) exposes `(org_id, id)`, so the regenerated types carry `tasks_org_mandate_fkey` onto it too.
- **`raise_key_recall_tasks`** re-created from 0091's text with `and t.org_id = c.org_id` in the duplicate guard and `and t.org_id = m.org_id` in the self-heal; **`expire_mandates`** from 0053's text with `and t.org_id = m.org_id` in step 2's guard and step 3's self-heal. Nothing else in either body moves (kinds and their separation, the `(mandate_id, kind)` key, the renewal cycle key, the three-arm assignee fallback, the seven Cyprus days, the held-key statuses, step order, the actor). The bodies were generated by a script that copied the two canonical function texts verbatim and inserted the four lines at anchors each asserted to occur once. ACLs restated: `raise_key_recall_tasks` service_role only (T-C4), `expire_mandates` its owner only (0022). Both functions gained or updated a `comment on function`.
- **Apply-time assertions:** exactly one key from tasks to mandates — named, columns, validated, NO ACTION, MATCH SIMPLE; both `org_id` columns NOT NULL (MATCH SIMPLE skips a row with any null key column); the old key gone; the unique key and the index with its definition; **0119's and 0120's keys still validated, with their definitions**; one overload each; each body definer with `search_path=public`; each predicate in its place (comments stripped); **each body equal, by md5, to the canonical 0091 / 0053 body once exactly its added lines are removed** (each line asserted to occur once, `\r` stripped first); the ACLs; and the key EXERCISED once in a sub-block (two organisations, A's property and mandate, A's own link and a mandate-less task accepted, B's cross-organisation task refused by THIS key, at THAT insert — `get stacked diagnostics … constraint_name` plus a step marker, so a key that refused the own-organisation link could not pass as a verdict). The probe needs no profile (a mandate's `created_by` is nullable), so unlike 0120's it also runs on CI's empty database.
- **The restore pack** gains `INTEGRITY: no task names a mandate of another organisation (0121)`, and its migrations pin moves 120 → 121.

**Tests** — `supabase/tests/task-mandate-org-isolation.test.ts`, 28, the structure of 0119/0120's files plus one new device: supabase-js through PostgREST for every write the app sends (users, and the service role exactly as `setMandateStatus` calls the raiser), one `pg` session as postgres that plants B's rows past the key (`session_replication_role = replica`) and runs the nightly sweep AS pg_cron does — `select expire_mandates()` as postgres — inside a transaction that is ROLLED BACK after its reads (the sweep is global; a committed run would also flip, raise and complete other files' fixtures). Because the global sweep also serves this file's other fixtures, the nightly tests assert with `foreignWrites` — no event in an organisation's chain concerns a mandate of another organisation (as entity, through the task, or in the payload) or carries another organisation's user as actor — instead of an empty chain. Covered: the premise; cross-organisation INSERT, UPDATE, UPSERT refused with 23503 and nothing written; the org move (42501 on a user session, 23503 for the service role); the oracle closed; same-organisation links, re-pointing, clearing, mandate-less tasks; embeds `mandates(...)` and `mandates_safe(...)` from tasks and `tasks(...)` from both (no PGRST201); NO ACTION deletion directly and through the property cascade, no DELETE grant on mandates, the task itself deletable; `raise_key_recall_tasks` refused (42501) to anon and to authenticated users of both organisations with nothing written, `expire_mandates` refused to all three API roles and scheduled as postgres; a legitimate recall raised once in its own organisation — title and key count (with_owner and lost not chased), property, assignee (first arm, and the admin fallback), 23:59 Cyprus seven Cyprus days out (and, added after the review, the same with the SESSION's calendar forced a day away from Cyprus's — Pacific/Kiritimati or Etc/GMT+12, whichever disagrees now — so a return to 0053's `current_date + 7` fails at any hour instead of two or three hours a day), one `key_recall_task_created` event with actor = the admin and its exact payload, a repeat raising nothing; B's planted row neither suppressing A's reminder nor being completed by A's self-heal, A's `superseded` event actor = the admin with its exact payload, B's own reminder untouched, nothing in B's chain, both chains verifying; `tasks_update` RLS keeping `supersedeRenewalTasks`' write (its filter re-typed as the admin's client sends it — a pin on the POLICY, not on the action) to A's renewal rows; an injected `key_recall_task_created` refusal and an injected `superseded` refusal each rolling back the call's own task writes (then the retry succeeding); `setMandateStatus`'s two writes replayed as it sends them (read from `lib/actions/mandates.ts`: the status UPDATE, later the raiser RPC, separate requests — the action itself runs inside a Next request and is not driven here): a raise that fails after the committed termination leaves no task, and the nightly run catches it up with a null actor. **The server action is therefore not atomic**: the termination can stand without its reminder until 03:00 UTC — by design since 0053 ("Not fatal … tonight's expire_mandates() will raise anyway"), unchanged here; the nightly run raising each organisation's own reminders once however often it runs, B's planted rows neither blocking nor completed; an overnight expiry flipped and its keys chased in the same pass; the renewal reminder raised on the expiry's Cyprus end of day despite a planted same-day row; the renewal self-heal completing A's stale row only; the kinds kept apart (neither guard satisfied by the other kind; a raised recall surviving the renewal self-heal); the catalogue.

**Test 37 was vacuous, and is honest now.** `rls.test.ts` #37 called `svc.rpc("expire_mandates")` and asserted the recall task survived — but since 0022 not even the service role may execute `expire_mandates` (the restore pack pins it), the RPC was refused with 42501, its error discarded, and the assertion could not fail. 0022 predates 0053, so the test's own "the assertion that earns its keep" never once ran the sweep (0053's apply-time probe did, once, on the database it was applied to). It now asserts the refusal and points to the new file, whose "the kinds stay distinct" test runs the sweep as postgres (mutant M4 below shows that test can fail). Found independently by the mapping workflow.

**Mutation proofs** (local stack, each mutant installed and its installation printed, the file run whole, the correct objects restored and md5-checked afterwards — `raise_key_recall_tasks` `00c9a0ef…`, `expire_mandates` `5615951b…`, the key validated; each mutant ALSO run through the migration's own DO block in a rolled-back transaction): M1 the recall guard predicate removed → 3 fail (the suppression test, the nightly test, the catalogue), DO block aborts "does not scope"; M2 the recall self-heal predicate removed → 5 fail (the edit-time completion, the nightly test, both renewal tests — their `foreignWrites` scan caught the earlier planted recall rows being completed into B's chain — and the catalogue), DO block aborts; M3 the renewal guard predicate removed → 2 fail, DO block aborts; M4 the renewal self-heal predicate removed → 4 fail, DO block aborts; M5 a single-column key kept beside the composite → the embed test (PGRST201) and the catalogue, DO block aborts "found 2"; M6 ON DELETE CASCADE → the deletion test and the catalogue, DO block aborts; M7 the single-column key instead of the composite → 6 fail (INSERT, UPDATE, UPSERT, org move, oracle, catalogue), DO block aborts; M8 (after the review) 0053's `current_date + 7` anchor reinstalled → the new Cyprus-calendar test fails (`days: 8` with the session in Kiritimati). Control: the DO block passes on the restored catalogue.

**Adjacent gaps found, measured, NOT fixed here** (BACKLOG "A mandate's and a key's own parent links are organisation-blind"): measured at 0121 through PostgREST — B's admin can create and activate a B mandate on A's property (201 / 200), after which A cannot activate its own (23505 — `mandates_one_active_per_property` is unique on `property_id` alone) and B's recall task carries A's property reference, A's held-key count, A's property id and A's agent as assignee; a B key filed on A's property (201) on its own raised a recall task in A and would keep A's task from self-healing; B can point B's property's agent at A's agent by a direct PATCH (200), and B's recall task is then assigned to someone who cannot see it. Each is a different relationship (`mandates.property_id`, `property_keys.property_id`, the profile arms — and, found by the review, inferred not measured, `mandates.renewed_from_id`); left out on purpose to keep this change to the task↔mandate relationship, with `mandates.property_id` recorded as the ORDER MATTERS prerequisite of any `tasks.property_id` key.

**Measured** (the branch `ffe2ada`, local stack at 0121): the new file 27/27 (13 red at 0120); the full database suite 560/563 across 36 files — the 3 reds are rls 41/42/57, the public-feed residue on this machine (the feed's 50-row page fills with other files' listings; identical at 0119's and 0120's landings), both earlier isolation files and the new one green; unit 2876/2876 across 209 files; `verify-restore.test.ts` and `cron-jobs-pinned.test.ts` 6/6; `tsc --noEmit --incremental false` 0; eslint 0; the restore pack on the local stack — migrations 121 = 121, the 0121 invariant row 0, both functions' grant rows as pinned (its other reds are this machine's: row counts against the hosted baseline, slip files, and two grant rows that already fail on this stack without the branch).

## T-mandate-key-parent-org-isolation — a mandate names a property and a predecessor of its own organisation, a key a property of its own, and the mandate sweeps read only their own (2026-09-28; migration 0122)

**The gap** (BACKLOG "A mandate's and a key's own parent links are organisation-blind", found and measured by T-task-mandate-org-isolation's scouting; built on the operator's "go ahead with the mandate and key parent links"). Inspected: gnk-crm `main` = `6f6c5f7` (0121's landing records), gnk-web `b158f37`; no open pull request on either. `mandates.property_id` and `property_keys.property_id` (0001, ON DELETE CASCADE) referenced `properties(id)` alone, `mandates.renewed_from_id` (0036, NO ACTION) `mandates(id)` alone; `mandates_insert` / `_update` and `property_keys_insert` / `_update` check only the caller's organisation and role; `saveMandate` and `registerKey` copy the form's property id with no RLS re-read, and authenticated holds column INSERT / UPDATE on every key column. `raise_key_recall_tasks` joined properties and counted keys by `property_id` alone; `expire_mandates` step 2 joined properties the same way. A read-only mapping workflow (three readers and a completeness critic) confirmed the legitimate writers are all same-organisation (`renewMandate` copies org, property and predecessor from a row it read under RLS; the importer creates each mandate on a property it inserted in the same run; every seed, fixture and test is same-organisation), no SQL function writes these columns, and the only app embeds across them are `properties → mandates_safe(!inner)(type, status)` (property list, map, CSV) and `property_keys → properties(reference)` (keys page, keys CSV, movement feed) — no constraint-name or column hint anywhere.

**Reproduced before anything changed** — the local stack at 0121, real PostgREST, aal2 sessions of two throwaway organisations; the new test file run RED (the 15 tests marked "RED at 0121" failed, the 4 controls passed):
| attempt at 0121 | result |
|---|---|
| B's admin INSERTs (draft, active), PATCHes, UPSERTs a B mandate onto A's property | accepted |
| then A activates its own mandate on that property | **23505** — B's active mandate held `mandates_one_active_per_property` (unique on `property_id` alone) |
| the service role moves a mandate's / key's `org_id` away from its property's | accepted |
| B's admin and listing manager file, re-point, upsert a B key onto A's property | accepted |
| B names an A mandate as a B mandate's predecessor (INSERT, PATCH) | accepted |
| real vs missing id on each link | accepted vs 23503 — an existence oracle |
| `raise_key_recall_tasks` for B's mandate on A's property (planted) | a task in B carrying A's reference and key count |
| A's ended mandate with no key of its own, a B key on the property | a "Return keys" task raised in A; with A's own key back, A's task stayed open |
| the nightly `expire_mandates()` | a B renewal reminder naming A's property |
Hosted (read-only, 15:11Z): ledger 0121, 1 organisation, 17 properties, 4 mandates (none renewed), 2 keys, 0 mismatches on each link. Nothing to repair.

**The fix — migration 0122** (0119–0121's two layers):
- **Preflight** aborts the whole file over any mismatch on the three links, naming the counts; never NOT VALID. Proven with a planted key in a rolled-back transaction.
- **`mandates_org_property_fkey` (org_id, property_id) → properties (org_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE, `property_keys_org_property_fkey` the same, `mandates_org_renewed_from_fkey` (org_id, renewed_from_id) → mandates (org_id, id)**, each REPLACING its single-column key (one relationship per pair; the embeds above resolve, including through `mandates_safe`, which exposes both columns), on 0088's `properties_org_id_id_key` and 0121's `mandates_org_id_id_key`, each with a referencing index. New effect, as in 0119–0121: the update rules now also pin `properties.org_id` under a property's mandates and keys, and `mandates.org_id` under a successor (no application path writes either).
- **`mandates_one_active_per_property` re-keyed to (org_id, property_id)** WHERE status = 'active' — added after the review: a unique index is checked at insert and a foreign key at the end of the statement, so on the old key B's active mandate naming A's property answered 23505 when A's property was under an active mandate and 23503 when not — an oracle on A's mandate state that the key alone left open. With the key, every mandate of a property is that property's organisation's, so the rule is unchanged for valid rows (A's own second active mandate still answers 23505, which `setMandateStatus` maps to "This property already has an active mandate"), and a foreign row can no longer collide.
- **The sweeps:** `raise_key_recall_tasks` gains `and p.org_id = m.org_id` in its candidates' property join and `and k.org_id = m.org_id` in both held-key tests (the count and the self-heal's NOT EXISTS); `expire_mandates` gains `and p.org_id = m.org_id` in step 2. Row by row, never `current_org_id()`. Bodies generated by a script from 0121's text; each asserted by md5 to be 0121's body plus exactly the added lines (`00c9a0ef…` / `5615951b…`).
- **Assertions:** a single-transaction guard; each key's pair, columns, validity, delete rule, NO ACTION update, MATCH SIMPLE, exactly one key per pair, the old names gone; the referencing indexes' and the re-keyed index's definitions; every `org_id` involved NOT NULL; 0088's and 0119–0121's keys unchanged; one overload each; definer, `search_path`, ACLs (recall service_role only, expire owner only); and four probes — B's mandate, B's ACTIVE mandate on a property that has an active one, B's key, B's renewal — each refused by ITS key at the cross-organisation step (a unique violation there is reported as a failed verdict). No profile needed: the probes run on CI's empty database too.
- **The restore pack** gains three 0122 INTEGRITY rows (mandate→property, key→property, mandate→predecessor); its migrations pin moves 121 → 122.

**Tests** — `supabase/tests/mandate-key-parent-org-isolation.test.ts`, 20, 0121's structure (PostgREST for every write the app sends and the service role's calls; one `pg` session as postgres for fixtures, committed replica-mode plants, the nightly sweep in a rolled-back transaction, verification and cleanup; two throwaway organisations with admin, agent and listing-manager users). Covered: the premise; cross-organisation INSERT / UPDATE / UPSERT refused on all three links with nothing written; org moves refused (42501 for a user, 23503 for the service role); the key's refusal no longer an oracle on property or mandate ids; B's active mandate reading the same 23503 whether or not A's property has an active mandate, while A's own second active mandate still answers 23505; A able to activate its own; same-organisation creation, re-pointing, the renewal insert `renewMandate` sends, keys filed and re-pointed by a listing manager; every embed the app uses (the property list's `mandates_safe!inner` with its filter, `mandates → properties`, `properties → mandates / property_keys`, `property_keys → properties`, the movement feed's nested `key_movements → property_keys → properties`); deletion (a property cascades to its mandates — predecessor and successor — and keys; a predecessor cannot be deleted under its successor); the sweeps against planted rows (no B reminder carries A's property — with B's own key planted too, so only the property-join predicate stands in the way; B's key neither raises A a reminder nor blocks A's self-heal, whose `superseded` event is A's admin's; the nightly run mints no B renewal or recall for A's property and still serves B's own); the catalogue.

**Mutation proofs** (local stack; each installed and printed, the file run whole, restored and md5-checked; each also through the migration's own DO block in a rolled-back transaction): M1 the property-join predicate removed → at first killed ONLY by the catalogue's text check, because the held-count predicate zeroed the count for a B mandate without B keys — the test now plants a B key too and M1 fails it on its own; M2 the held-count predicate → the key test + catalogue; M3 the self-heal key predicate → the key test + catalogue; M4 the renewal property-join predicate → the nightly test + catalogue; M5 / M6 / M7 each key single-column → their INSERT / UPDATE / UPSERT / move / oracle tests + catalogue; M8 a second key beside the composite → the embed test (PGRST201) + catalogue; M9 NO ACTION instead of CASCADE → the deletion test + catalogue. The DO block aborted on all nine and passed the restored catalogue. The index re-key was proven the other way round: the new test and the catalogue check ran RED on the first draft (`8d275f6`, 23505 vs 23503) and GREEN on the revision.

**Review.** An adversarial workflow over `8d275f6` (four lenses, two refuters per finding). Its migration lens replayed the file on a 0121-shaped catalogue in a rolled-back transaction (clean apply, three probes refused, nothing left, a rerun aborting at the first DROP CONSTRAINT); its bypass lens found no role, NULL, view, definer body or restore route to a cross-organisation mandate or key after 0122. Two lenses independently found the one real residue — the active-slot oracle above — fixed in `987d39c` with its test and probe before anything reached hosted. Its tests lens (six findings survived, none a defect) found the same masking as M1 on the NIGHTLY path — the recall arm there now plants B's key too, and M1 fails it as well — a same-organisation re-point test that checked only the error (it now asserts the moved row), the renewal reminder wrongly said to carry a key count (header wording), and the kept indexes' provenance; all fixed on the branch before the hosted apply. Also acted on: the movement feed's nested embed now tested, test titles saying what the KEY's refusal no longer reveals (a primary-key collision is a separate, table-wide matter), the lock-wait wording, `key_movements.key_id` named among the deferred links. Deferred to BACKLOG ("The remaining parent links of mandates, keys and properties"): the profile links, the assignee fallback arms, `owner_contact_id`, `signed_document_id`, `key_movements.key_id`, and 13 single-column links onto properties.

**Measured** (the branch, local stack at 0122): the new file 20/20 (15 red at 0121, the oracle test red on the first draft); the four isolation files 80/80; the full database suite 580/583 across 37 files at `8d275f6` — the 3 reds rls 41/42/57, the public-feed residue on this machine; rls mandate / key tests green after the revision; unit 2876/2876; `verify-restore.test.ts` and `cron-jobs-pinned.test.ts` green; `tsc --noEmit --incremental false` 0; eslint 0; the restore pack on the local stack — migrations 122 = 122, all six INTEGRITY rows 0, both functions' grants as pinned; Playwright desktop 12/12 at `8d275f6` (`mandate-lifecycle`, `party-defaults`, `contact-merge`, `keys-export`, `properties-export` + setup) and `mandate-lifecycle` + `party-defaults` 6/6 again on the revision (its "cannot go live beside its predecessor" check rides the 23505 mapping); the final text applied through the CLI from a 0121-shaped catalogue (assertions and four probes passed; bodies `b13ee908…` / `1ef31492…`). Branch CI green on `8d275f6` (run 36444309002: checks, rls, e2e).

**Compatibility and deploy order.** ADDITIVE: every legitimate writer is same-organisation, so only a crafted foreign id — accepted until now — is refused (23503; `saveMandate` / `registerKey` show its raw message, as for any other database error); the sweeps copy property and mandate from the same row, so no nightly insert can be refused; no signature, return shape, grant or enum changes — no release-compat entry; `database.types.ts` regenerated (Relationships of mandates, mandates_safe and property_keys only). **Hosted 0122 first, then merge**, outside 03:00–04:00 UTC and away from a :x0 minute.

**Rollback.** A FORWARD migration: drop the three composite keys and their indexes, re-add `mandates_property_id_fkey` / `property_keys_property_id_fkey` (single-column, ON DELETE CASCADE) and `mandates_renewed_from_id_fkey`, re-create `mandates_one_active_per_property` on `(property_id)` WHERE active, re-create both functions from 0121's text with 0121's comments; regenerate the types, move the restore pin FORWARD, remove the three 0122 invariant rows, remove the new test file, revert the docs. No data moves either way.

## T-viewing-parent-org-isolation — a viewing shows a property, and is for a contact, of its own organisation, and the sweep's viewing reminders read only their own property (2026-09-28; migration 0123)

**The gap** (BACKLOG "A viewing's own parent links are organisation-blind", found by T-task-viewing-org-isolation's review; handed over by the operator as an external audit's hypothesis to verify, not to assume). Inspected: gnk-crm `main` = `6501aec` (0122's landing records, the audit's commit), gnk-web untouched (it writes no viewing and reads none). `viewings.property_id` and `viewings.contact_id` (0001, NO ACTION) referenced `properties(id)` / `contacts(id)` alone; `viewings_insert` (0030) and `viewings_update` (0032) check only the caller's organisation and role; `createViewing` copies the form's ids with no RLS re-read; contacts had no `(org_id, id)` key. `create_followup_nudges` (0078, never redefined since) arms 2 and 2b joined `properties p on p.id = v.property_id` with no organisation predicate and copy `v.property_id` and `p.reference` into the reminder. No later migration, trigger or guard closed either.

**Reproduced before anything changed** — the local stack at 0122, real PostgREST, aal2 sessions (TOTP factors enrolled) of two throwaway organisations; the new test file run RED (17 of 21 failed; the 4 that passed are the premise and the same-organisation controls):
| attempt at 0122 | result |
|---|---|
| B's agent / admin INSERT a viewing of B naming A's property, or A's contact (createViewing's exact payload) | accepted |
| B re-points its own viewing onto A's property / contact (PATCH), UPSERT merge and new id | accepted |
| a real A id vs a random id on either link | accepted vs 23503 — an existence oracle |
| the service role and the table owner insert the same rows | accepted |
| the service role moves a viewing's `org_id`, a property's or a contact's `org_id` out from under its viewings | accepted |
| arm 2 (global run) over B's completed viewing on A's property (planted, rolled back) | a task IN B: `Log viewing feedback: <A's reference>`, `property_id` = A's property |
| arm 2b (org-scoped run) over B's no-show on A's property | a task IN B: `Rebook after no-show: <A's reference>`, `property_id` = A's property |
B could read neither parent directly (premise test). Nothing was written into A. The sweep reads no contact data (arm 2b compares contact ids inside the viewing's own organisation), so the contact link was an acceptance and an oracle, not a disclosure. Hosted (read-only): ledger 0122, 1 organisation, 2 profiles, 0 viewings, 0 tasks, 0 mismatches on either link, the sweep body = 0078's. **Business impact, honestly scaled:** production holds ONE organisation, so nothing was exposed; the defect is a tenant boundary that did not hold the moment a second organisation exists — any member of it who learned a property or contact id (they travel in links, slips and logs) could plant viewings on another agency's listing, receive reminders carrying its reference, and probe which ids exist.

**The fix — migration 0123** (0119–0122's two layers):
- **Lock, then preflight.** `lock table viewings, properties, contacts in access exclusive mode` (every lock the DDL needs, at its strongest, so none is upgraded mid-file) BEFORE the counts, then abort the whole file over any mismatch on either link, naming both counts and the query that lists them; never NOT VALID; nothing deleted, reassigned or repaired. The preflight also refuses when the live `create_followup_nudges` is not 0078's body (md5, CRs stripped — added on the review's suggestion): section B restates 0078's text and must not silently overwrite an unrecorded change on the target. Run twice by mistake, the file therefore stops in its preflight. The LOCK lives inside the preflight's DO block: the Supabase CLI sends a migration as one pipelined implicit transaction, where `SET LOCAL` takes effect but a top-level `LOCK TABLE` is refused (25P01 — measured on the first local apply, which changed nothing).
- **`viewings_org_property_fkey` (org_id, property_id) → properties (org_id, id)** and **`viewings_org_contact_fkey` (org_id, contact_id) → contacts (org_id, id)**, NO ACTION, each REPLACING its single-column key (one relationship per pair — every embed the app sends still resolves), on 0088's `properties_org_id_id_key` and a new `contacts_org_id_id_key`; referencing indexes `(org_id, property_id)` / `(org_id, contact_id)` (the unindexed-FK advisor keys on leading columns); 0077's single-column indexes kept. No unique index covers either column, so no 23505 answers before the key (0122's lesson, asserted). New effect, as in 0119–0122: the update rule pins `properties.org_id` / `contacts.org_id` under their viewings (no application path writes either).
- **The sweep:** `and p.org_id = v.org_id` in arms 2 and 2b's property join, row by row, never `current_org_id()`; the body is 0078's plus exactly those two lines (md5 `09f1d936…` asserted on the remainder, CRs stripped), same signature, return type, definer, `search_path`, ACL (service_role only, restated); a function comment added.
- **Assertions:** single-transaction guard; each key's pair, columns, validity, NO ACTION both ways, MATCH SIMPLE, exactly one key per pair, the old names gone; the unique key and index definitions; every column involved NOT NULL; 0088's and 0119–0122's eight tenant keys unchanged; one overload; and two probes (B's viewing on A's property with B's contact, on A's contact with B's property), each refused by ITS key at the cross-organisation step. A viewing needs a profile as agent, so the probes skip with a NOTICE on a profile-less database (CI's and `db reset`'s migration run); hosted has 2 profiles, so they run there.
- **The restore pack** gains two 0123 INTEGRITY rows; its migrations pin moves 122 → 123.

**Tests** — `supabase/tests/viewing-parent-org-isolation.test.ts`, 22, 0122's structure. Every sweep scenario and every migration replay runs in ONE transaction on the postgres connection that is rolled back after its reads, so the malformed rows (planted with `session_replication_role = replica`) never outlive the test and the local crons never see them. Covered: the premise; INSERT / UPDATE / UPSERT on each link refused for B's agent and admin with nothing written; the same 23503 message for a foreign and a missing id, the detail differing only in the id B sent, and nothing of A's (org id, reference, contact name) in the error body; the service role and the table owner refused; org moves refused (42501 for a session, 23503 for the service role, for the viewing and for either parent); same-organisation create (createViewing's payload), re-point, the contact merge's repoint, a reschedule; every embed shape the app sends (detail, list, clash check, the CSV export with `viewing_slips`) and the reverse embeds; deletion still NO ACTION; arm 2 (global) and arm 2b (org-scoped) each ignoring a planted foreign-property viewing while serving B's own; valid reminders for BOTH organisations through org-scoped and global runs, twice — one task and one `followup_task_created` each, titles, Cyprus due dates computed in SQL, the assignee fallback (B's agent deactivated → B's admin), the event payloads, both chains verifying; completion by arms 4 / 4b (feedback written with the edit-time trigger off; a rebooking) with one `superseded` each; the catalogue; and the file itself — applied over a 0122-shaped catalogue and this database's accumulated data (both probes ran), refusing in its preflight over planted mismatches (1 property, 2 contacts — the message proves the preflight fired before the key additions; that it precedes ALL DDL is the file's text order, not a test), refusing before any DDL when the live sweep is not 0078's (a tampered title), stopping in its preflight when run twice, and waiting at its LOCK — before the preflight's pass notice — behind an uncommitted viewing insert until 55P03. The events half of the "B holds nothing of A's" check is defensive (the arms' payloads carry no property); the task half is what failed at 0122.

## T-deal-close-settled-flake — a lock-wait test helper marks its promise handled at creation (2026-09-28; tests only)

CI run 36474616830 on main `e45bd74` failed its `rls` job with all 606 database tests green: vitest caught one unhandled rejection (`Account deactivated.`, P0001 from `close_deal`) in `deal-close.test.ts`. `settled()` wrapped the blocked call as `p.finally(...)` and attached its rejection handler only after `await a.query("commit")`; B's refusal can land in the same event-loop turn as A's COMMIT reply, so the promise was briefly rejected with no handler. Reproduced deterministically with a 300 ms delay between commit and `value()` (two unhandled rejections, exit 1, both tests green); fixed by `tracked.catch(() => {})` in `settled()` — `value()` still returns `tracked`, so callers see the rejection — in `deal-close.test.ts` and the identical helper in `events-chain-order.test.ts` (latent there). No assertion changed; both files 117/117 on three consecutive runs. The merge commit's failed `rls` job was re-run green (attempt 2).
