**The fix — migration 0124** (0119–0123's two layers):
- **Lock, then preflight.** `lock table reservation_installments, reservations, leads, properties in access exclusive mode` inside the preflight's DO block (0123's CLI lesson), children first, properties last; then abort whole over any mismatch on the three links (counts and the joins that list them), and over any of the four functions whose BODY (md5, CRs stripped) or ATTRIBUTES (definer, search_path, volatility, EXECUTE grants — the review's suggestion) differ from what it restates, so an unrecorded change is never silently overwritten. No order avoids every lock cycle — the proposal door and a key-less enquiry read properties before leads — so an apply-time collision can end 40P01 as well as 55P03; either rolls back cleanly (a visitor's request answers 503 and is sent again).
- **Keys** (each REPLACING its single-column key — one relationship per pair): `reservations_org_property_fkey` (org_id, property_id) → properties (org_id, id) ON DELETE RESTRICT; `reservation_installments_org_reservation_fkey` (org_id, reservation_id) → reservations (org_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE, on a new `reservations_org_id_id_key`; `leads_org_property_fkey` (org_id, property_id) → properties (org_id, id), MATCH SIMPLE (a lead with no property is not checked); referencing indexes `reservations_org_property_idx`, `leads_org_property_idx` (partial); the instalment key is covered by its unique rule.

- **The readers**, row by row: `and p.org_id = r.org_id` (warn), `and r.org_id = i.org_id` ×2 and `and p.org_id = r.org_id` (remind), `and p.org_id = l.org_id` plus `p.id as property_id` (the SLA sweep copies the property it READ — a lead naming a foreign property is still chased, without it), `and pr.org_id = c.org_id` (preview, STABLE kept). ## T-task-contact-property-org-isolation — a reservation belongs to the organisation of its contact, a task to the organisation of the contact and the property it names; the retention sweep looks for and completes only the contact's own organisation's reminders (2026-09-29; migration 0126)

**The gap** (BACKLOG "Every other `tasks.*` link is org-blind" — `contact_id` and `property_id`, the two 0125 left open, with `reservations.contact_id` named there as the one that must come first, and `create_followup_nudges` arm 4c; reported the same day by an external audit of `2bad473` that reproduced it on an isolated PostgreSQL fixture and asked for independent verification). | attempt at 0125 | result |
|---|---|
| B's agent / admin INSERT, PATCH, UPSERT a task naming A's contact, and one naming A's property | accepted |
| B's agent / admin INSERT, PATCH, UPSERT a reservation (on B's own property) naming A's contact | accepted |
| a real A id vs a missing id, per link (tasks' two, the hold's contact) | accepted vs 23503 — an existence oracle |

**Business impact, honestly scaled:** one organisation in production, so nothing was exposed; with a second organisation the gap let a member of it read another agency's AML retention dates and purges back from its own task list, silence its destruction reminder, and write rows naming its contacts and properties; hosted holds 0 tasks and 0 reservations.

**The fix — migration 0126** (0119–0125's two layers):
- **Lock, then preflight.** `lock table reservations, properties, contacts, tasks in access exclusive mode` inside the preflight's DO block, parents first, tasks last — the order the reservation and lead-SLA sweeps take them; no order avoids every cycle (`create_followup_nudges` writes tasks in arm 1 before it reads properties and contacts; any task insert naming a contact or property checks its key at statement end), so a collision is a clean 40P01 or 55P03 rollback. lock_timeout bounds each table's wait, so up to about 20 s during which properties and contacts — read by nearly every page — are unreadable. Then abort whole over any mismatch on the three links (the listing joins in the message), over any of the three keys it replaces not being 0001's / 0044's (validated, not deferrable, the only one for its pair, its exact delete rule — the rule it preserves), and over any of the three functions whose body (md5, CRs stripped) or attributes (definer, `search_path`, language, return type, volatility, the argument list with its default, strictness, parallel safety, leakproof, EXECUTE grants) differ from what it restates; comments restated, not guarded. Never NOT VALID; nothing deleted, reassigned or repaired.
- **Keys** (each REPLACING its single-column key — one relationship per pair), the reservation's FIRST, all in one transaction: `reservations_org_contact_fkey` (org_id, contact_id) → contacts (org_id, id) **ON DELETE SET NULL (contact_id)** — the first column-list SET NULL in this repository (PostgreSQL 15+; local and hosted run 17.6): a plain SET NULL on a composite key nulls every referencing column, and `reservations.org_id` is NOT NULL, so deleting a contact would fail 23502 where it used to clear the link; `tasks_org_contact_fkey` (org_id, contact_id) → contacts (org_id, id) and `tasks_org_property_fkey` (org_id, property_id) → properties (org_id, id), NO ACTION as 0001's were; partial `(org_id, x) WHERE x IS NOT NULL` indexes (the advisors' unindexed-FK rule reads leading columns; the single-column indexes stay for the contact and property pages); MATCH SIMPLE; every org_id NOT NULL (asserted). ON UPDATE NO ACTION now covers the parents' org_id: a linked contact or property cannot move organisation.
- **Why the reservation key must come first, and in the same file.** Both reservation sweeps copy the hold's contact into `tasks.contact_id`; the tasks contact key alone turns one B hold naming an A contact into a refused insert that aborts both sweeps for EVERY organisation (the audit measured it). Together, in one transaction, there is no moment with the second and without the first.
- **The sweeps**, row by row, never `current_org_id()` (every one serves every organisation in one cron run; the existing `p_org` filters are the caller's scope and stay): `create_followup_nudges` gains `and t.org_id = d.org_id` in arm 2c's duplicate guard and `and t.org_id = c.org_id` in arm 4c's self-heal — arm 2c's guard keeps ignoring `is_done` on purpose (0078's cycle key: an admin who ticks the reminder off by hand is not re-reminded every night), pinned by a test; `warn_expiring_reservations` and `remind_due_installments` copy the hold's contact through `left join contacts ct on ct.id = r.contact_id and ct.org_id = r.org_id` (`ct.id as contact_id`) instead of `r.contact_id` — 0124's SLA-sweep idiom (copy what was read through a tenant-bound join). For every hold the key admits that is the same id; for a hold it could not have stopped (a replica-mode restore, a future NOT VALID repair) the reminder is raised WITHOUT the foreign contact instead of the tasks key aborting the run for every organisation — LEFT, because a hold's contact is optional and an absent one must not suppress a valid reminder. The file is GENERATED from 0123's and 0125's committed text by a script that checks every insertion count and md5; bodies otherwise byte-identical (titles, due dates, Cyprus-day keys, assignees, events, guards, self-heals, `p_org` scope); ACLs restated (service_role only); comments restated with one " Since 0126" sentence.
- **Assertions:** single-transaction guard; each key's pair, columns, validity, delete rule and SET NULL column list, NO ACTION update, MATCH SIMPLE, not deferrable, one key per pair, old names gone, and its exact `pg_get_constraintdef` text (what pg_dump writes and the restore pack reads); the two referenced keys; the three indexes; no unique index naming contact_id / property_id without org_id; NOT NULL org_ids; 0119–0125's and 0123's ten keys unchanged; each function's attributes, md5 (old body + exactly ITS OWN lines), counted predicates and grants; and four probes needing no profile — B's task on A's contact, B's task on A's property, B's hold on its own property naming A's contact, each refused by ITS key at the cross-organisation step, and deleting a contact a hold names clearing only its contact_id (org_id, property, status kept).
- **The restore pack** gains four 0126 INTEGRITY rows — the three mismatch counts and one of dangling ids (a row that escaped a composite key is neither cleared by SET NULL nor refused by its parent's delete); its migrations pin moves 125 → 126.

**Tests** — `supabase/tests/task-contact-property-org-isolation.test.ts`, 56; the shared `supabase/tests/revert-0126.ts` (0126's lines, `strip0126` / `stripContactJoin0126`, and `REVERT_0126_SQL` — 0125's catalogue rebuilt inside the caller's transaction, a no-op at 0125). 0123's, 0124's and 0125's test files now take 0126 off first in their reverts and strip 0126's lines before comparing their bodies (0126's contact keys depend on 0123's `contacts_org_id_id_key`; its lines sit in the bodies 0123 / 0124 / 0125 pin). ## T-contact-merge-org-isolation — a contact merge moves only its own organisation's rows (2026-09-30; no migration)

**Defect (BACKLOG, found by T-task-viewing-org-isolation's review; re-reported by an external audit of `378e5e1`).** `mergeContacts` proved both contacts belonged to the caller's organisation and then ran every repoint on the service-role client filtered by the duplicate's id alone. The service role bypasses RLS, so the ownership check on the two contacts constrained nothing else. Ten links onto `contacts` are still single-column (`leads.contact_id`, `deals.buyer_contact_id` / `seller_contact_id`, `offers.contact_id`, `share_links.contact_id`, `buyer_requirements.contact_id`, `mandates.owner_contact_id`, `properties.owner_contact_id` / `developer_contact_id`, `contacts.merged_into_id`), and `documents.entity_id` is polymorphic, so a row of B may name A's contact; A's merge then rewrote it onto A's primary, and B could read A's surviving contact id through its own row.

**Reproduced before the change**, independently, at `378e5e1` on the local stack at 0126 — `supabase/tests/contact-merge-org-isolation.test.ts`, which drives the REAL action (real service client, real `logEvent`, aal2 sessions of two throwaway organisations; only `revalidatePath` and the Next request plumbing stubbed): B cannot read A's contacts; B's admin's `POST /leads` naming A's duplicate is ACCEPTED; A's admin merging two A contacts moved all fourteen A references correctly AND rewrote all eleven B references onto A's primary (2 of 8 tests RED, each on exactly that). `viewings`, `reservations` and `tasks` refuse a B row naming A's contact with 23503 (0123 / 0126), so for those three the new filter is defence in depth. The e2e spec and `merge-repoints-every-fk.test.ts` could not see it: neither seeds a second organisation, and the latter only checked that each column was repointed.

**Fix.** `orgId = profile.orgId` (never a form value) and `.eq("org_id", orgId)` on every service-role query: both contact reads, the archive, all fourteen repoints (the document repoint keeps `entity_type = 'contact'`, the merged-into repoint keeps `neq("id", duplicateId)`), and the backfill. The archive and the backfill now `.select("id")` and refuse a zero-row write ("Contact not found" before anything moved; "The primary contact was not found — … run the merge again" after the archive) rather than report a merge. The resumable order (archive first, idempotent repoints and note backfill), the event types and payloads, actor and org attribution, and the revalidation are unchanged. The old "Cross-org merge refused" check stays as a second line; with the scoped reads a foreign id now reads as "Contact not found". Foreign rows that name our contact are left exactly as stored — not repaired, not reassigned.

**Not done, on purpose.** No migration: tenant-bound keys for the ten single-column links remain the BACKLOG catalogue's work (a B row can still NAME A's contact, an existence oracle through accepted-vs-23503, and after an A merge such a row keeps pointing at A's archived duplicate). Nothing in gnk-web depends on this action.

**Tests.** `supabase/tests/contact-merge-org-isolation.test.ts` (8, real stack: the live FK list; B's read refused and B's lead plant accepted; the three tenant keys' 23503; a full merge — A moved, B untouched, B's lead still reads the duplicate, the other-type document untouched, duplicate archived onto the primary, backfill of e-mail / extra phone / note, exactly one `merged` and one `archived` event in A by A's admin and none in B; an interrupted merge resumed, and a third run moving no row in either organisation, note appended once (it does log the `merged` / `archived` pair again — pre-existing, BACKLOG); agent refused; B's admin refused for A/A, B/A and A/B pairs; unknown id refused) — RED 2 / GREEN 8 before / after. `lib/actions/merge-contacts-org-scope.test.ts` (20, recording client with ONE record per `from()` chain: each of the fourteen repoints individually carries the profile org, its duplicate filter and its extra predicate; reads / archive / backfill scoped; no chain without the profile org and none carrying the form's forged `org_id`; events in the profile org; zero-row read / archive / backfill refused with nothing logged) — 18 of 20 fail on the pre-fix action (the two that pass pin what it already did right: events in the profile org, a foreign id read as missing), and a mutant dropping ONLY the offers filter fails exactly three assertions across the two unit files — two here (that chain's own check and the no-unbounded-chain check) and the offers line of `merge-repoints-every-fk.test.ts`. `tests/unit/merge-repoints-every-fk.test.ts` now also requires (14 new tests, all RED on the pre-fix action) each migration-derived column's OWN chain to carry `.eq("org_id", orgId)` and `orgId` to be bound to `profile.orgId`. `merge-contacts-event-payload.test.ts` scripts the archive and backfill rows it now needs.

**Review before merge (2026-09-30, ULTRACODE).** Four independent reviewers (correctness / isolation, schema completeness, test validity, docs / CI), each finding put to two skeptics told to refute it: 18 agents, 7 findings, none against the fix. Three were errors in this record, corrected before merge: the struck BACKLOG entry had taken nine of the ten single-column links out of open work (now their own entry, with a `pg_constraint` VERIFY), a mandate line still said the merge rewrites B's mandate, and the mutant count above had been credited to one file. Three are pre-existing and filed in BACKLOG rather than fixed here, because the brief kept the resumable design unless a demonstrated defect forced a change: two concurrent merges of one duplicate split its rows (the archive has no `is_archived = false` predicate), a re-run of a completed merge logs its events again, and contact notes stay on the merged-away duplicate (one of two reviewers upheld that one). A claim that HANDOFF was stale was refuted — HANDOFF records landed state and is updated at landing.

**Landing (2026-09-30, on the operator's "land it", then "merge #82 and #81").** The first branch run (`1e2f0ca`, run 36690186210) had rls and e2e green but `checks` red at its first verification step (`npm audit`, after install) — four advisories against two transitive deps of `@sentry/nextjs`' build tooling, published 2026-09-29 ~23:45Z; the finding was in main's lockfile, though no run on main was red — so CI had not run typecheck / lint / unit. The brief excluded dependency upgrades, so the operator chose: a separate lockfile-only PR #82 first (`T-audit-fix-2026-09-30` below), then #81's branch updated with main (`d710379`, run 36708055298 green: checks with unit 2910 incl. the 20 + 27 merge tests, rls with the new file 8/8, e2e). The first merge attempt for #82 was refused by the session's auto-mode classifier; the same command passed after the operator named the merges. ## T-aal1-definer-boundary — every definer surface a signed-in session reaches checks the second factor; keys move only through their RPC (2026-09-30; migration 0127)

**Defect.** The second factor is mandatory (0059): every table carries a RESTRICTIVE `require_aal2`, and every RPC since 0101 calls `mfa_satisfied()`. A SECURITY DEFINER function or a view without `security_invoker` runs as its owner, so the tables' policy is not between it and the data. At 0126 four did not check: `record_key_movement` (BACKLOG 2529) — a password-only (aal1) admin, listing manager or agent moved keys and wrote key events; `next_reference` — checked nothing at all, so any signed-in session advanced ANY organisation's counter or created one for an arbitrary id; `mandates_safe` (definer on purpose, 0100) — its WHERE mirrors `mandates_select` but not `require_aal2`, so aal1 read the organisation's mandates; `org_mfa_status` — aal1 listed which colleagues have no factor. And the key tables could be written around the RPC (2540): `key_movements_insert` (0002, from the retired app-side writer) admitted a direct INSERT, and `property_keys` a direct write of status and the holder cache — no movement, no event. `record_key_movement` also dropped a typed holder (2535): a non-STRICT SELECT INTO that finds no row NULLs every target. The two new surfaces were found by the 2026-09-30 backlog triage's challenge round; 2529 / 2535 / 2540 had been read, not run.

**Reproduced first** against `53bcef0` on the local stack at 0126, through PostgREST: `supabase/tests/aal1-definer-boundary.test.ts`, aal1 sessions being FRESH password-only sign-ins of users who DO hold a verified factor (the stolen-password shape; the helper asserts `aal1` from the token). 18 of 23 failed, each for the reason it names (aal1 moves, direct writes, the dropped name — checkout refused "Pick a staff member" —, aal1 and cross-organisation references, aal1 mandate and MFA-status reads, and the catalogue listing exactly `record_key_movement`, `next_reference`, `org_mfa_status`, `mandates_safe`); the 5 that passed are the aal2 paths the fix must keep.

**Fix — 0127**, md5-guarded against 0116 / 0033 / 0028's bodies and 0036's view (and one overload each, definer, no view options), `lock_timeout` 5 s and the one-transaction check (0113 / 0126's rule), the view hashed under a fixed `search_path`:
- `mfa_satisfied()` in all three functions (42501, "Second factor required.", `close_deal`'s text) and in the view's WHERE (aal1 gets no rows, as from the table).
- `next_reference` also binds `p_org` to `current_org_id()` for an API USER — recognised by `current_setting('role') in ('authenticated', 'anon')`. Measured inside a definer body: `current_user` is the owner, but the role GUC still shows PostgREST's SET ROLE (`service_role` / `authenticated`; a direct session `none`), with or without JWT claims, so it does not depend on hosted's `sb_secret_` key format. The service role (the property importer) and direct sessions (the demo script via execute_sql) are unchanged; the API can set no other role.
- `key_movements_insert` dropped; `property_keys_movement_fields_guard`, a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger keyed on `current_user in ('authenticated','anon')`, refuses a key born out of the office or with a holder and any change of status / holder. Inside `record_key_movement` (a definer) the statement runs as its owner, so the RPC passes. A trigger, not column grants: a column grant refuses a payload that merely NAMES `status` (42501) before the `(org_id, property_id)` key can answer 23503 — 0122's tenant tests send `status: "in_office"` and would have been blinded to the key they pin (PR #74's "one predicate can mask another"). Its function is revoked from all four roles, as 0117's guard.
- The holder resolved into separate locals: an active same-organisation profile still wins; otherwise the typed name is kept.
- No signature, ACL, owner or generated-type change; app code unchanged.

**The hosted preflight changed the file before it was applied.** Read-only on hosted: ledger 0126, every hash as expected EXCEPT `next_reference` — md5 `55789a1a…`, not 0033's `6b096cb7…`. Byte for byte it is 0033's body with its one comment line (`-- was: format('GNK-%s-%s', …)`) removed: the 2026-08-20 apply went through a path that dropped it. The guard accepts exactly those two texts. Rehearsed twice in a rolled-back transaction on the local stack rebuilt to hosted's state (hosted's `next_reference` text, hosted's session `search_path`): preflight and postflight pass, ACLs unchanged. NOTE for the next file that guards a function by md5: a hosted body can differ from the repo's by comments — hash hosted first.

**The catalogue.** The test's last block lists every SECURITY DEFINER function in `public` that `authenticated` may execute and every non-invoker view it may read (`has_any_column_privilege`, so a column-granted view counts), and fails unless the body calls `mfa_satisfied(` — block and line comments and string literals stripped, whole word — or the surface is in a reviewed exemption map with its reason (the identity helpers, `rls_bare_auth_calls`, the anon surface, PostGIS). A materialized view never counts as guarded (its WHERE runs at refresh). Proven with planted mutants, each caught: an unguarded function, one naming the check only in a `--` comment, one in a `/* */` comment, one in a string literal, one calling a lookalike (`zz_xmfa_satisfied()`), a plain definer view and a column-granted one. The same stripped check is in 0127's postflight and in two new `verify-restore.sql` invariants (with the trigger function's grant pin and the migrations baseline 127).

**Review before push (ULTRACODE).** Four lenses — bypass hunting, regression across every caller (app, scripts, cron, seeds, e2e, gnk-web, release-compat), test validity, hosted-apply safety — each finding put to two skeptics told to refute it: 32 agents, no bypass, nothing high or medium upheld. Folded in before push: column-granted views and materialized views in the catalogue, the stricter body check, the lock / one-transaction rule, one-overload / definer / no-options preflight asserts and a clearer view-hash message, the trigger function revoked from service_role and pinned, the full rollback recipe, `next_reference`'s rule narrowed to the two API user roles (a direct session that had run `SET ROLE postgres` was refused), tests for the holder-id-only insert and the direct-session path, and sequential fixture enrolment. Filed, pre-existing: the media importer's `mandates_safe` read as the service role (BACKLOG).

**Tests / measured locally.** The new file 24/24 at 0127 (RED 18 of 23 at 0126, before the review's additions); the full DB suite green bar `rls.test.ts` #41 / #42 / #57 (the shared stack's leftover `MEDIA-*` listings; red on main too); RLS 13 now asserts the refusal of a direct movement for admin, agent and listing manager; unit 2910 with the restore-pack baseline; the restore pack runs clean on local and its 0127 rows read true; tsc / eslint clean; generated types unchanged. RLS matrix updated (and its stale 0029 opt-in sentence corrected). Rollback: a forward migration, spelled out in 0127's header.

## T-export-filter-shape — a list export records which filters shaped it, never what was typed into them (2026-10-01; no migration)

**Defect (BACKLOG, found by T-key-holder-shape's scouts).** `logListExport` writes an `exported` event — hash-chained, beyond erasure — and the contacts, keys, leads and properties routes handed it the request's RAW search params. The search box matches a contact's name, phone and e-mail and a key's holder, so a name searched and then exported was in the chain for good; leads recorded every parameter at all, including ones the list never reads. Pipeline, performance, tasks and viewings already passed shape only. **Reproduced first:** `tests/unit/export-routes-audit.test.ts` drives the REAL route handlers with a request searching "Maria Georgiou" plus a junk parameter and reads the payload handed to `logEvent` — the name reached all four (6 of 6 RED).

**Fix.** `auditFilters(parsed, vetting)` in `lib/services/export-audit.ts`: each route passes its PARSED filters and an explicit vetting map keyed by the list's own filter names (a typo is a type error); a value is kept only when it passes (`vet.oneOf(vocabulary)`, `vet.uuid`, `vet.number`, `vet.flag`) and is a primitive; any other set filter is recorded as `true` — used, never typed; unset filters are left out. `q` has no vetting anywhere; contacts' `nationality` is a free-text input and has none either; an off-vocabulary contact `source` / `type` / `temperature` / `language` or a malformed `agent` id (a crafted URL) becomes `true`; properties' `view` and `page` are not recorded (presentation, not rows). Production held 0 `exported` events, so nothing in the chain needed attention. Nothing reads `payload.filters` back. Tests: the route test (6, RED 6 at main) and `auditFilters`' edge cases (NaN, arrays, objects, unset values).

## T-redact-lead-notes — redacting an enquiry takes the desk's notes with its message, and resumes (2026-10-01; no migration)

**Defect (BACKLOG, found by T-lead-lost-reason-shape's review).** Article 17 on an UNLINKED enquiry (`redactLead`) rewrote `leads.message` and logged `redacted`, but left the lead's `interaction_notes` — the desk's own words about the person, which 0094 made erasable so they could go with the message, and which contact erasure and `redact_stale_enquiries` both blank. The 2026-09-30 triage's challenge added: once the message showed the marker the Redact button was gone, so notes left behind could never be finished from the app. **Reproduced first** on the real stack (`supabase/tests/redact-lead-notes.test.ts`, the real action, an aal2 admin session, the real service client and chain): against main the note text survived the redaction, and a lead whose message was redacted but whose notes were not was refused "Already redacted." (2 of 2 RED).

**Fix.** `redactLead` keeps the message write, now exactly-once (`contact_id is null` as before, and not already the marker — null-safe — so two presses or the retention sweep racing it redact and log once), and logs its one `redacted` event (payload `{}` as before) right after that write. Then it blanks the lead's notes through `createAdminClient()` — 0094's only admitted UPDATE (`body = null`, `redacted_at` set), as contact erasure does — bounded by the caller's org, `entity_type = 'lead'`, this lead, and `redacted_at is null`. It RESUMES: a lead whose message is already the marker skips the message write (and logs nothing) and finishes the notes; a failed notes step answers "The message is redacted, but the notes on this enquiry are not — use Finish redaction on its row."; a press with nothing left to do is "Already redacted." as before. It now RETURNS its own refusals as `{ error }` instead of throwing (one path still throws: `getLead`'s "Lead not found" for a lead the caller cannot read, which a production build shows generically) — a production build replaces a thrown Server Action message with a generic one, so none of these sentences (the old ones included) reached the admin; the button throws the returned sentence on the client, where the toast keeps it. The leads page asks — for an admin only, one read for the page, none when no row qualifies (`loadLeadsWithUnredactedNotes`) — which redacted, unlinked rows still hold notes, and `LeadRowActions` offers those "Finish redaction" (behind "More…" on a phone, like Redact). A note logged on a lead AFTER its redaction is offered the same way: the person asked to be erased. And `createContactFromEnquiry`'s own link write now refuses a redacted lead as `lead-contact-link`'s does — before, a redaction committing while a colleague created the contact could leave a lead both redacted and linked, the state `redactLead` exists to refuse. The `conversation_logged` events (note id and digest, never the words) are untouched, and the chain still verifies. Production held 0 redacted leads and 0 lead notes: no backfill. Typed `lost_reason` and task titles on a lead stay with the operator's erasure-scope decision (BACKLOG "Erasure leaves a lost deal's or lead's typed reason…", "Erasure leaves a person's name in task titles").

**Review before merge (ULTRACODE).** Four lenses (privacy completeness, redaction correctness, test validity, regression) — 15 findings, every in-scope one folded in before merge: the event moved back to the message write (completion logging produced a second event for a late note or a racing press, and none at all when the notes step failed on a lead without notes); the exactly-once guard; `{ error }` instead of throws; the `createContactFromEnquiry` marker guard; the e2e spec opening "More…" on a phone (it failed CI's mobile project), seeding inside `try`, and no longer deleting hash-chained events from the shared fixture organisation; a vacuous chain assertion replaced by `verify_events_chain`. Mutants — the notes write without its org bound, the message write without its exactly-once guard, the link write without its marker guard — each fail exactly the test written for them.

**Tests.** Unit (`redact-lead-notes.test.ts`, 8; the first version's RED 3 of 7 at main): the message write's exactly-once clause and its one event, the notes write's exact bounds and patch, the failure answer (the message's event kept), the resume (no event), a lead redacted meanwhile by someone else (no second event, notes still finished), nothing-left, and that a linked lead, a non-admin, or a lead linked mid-flight never creates the admin client; `leads-link-contact.test.ts` adds the link write's marker clause. `lead-unredacted-notes.test.ts` (3). Real stack (2): this lead's notes blanked; another lead's, and a row of ANOTHER organisation planted naming this lead, untouched; `conversation_logged` count unchanged and `verify_events_chain` true; one `redacted`; the resume (no event); the page query before and after. E2E `tests/e2e/lead-redaction.spec.ts`, desktop and mobile: Redact from the inbox blanks the note; a half-redacted row shows "Finish redaction", which completes it (RED at main: the note survived).

**Landing (2026-10-01, on the operator's "merge #2", then "merge #86, #13 and #87").** #87's `checks` was red on `bd70174` and `c03281b` at its first verification step — `npm audit`, for a critical Next.js advisory published the day before (GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j) — while rls and e2e were green. Neither app was exploitable (gnk-crm has no `next/og`; gnk-web's OG route takes no input); on the operator's choice both repos took `next` 16.3.8 first (`T-next-16-3-8` below), then #87's branch was updated with main (`eaf26a1`, all three jobs green, run 36847652005) → main `bf5275e` (pinned to `eaf26a1`) → Vercel `dpl_3j5qU5eQMkzQWDvXuBWT2Lz9pDRk` READY, no runtime errors, `/leads` and the four export routes 307 signed out → CI on the merge commit: green — checks, rls, e2e (run 36849265871). Nothing was exported or redacted in production to exercise it.

## T-next-16-3-8 — next 16.3.5 → 16.3.8 in both repos for GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j (2026-10-01; gnk-crm PR #86, gnk-web PR #13)

GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j (critical, published 2026-09-30 14:48Z): remote code execution in `next/og`'s Node.js `ImageResponse` when attacker-controlled values reach SVG content, attributes or styles; `next` >= 16.2.0, < 16.3.6; the Edge implementation and input-free renders are not affected.
