## T-system-event-types — a session cannot write the records only the system writes: `enquiry_alert`, `lead_escalation` and `opened` (2026-10-03; migration 0138)

The operator's "go next"; BACKLOG "A session may write ANY event type…" — the machine-reader addendum T-routing-own-org's and T-share-link-opened-own-org's reviews added (the desk-alert closure trusting a session-writable `enquiry_alert`; a session's `opened` line rendering like a buyer's view).

**The gap, reproduced first.** `events_insert` (latest 0134) let an aal2 session write any event type in its own organisation but six strings 0128 / 0131 / 0134 reserve (won / lost / won_override on deals; stage_changed, erased and retention_purged under any entity_type). Three more are written only by the system — every literal and every computed `eventType` in lib/ and app/ was read: the app writes none of them through a session — and machines read them as the system's word: `claim_notification_jobs` (0111) closes a pending desk alert as already sent when it finds an `enquiry_alert` line with `outcome = 'sent'` for the lead; `lead_escalation` is the escalation's own record (0107 / 0111); a session's `opened` share_link line renders as "Proposal link opened — N properties", like a buyer's view, with a payload of its choosing. Pinned RED by `supabase/tests/system-event-types.test.ts`: through PostgREST an aal2 agent's insert of each type — and of two under a foreign entity_type — was accepted; and, end to end inside a rolled-back transaction, a member's forged `enquiry_alert` 'sent' line for a real website enquiry made the claim hand out nothing and closed the job (`accepted` / `legacy_sender`): the desk was never told. RED at 0134's policy: 9 of 19 — 6 behavioural (the five refusals, the forged closure), 3 0138's own state. Hosted, read-only on 2026-10-03: one organisation; no `enquiry_alert` 'sent' line with an actor and no actor line of the three types.

**Fix — 0138.** `events_insert` gains `event_type not in ('enquiry_alert', 'lead_escalation', 'opened')` under any entity_type, as 0134 did for erased / retention_purged; 0128's, 0131's and 0134's clauses kept verbatim, each its own clause (their restore-pack rows read them). Preflight (under the fixed search_path): the check exactly 0134's; the hoisted-policy count noted. Postflight: the check exactly 0138's; the hoisted count unchanged; no bare helper or auth call. A READ-ONLY diagnostic, the file's last row, in three columns — `forged_sent_alerts` (an actor's 'sent' line: the shape the closure honours, which no system writer signs), `actor_request_lines` (the shape the two staff-called definers sign), `actor_other_lines` (any other actor line of the three types, a line with no outcome included) — and the boundary, the largest event id when sessions lost the right, kept as the policy's comment as 0131 / 0134 kept theirs. No function changes; types identical; not deploy-coupled (the deployed app writes none of the three through a session): hosted first, then merge.

**Who still writes them.** RLS binds sessions only: the definers — the claim and finish functions, the escalation sweep, `resolve_share_link` (the share page calls it as anon) — with a null actor; two definers a staff member calls, which sign with the caller — `request_enquiry_alert_retry` ('retry_requested') and `request_lead_escalation_recovery` ('recovery_requested'); the service role (the alert worker, the tests' fixtures).

**Not closed (BACKLOG, the ANY-event-type entry).** `assigned` is not reserved — the app writes it through the session — so a member can still steer the round-robin within their organisation. The closure has no actor predicate: a 'sent' line written before 0138 would still close its alert (hosted held none). The staff RPC-by-hash `opened` route (its own entry). Look-alike types are accepted and print as written.

**Tests.** `supabase/tests/system-event-types.test.ts` (19): PostgREST refusals (403 / 42501, the RLS message) for lead `enquiry_alert`, lead `lead_escalation`, share_link `opened`, contact `enquiry_alert` and deal `opened`; the forged-'sent' closure end to end in a rolled-back transaction — refused at 0138 with the job handed out, accepted at 0134's policy with the job closed; what still works — a session's ordinary event (201), the service role writing all three, the share page called AS anon writing its own `opened` line; the policy text exactly 0138's; the replay over 0134's policy (the diagnostic as the last row, the boundary comment); the diagnostic asserted column by column (a forged 'sent' line, a request-shaped line and two other actor lines — one with no outcome — each in its column; null-actor lines in none; every plant kept); the preflight refusal (applied twice); the postflight refusal (the file without the clause); refusals before the first change; the one-transaction guard; the rollback restoring a session's right to write all three; the restore pack's 0138 row true now and false at 0134's policy. `share-link-opened-own-org.test.ts` now plants its staff-session `opened` lines as postgres — the pre-0138 shape they stand for.

## T-contact-links-org-isolation — every link onto a contact belongs to the contact's organisation (2026-10-03; two releases — release 1: the application, no migration; release 2: migration 0139)

The operator's "go next … fix all"; the 2026-09-30 triage's #5: BACKLOG "Ten links onto `contacts` are still single-column" and "`createLead` creates the contact before the lead and never re-reads the property".

**The gap.** Ten foreign keys reference `contacts(id)` alone — leads.contact_id, deals.buyer_contact_id / seller_contact_id, offers.contact_id, share_links.contact_id, buyer_requirements.contact_id, mandates.owner_contact_id, properties.owner_contact_id / developer_contact_id, contacts.merged_into_id — and every insert / update policy checks only the caller's organisation. Organisation B could hang its rows on organisation A's contact, and a real id (accepted) against a missing one (23503) told B the contact exists. Hosted, read-only on 2026-10-03: the ten keys as 0001 left them, 0 cross-organisation rows on every link.

**Why two releases, and why the names are kept.** The fix is 0123 / 0126's: each key re-made `(org_id, <col>) → contacts (org_id, id)`. But the deals and properties CSV exports embed their parties with COLUMN hints (`contacts!buyer_contact_id`), and a column hint answers PGRST200 once its key is composite — the exports would 500 the moment the migration applied. A constraint-NAME hint resolves only while that name exists, so with 0123 / 0126's renames (`<t>_org_<x>_fkey`) no hint string works on both sides of the migration; `lib/queries/enquiry-contact-suggestions.ts` already hinted `leads!leads_contact_id_fkey`. Decision: the migration KEEPS every constraint's name (drop and re-add under the same name, in one statement), and release 1 moves the hints to those names first. Rehearsed on the local stack (four keys re-made composite under their old names, committed, then restored identical): the old column hints answered 400 PGRST200, the new name hints 200, and `supabase/tests/contact-link-embeds.test.ts` passed unchanged; hosted PostgREST resolves a name hint on its already-composite `viewings_org_contact_fkey` and refuses the column hint the same way (read-only GETs, `limit=0`). House rule from here: a re-key keeps the constraint's name.

**Release 1 — the application (no migration).**
- The exports hint by constraint name: `lib/services/deal-export.ts` (`contacts!deals_buyer_contact_id_fkey`, `contacts!deals_seller_contact_id_fkey`) and `lib/services/property-export.ts` (`contacts!properties_owner_contact_id_fkey`, `contacts!properties_developer_contact_id_fkey`, and `profiles!properties_assigned_agent_id_fkey` ahead of the profile re-key). Unit tests pin the strings and refuse any `!<col>_id(` hint; `supabase/tests/contact-link-embeds.test.ts` runs the deal select and the property select exactly as the route builds it (with the plain and the inner-joined mandate embed) as an aal2 session, and pins that each hinted constraint exists on the column it is named for — it runs at 0138 here and, unchanged, at 0139 in release 2's CI.
- Eight actions wrote a form's contact id straight through and would have shown the driver's 23503 after the keys: createLead, updateDealSection (buyer, seller), saveOffer (create, edit), createShareLink, createAvailabilityLink, saveMandate (create, edit), createProperty, updatePropertySection (owner, developer). Each now calls `contactLinkError` (`lib/services/contact-reread.ts`) BEFORE any side effect, for a link the row does not already carry (an unchanged buyer, the offer's default — the deal's own buyer —, an unchanged owner are not read again), and answers "That contact is no longer available to you." or, when the read itself failed, "Could not check that contact just now — please try again." — writing nothing. `contacts_select` is organisation-wide for every role (measured), so the read refuses exactly what the key will refuse: never a colleague's contact. createProperty reads before `generateReference`, so a refused party burns no sequence number.
- createLead re-reads its property (and picked contact) BEFORE the duplicate check and the typed enquirer's contact insert: a refused property no longer leaves an orphan contact with a chained `created` event.

**Tests (release 1).** `lib/actions/contact-link-reread.test.ts` (27) — every refusal writes nothing and reads by the posted id (fakeClient's default `{data: []}` would read as "found", so every refusal scripts `{data: null}` explicitly); two new parties with one unseen refused; unchanged parties not read; a real save reaches the write; a failed read reported as a failure. `lib/services/contact-reread.test.ts` (5) — every id not some, repeats read once, failure vs absence. RED 14/22 before the fix (the first file as first written). Five mutants, each killed by its own test. 3017/3017 unit tests; tsc and eslint clean.

**Review (ULTRACODE).** Release 1: four read-only lenses (correctness, completeness, tests, release / claims) with two refuting skeptics per finding (18 agents): no correctness defect, no missed writer (buyer-requirements, linkLeadContact, createContactFromEnquiry, convertLead, renewMandate, syncPropertyOwner and the unit writers are re-read, org-checked or same-organisation by construction). Folded in: a failed read is told apart from a missing contact; the helper pinned directly; the missing two-party and not-read-again tests; the live test builds the route's exact selects. (Correction: release 1's first commit message says "seven actions" and lists eight.)

**Release 1 landed.** PR #99 → main `8c9f329` (2026-10-03 20:29:58Z, pinned to `7efb7ac`; standalone `gh pr merge … --repo`) → Vercel production `dpl_6tD8Vhfr42gBFucKAwDztSBkmmiP` READY 20:31:00Z, aliased; `/login` 200, protected routes (both exports included) 307; no runtime errors. CI on the merge commit green (checks, rls, e2e). Remote branch deleted.

**Release 2 — migration 0139.** Each of the ten keys is dropped and re-added under the SAME NAME in one `ALTER TABLE` (so PostgREST never sees two relationships for a column — an unhinted embed would answer PGRST201 — and every name hint keeps resolving): `(org_id, <col>) → contacts (org_id, id)` on `contacts_org_id_id_key` (0123), the predecessor's delete rule kept (CASCADE for buyer_requirements, NO ACTION for the rest — `contacts.merged_into_id` stays NO ACTION: SET NULL would clear the pointer unarchiveContact's guard reads, CASCADE would delete merged duplicates), an `(org_id, <col>)` index each (partial where nullable; share_links and mandates had none on the column). Preflight, under ONE LOCK on the eight tables (contacts first) taken before anything else: aborts on any cross-organisation row (ten named counts), on a key that is not its original (0001's; 0023's for share_links, 0043's for buyer_requirements — the message names the file), on a second key on a link column, on a unique index over one (it would answer 23505 before the key's 23503 — 0122), on a taken index name, and unless exactly ten keys onto contacts sit on the eight tables. Postflight: each key composite, validated, its rule, NO ACTION on update, MATCH SIMPLE, its name; no single-column key onto contacts left (the BACKLOG VERIFY); the ten index definitions; every org_id NOT NULL; contacts_org_id_id_key and the three 0123 / 0126 contact keys unchanged; then ten probes in two throwaway organisations — A's ten same-organisation links accepted, each B row naming A's contact refused by ITS key at ITS step — and a summary as the file's last row. No function, policy, grant or row changes; no function writes any of the ten columns (pg_proc).

**Deploy order and rollback floor.** APPLICATION FIRST: release 1 merged and confirmed deployed (above), 0139's CI green on a head containing release 1 (`ffa101d`: rls 1237/1237 on a fresh DB that applied 0139 — the new file 51/51, `contact-link-embeds` 9/9 — and e2e, the export specs included), then hosted 0139, then merge. ROLLBACK FLOOR with hosted at or past 0139: never roll the application back past `8c9f329` — an older application's exports answer PGRST200 → 500. Rollback: a forward migration restoring each key's original single-column definition under the same name (buyer_requirements' with CASCADE) and dropping the ten indexes, wrapped in 0139's own lock discipline (lock_timeout, the one-transaction guard, one LOCK on the eight tables before the ALTERs — `revert-0139.ts`'s statement has neither and is for the tests' rolled-back use); it must precede 0123's revert, the only one that drops `contacts_org_id_id_key`; then the types, the pack's three 0139 rows and its pin, the test file, the BACKLOG entry and the contact-merge test's B-side plants. No data moves either way.

**Tests (release 2).** `supabase/tests/contact-links-org-isolation.test.ts` (51), RED 16 at 0138, each for its reason (measured per section — section 1's accepted RED writes commit cross-organisation rows and section 4's replays count mismatches database-wide): through PostgREST as B's admin, each link naming A's contact refused 23503 by its key with the SAME message as a missing contact (no oracle), B's own accepted; the delete rules (a requirement still cascades; a contact named by a lead or a merged duplicate cannot be deleted); the catalogue (thirteen composite keys onto contacts, the BACKLOG VERIFY 0, the ten index definitions, no unique index on a link column, PostgREST's ONE relationship each way for every single-link table, and the ROLLBACK FLOOR — a column hint answers PGRST200, its name hint resolves); the file replayed over 0138 (summary row), refusing over a single mismatch on EACH of the ten links with the right count and changing nothing, refusing over drift (a different rule, a second key, a unique index, a taken name), stopping when run twice, its preflight ahead of every change and each key dropped and re-added under its name in one statement, the one-transaction guard, the rollback recipe restoring 0138's catalogue (and with it a cross-organisation lead), the LOCK holding the file at a writer on the last table until 55P03; ## T-sw-no-private-cache — the service worker keeps nothing a session or a share link can see; offline, every page load gets one generic page (2026-10-05; no migration; LANDED 2026-10-05 — PR #101, main `5782218`, deployed)

**The brief.** An external audit's priority 1, examined at `4dc234d`: the production worker cached authenticated CRM pages and revocable proposal pages and replayed them offline whatever the current session or the token's validity. Taken as a hypothesis. `origin/main` was still `4dc234d` when this started, so the audited code was the current code.

**Finding: CONFIRMED, reproduced before any change — and wider than reported.** `public/sw.js` at `4dc234d`:
- :97-104 — every same-origin GET navigation answering `res.ok` (bar an `RSC` header) went into `gnk-pages-v1` whatever its `Cache-Control`; Next sends `private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate` on every dynamic page and the Cache API ignores it. :107-109 — on a network failure that copy was replayed, with no session, token or validity check. Online, a 307/401/403 passed through but never evicted it; a withdrawn link's neutral page (a 200) overwrote it only if the buyer revisited online first.
- :57-59, :73 — any path ending in png/jpg/jpeg/webp/avif/svg/ico/woff/woff2 went cache-FIRST into `gnk-static-v1`, navigations included, so it was stale for good even online; a subresource redirected to `/login` was stored as the login page under the asset's name. No current route answers a private 200 at such a path (`[id]` lookups 404/500 on a suffixed uuid), so this was latent.
- :108, :110 — `caches.match()` with no `cacheName` searched every cache on the origin.
- :43 — activation kept every cache ending in `v1` (a fix at the same VERSION would never have removed `gnk-pages-v1`) and deleted any other cache that did not.
- :53 — the sign-out purge deleted `gnk-shell-v1` too, and only install writes it: after the first header sign-out the offline page was gone for good on that device. Only `LogoutButton` posts the purge; `/session-clock`'s "Sign in again", the 2FA screen's "Sign out instead", expiry, a ban and a global sign-out from another device purge nothing. The registrar sits in the ROOT layout, so buyers on `/p/<token>` install the worker too, and a buyer never signs out.
- `tests/e2e/pwa.spec.ts:78-79` asserted the words `PURGE` and `/api/` in the worker's source. Its header comment contains both: the test passed with the purge listener and the `/api/` guard deleted.

**Reproduction.** (1) A node:vm probe ran the unmodified worker with synthetic responses: twelve cases, plus a pass-through negative control that showed no risk on any of them. (2) A real browser against a production build of `4dc234d`, with synthetic records: `gnk-pages-v1` held the contact page (with the signed-in user's e-mail from the header), the proposal, `/contacts?q=<client name>` (the search term is the cache key), `/dashboard`, and the contacts CSV fetched through a plain link — the shape `reports/performance` renders. `<a download>` links never reached the worker in Chromium, but a plain link, a new tab or a typed export URL did. (3) The same legacy build behind a proxy that really dropped the connection: the contact page was replayed with the server unreachable.

**Fix — `public/sw.js` v2 is an allowlist, not a pattern.**
- **Navigations: network only.** The server's answer — the live page, a redirect, a 401/403, a withdrawn link's neutral page — passes through, and nothing of it is kept. When there is no answer, the generic `/offline` page from `gnk-shell-v2` stands in. It is never a copy of the page asked for. That includes an export or `.ics` file opened by navigation (a plain link, a new tab, a typed URL): network only like any page, and offline the generic page.
- **`gnk-shell-v2` holds `/offline` alone.** It is precached with `credentials: "omit"` and `redirect: "error"`, refused unless 200, and stored again by the next page load if anything removed it. The icon and the manifest are no longer precached. v1 never served the manifest, and the icon now comes from the network and the HTTP cache like any image.
- **`gnk-static-v2` holds `/_next/static/` alone.** A response is stored only as a 200 that was not redirected and is not marked `private`/`no-store`, and it is read from that cache only. Offline, a miss is a network error, never the offline page. The write is started on a clone before the page reads the body, and `waitUntil` is called synchronously. A file extension qualifies nothing.
- **Everything else is not intercepted.** That covers `/api/`, RSC payloads, non-GET requests (a form posted before hydration included), images, and an export fetched with `<a download>`. They fail as they would with no worker.
- **Activation** deletes every `gnk-` cache of another version before claiming, and the deletion is awaited. Caches without the prefix are left alone. Each page load also deletes the three v1 caches **by name**, in case a v1 write still in flight re-created one. The by-name rule keeps a successor's install-time caches safe while v2 is still the active worker.
- **Sign-out.** `purgeOfflineCaches` and v2's PURGE listener now keep `gnk-shell-*`: it holds only the anonymous `/offline`. Sign-out and the next sign-in are client-side navigations, so nothing would re-store it before a full page load. On a device still running v1, the old copies are cleared by v1's own listener plus the window-side delete, as before.
- **Wording.** `/offline` no longer promises that visited screens work offline. `pwa.tsx`'s docblock no longer claims a timeout it never had. The comments in `proxy.ts` and `pwa.spec.ts` that said a gated precache would store a redirect to `/login` now say it stores nothing.

**Why this shape.** (a) Keeping page caching and purging on every session change cannot work: the worker never sees expiry, a ban or a sign-out on another device, and a buyer never signs out. (b) Per-session cache partitions or an encrypted offline store would be new infrastructure for a requirement nobody has stated; the brief excluded them. (c) Unregistering the worker (a kill switch) would cost the one product benefit left: the honest "nothing was sent" screen an agent needs after a failed slip signing (T-pwa). (d) This keeps installability and that screen, and stores only bytes that are the same for every visitor.

**Upgrade and rollout — what a deploy can and cannot do.** A device runs v2 only once it is online again and its browser fetches `/sw.js`; any page load triggers that check. On the cross-build run, v2 was active 4.2 s after the first online page load, and before any further navigation `gnk-shell-v2` was the only cache left. Until then the device keeps `gnk-pages-v1`, and its v1 worker keeps replaying it. Measured: a device offline across the deploy still replayed the contact page. Open tabs are claimed (`skipWaiting` + `clients.claim`). A v1 write still in flight at the switch is never read, and the next page load deletes it. No deploy reaches a device that never comes back online. Nothing here changes Vercel, the database or any setting.

**ROLLBACK FLOOR — never roll the application back past `5782218` (the merge of PR #101).** A rollback re-serves the v1 `/sw.js`, which every device re-installs the next time it is online (the bytes differ). v1's activation then deletes `gnk-shell-v2` and `gnk-static-v2`, and it resumes storing pages in `gnk-pages-v1`. On a device that stays offline after the roll-forward, those copies outlive it. If the worker itself must change, ship a new VERSION forward.

**Tests.**
- **`tests/unit/service-worker.test.ts` (72),** on `lib/testing/service-worker-harness.ts`. It runs the real worker file in a simulated worker scope against synthetic markers and reads every Cache Storage entry.
  - 23 tests run under three page-header variants: Next's `private, no-store`, `public, max-age=60`, and none. So no privacy assertion leans on today's headers.
  - They cover private pages, session end, a second account, 401/403, a withdrawn proposal, query variants, extension look-alikes, a navigated CSV, and the RSC, API and POST pass-throughs (a POST navigation included).
  - Build assets: the storage rules, reads from the worker's own cache only, and an offline miss that must fail as a network error.
  - The offline page: the anonymous precache, a refused precache, the fallback reading only its own cache, sign-out keeping the page, and the page stored again after a loss.
  - A successor's caches surviving, and a failing write.
  - Three more tests replay a v1 device on the same Cache Storage (`tests/fixtures/sw-legacy-v1.js`, byte-identical to `4dc234d`'s worker below its 8-line header; `tail -n +9 tests/fixtures/sw-legacy-v1.js | sha256sum` = `4beda2ef…`): the v1 positive control, activation cleanup asserted at the END of activate's lifetime (awaited work only), and a late v1 write.
  - The harness snapshots Cache Storage when each event's lifetime settles, before fire-and-forget work drains. Its writes and deletes take real time, so a detached operation is visible as detached.
  - **RED:** pointed at v1 (`SW_UNDER_TEST=tests/fixtures/sw-legacy-v1.js`), vitest reports 53 failed and 19 passed of 72. The passes: per variant, the three pass-throughs (401/403, RSC/API, writes), the refused precache on a server error, the offline asset miss and the successor's caches (v1 never sweeps); plus the v1 positive control, which always runs v1.
  - **Mutants:** 23, all killed. That includes the seven a review found surviving an earlier version of the suite: pages cached unless marked private, the GET guard removed, an unscoped asset read, offline HTML for a missed asset, a detached asset write, a detached activation cleanup, and a detached navigation sweep.
- **`tests/e2e/pwa-offline-privacy.spec.ts` (5)** runs against a production build in Chromium and reads Cache Storage itself.
  - It covers a fresh install; the same browser context upgraded from v1, with the positive control that v1 stores the pages and replays them offline; a buyer's withdrawn proposal; and session expiry, a second account and the header sign-out (offline page kept through it), with throwaway users.
  - The fifth is a no-worker control: the private page is served `no-store`, and an offline *navigation* to it (not a reload, which would fail regardless) fails.
  - **RED** against the `4dc234d` build: 4 of 5 fail, each listing the leaked entries; the control passes, as it should. **GREEN** 5/5.
  - It is the first test that clicks `LogoutButton`. The note in `tests/e2e/session-clock.spec.ts:40-50` ("asserting it again buys nothing") assumed a test that did not exist.
- `pwa.spec.ts` loses its two source-string assertions.

**Review (ULTRACODE).** Eight read-only agents covered four lenses (privacy and correctness; lifecycle and regressions; test validity; claims), with one refuting verifier per lens. They found no way for v2 to store or serve private content. Folded in from them: the sign-out purge keeping the offline page; the navigation sweep narrowed to v1's names; the synchronous `waitUntil`; the header variants, POST navigations and asset-read tests; the harness's lifetime snapshots; the rewritten HTTP-cache control; the rollback floor; corrected counts, quotes and comments. Not taken: a backoff for a failing `/offline` precache. Only a broken `/offline` triggers it, and the cost is one request per page load.

**Measured locally (2026-10-05).** `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` and `npm run check:static-routes` are clean, and unit is 3089/3089 (220 files). Full desktop e2e (setup + desktop, the CI projects) against `next start` of this branch: 302 passed, 0 failed, 0 flaky (15.1 min). The RLS suite was not run locally because nothing in the database changed; CI ran it (below).

**Other persistence, measured, not changed.**
- The HTTP cache: see the control above.
- Back after signing out: sign-out is a client-side (same-document) navigation, so Chrome's back-forward cache is not involved; Next's router handles Back. Within 2.5 s Back shows `/login` and nothing private. In one run, 500 ms after Back, the document's HTML still contained the previous user's e-mail. That is most likely the hard-loaded page's inline RSC data left in the DOM by the soft navigation: in memory, not in a cache.
- A tab left open keeps what it rendered after the user signs out in another tab (measured).

These are separate mechanisms, and this change claims none of them.

**Not done here** — BACKLOG "Offline privacy — 2026-10-05".

**Landing (2026-10-05, on the operator's "push it and land it" and "land it when green").** Branch pushed and PR [#101](https://github.com/KALAITSIDIS/gnk-crm/pull/101) opened from `1e3988a`. Branch CI run 37344242173 on that head was green on checks, rls and e2e; e2e passed 301, the new spec 5/5 among them, with none failed or flaky. Merged 17:26:31Z as main `5782218`, pinned to `1e3988a` (standalone `gh pr merge … --merge --match-head-commit`); `main` had not moved from `4dc234d`. Vercel production `dpl_DEjy4PBew1yxF8r3tCY7y6THGYRB` was READY 17:27:34Z and aliased to `gnk-crm.vercel.app`. Production probes, anonymous: `/sw.js` 200 serving `VERSION = "v2"` with `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate`; `/offline` 200 with the new copy, so the anonymous precache works in production; `/login` 200; `/dashboard` 307 → `/login`; a malformed `/p/` token 200 with the neutral page. No runtime errors since the deploy. Merge-commit CI (run 37348452361) was still running when this was written. No migration; hosted untouched. **Preview deployments differ:** they sit behind Vercel's login, so every anonymous request answers 302 to `vercel.com/sso-api`. The credential-less precache therefore cannot store `/offline` on a preview; the fallback there is the plain-text 503, and each page load makes one refused re-try. Production is public and unaffected. v1 managed on previews only because it fetched with cookies, which is exactly what v2 must not do. Devices update on their next online page load (measured locally: 4.2 s); a device that stays offline keeps its v1 copy until then.

## T-price-uplift-atomic — a bulk reprice and the price-list version that records it commit as ONE transaction; a retry is answered, never applied twice (2026-10-05; migration 0141; LANDED 2026-10-06 — hosted 0141 first, PR #106, main `f72c805`, deployed)

**The brief.** An external audit's priority 2, examined at `2ef18a1`: make bulk repricing and its price-list snapshot atomic, with correct audit events and safe retry behaviour. Taken as a hypothesis. `origin/main` was still `2ef18a1` when this started, so the audited code was the current code. The branch was cut from it in its own worktree (`.worktrees/gnk-crm/price-uplift-atomic`); the main checkout's uncommitted #90 landing records were left alone.

**Finding: CONFIRMED, reproduced before any change — and wider than reported.** `supabase/tests/price-uplift-actions.test.ts` drives the REAL `applyPriceUplift` / `createPriceListVersion` against a disposable stack (a second Supabase stack on ports 553xx, fresh from the migrations; a throwaway organisation plus a second one as the isolation control; two blocks, a blockless unit, an unpriced unit, a zero-priced unit, an archived priced unit, a unit under a phase). Against `2ef18a1` it failed 23 of 26; each scenario prints what the database holds afterwards:
- **Duplicate events.** Every moved unit got TWO `price_changed` lines: `trg_price_history`'s (0005) and the action's own `logEvents` copy with `source: "bulk_uplift"`. The timeline renders only from/to (`lib/services/events.ts`), so each unit showed "Price X → Y" twice; nothing rendered the extra keys.
- **Partial commits at every stage.** A refusal on a later unit's UPDATE, or on its `price_changed` line, left the earlier units repriced with history and events and no version. A refused header left every price moved ("Prices updated, but the version was not created"). Refused items left an EMPTY v1 header (0 items) that `price_lists_delete` lets nobody remove while it is the latest. A refused `price_list_created` left a complete version with no event — and the action THREW (Next hides the message in production). The standalone "New version" behaved the same: an empty header, or a version with no event.
- **Version allocation.** `max(version) + 1` was read without a lock: two concurrent snapshots, or a reprice and a snapshot, collided on `price_lists_project_id_version_key` (23505) — for a reprice, after its prices had moved.
- **Nothing tied the write to the preview.** A price edited after the page was drawn was uplifted again from its new value (reviewed 200.000 → 220.000; written 210.000 → 231.000). A unit added to the block after the review was repriced unseen. The same submission twice applied +10% twice and minted two versions; a double submit minted two versions and three `price_changed` lines per unit.
- **Archived units** — which the page never previews (it excludes them, as `container-units.ts` does) — were repriced, evented and alerted on.
- **An agent's direct call** (the action had no role check; only the page hid the form) repriced the unit assigned to them and wrote `price_changed` lines for five units RLS had silently NOT changed (a 0-row PATCH answers no error), then failed at `price_lists`. An aal1 session made the action throw ("Profile not found for authenticated user"); nothing was written.
- **The 1,000-row page.** A 1,200-unit project: 1,000 units repriced, 200 silently not, and a version of 1,000 items — every unit read was an unpaged PostgREST select (`max_rows = 1000`). The units page read the same way, so its preview stopped at 1,000 too.
- **Rounding.** The preview and the write multiplied in floating point: €50.000 + 0,1% is exactly €50.050, which the €100 rule rounds UP to €50.100; float made it 50.049,999… and wrote €50.000. 509 of the 679.677 percentage grid points sampled disagreed with exact decimals; fixed amounts never did.
- **Not reproduced:** a snapshot mixing pre- and post-reprice prices under a concurrent reprice and snapshot — the interleaving the harness produced kept both versions consistent. Closed by the locks regardless; reported as a risk, not a defect.

**Fix — `record_price_list_version` (0141), SECURITY INVOKER, called by both actions.** One function, two modes: no `p_mode` is the "New version" snapshot; `percent` / `fixed` is the reprice and its snapshot. In the caller's transaction:
1. The caller from the session (uid, aal2, organisation, role): admin or listing manager, checked before any row is read.
2. The project or phase locked **FOR NO KEY UPDATE** (see the review below for why not FOR UPDATE): every version and every reprice of it queues there, so `max(version) + 1` is read by one writer at a time. Then the caller re-read under the lock (0118's step 4b).
3. The operation id: `price_lists.operation_id` (unique per organisation) and `operation` (the request's md5 and the counts). The same id, same project, same user and same request answers `replayed` with the original version, counts and the changes read back from `price_history`; anything else under the same id is refused ("already used for a different change").
4. Every unit of the container locked FOR NO KEY UPDATE **in id order**, before anything is written.
5. Reprice only: the reviewed scope (`p_expected`: every unit the page previewed, priced or not, with the price it showed) must be exactly the scope now — direct, NOT archived, the block or all — or the answer is `stale` and nothing is written. Then the €100 rule in exact numeric (`round(price × (100 + amount), −4) / 100`, `round(price + amount, −2)`, floor €100, null/≤ 0 skipped, unchanged left alone), ONE UPDATE re-checked against the price each row was computed from (row count = changed), and the canonical trail COUNTED: one `price_history` row and one `price_changed` line per changed unit in this transaction, or the reprice is refused (a disabled trigger cannot make it record nothing).
6. The version: every priced direct unit (the snapshot's meaning since 0001, archived included), header + items (row count checked) + ONE `price_list_created` event carrying the operation (version, units, operation_id, and for a reprice source, mode, amount, scope, changed — ids and numbers, never the note).
Any refusal raises, so nothing is kept. `trg_price_history` is untouched and stays the ONE writer of per-unit history and `price_changed` — for direct edits and imports too. The actions write no event of their own any more.

**The application.**
- `applyPriceUplift` / `createPriceListVersion` call the function and never throw. P0001 is shown verbatim; 55P03 and 40P01 say "another change … nothing was changed, try again"; any other proven rollback says "nothing was changed"; an unknown outcome says "could not confirm — press again to check, the same submission is never applied twice" and is flagged `unconfirmed`. The error classifier moved from `lib/actions/deals.ts` to `lib/services/rpc-outcome.ts` (a "use server" file can export only async functions); the texts live in `lib/validators/price-lists.ts`.
- The bulk price-drop alert runs after a committed reprice — `applied`, or `replayed` from the read-back changes (the committing request may have lost its answer first; the alert's own guard keeps one open task per project). Its failure, or a failed page refresh, never turns a commit into an error.
- The forms mint the operation id at SUBMIT time, in a ref (`lib/utils/operation-id.ts`), keyed on everything the form sends: the same submission keeps its id; a change — including a redraw with new prices — gets a new one; after an UNCONFIRMED answer the id stays pinned whatever the form then holds, until an answer is definite.
- The reprice form sends `expected` (`reviewedScope`) and submits through `onSubmit` + `startTransition`, not `<form action>`. The snapshot form sends the latest version it shows, so a deliberate second snapshot is a new submission.
- The preview computes in exact decimals (`lib/services/price-uplift.ts`, BigInt), digit for digit with the database.
- The units page reads its units with `fetchAll` (ordered block, unit, id), so the preview — and the reviewed scope — covers every unit past 1,000.

**Why this shape.**
- **Invoker, not definer.** Every row the function writes, the caller could write through PostgREST under the same policies (`properties_update`, `price_lists_insert`, `price_list_items_insert`, `events_insert`, `require_aal2` on each), so the database keeps enforcing all of them statement by statement, and the function re-reads the caller under its lock in words of its own (measured: a listing manager demoted while the call waited is refused, nothing written). A definer would have to restate four tables' policies for no authority the caller lacks.
- **The version is the operation record.** Every successful submission creates exactly one header, so two nullable columns on it carry the idempotency key; a separate table would be a new RLS surface (aal2 coverage, grants, the PK catalogue) for the same record. Deleting a non-latest version or editing the columns can only turn a later retry into "already used", a stale refusal or — for a plain snapshot, which reviews nothing — one more identical version; never a second price change, because the reviewed-prices precondition refuses a request whose prices have moved.
- **The precondition is the reviewed scope, not `updated_at`.** The form already holds every unit and price it previewed; comparing those catches an edited price, an added, archived or removed unit, and a truncated page, with one message.
- **The trigger stays canonical.** Moving the per-unit line into the function would change the writer for direct edits and imports; the operation's context belongs on the version's event, and every event of the transaction shares its `occurred_at`.

**Deliberate behaviour changes.**
- Archived units are no longer repriced: the write now matches the preview. The snapshot still records every priced direct unit, archived included, as before.
- Rounding follows the stated rule exactly: half-way prices that floating point rounded down now round up, in the preview and in the database alike.
- No second `price_changed` line per unit; the version's event carries the operation's context instead.
- An agent, an aal1 session and another organisation's admin are refused up front with a sentence, and nothing is written.
- The default note keeps the old wording ("+3% on block A (2 units)").
- A stale review refreshes the page (the preview redraws from the current prices); an unconfirmed answer does not.

**Review (ULTRACODE).** Five read-only lenses (SQL and concurrency; security; pricing parity; the actions and forms; tests and migration), each followed by a refuting verifier, over the change as it then stood. Confirmed and fixed:
- **(high) A server-side "could not confirm" double-applied.** The action refreshed the page on an unknown outcome, the refreshed prices changed the form's key, and the next press — which the message invited — minted a new id that the database applied again. Fixed: no refresh on an unknown outcome, and the id stays pinned until a definite answer. Pinned by `lib/utils/operation-id.test.ts`, the action tests and the harness's "redrawn retry" case, which is refused rather than applied.
- **(high) The reprice form's Radix Selects jumped back to "All units · Percentage" after every action** — React resets a form after any action run from `<form action>`, refused ones included, and Radix answers the reset. Pre-existing. Reproduced: with the old wiring, a refused fixed +20.000 on block A redrew as €210.000 → €42.210.000 (+20.000% on every unit). Fixed by submitting through `onSubmit`; `tests/e2e/price-uplift.spec.ts` picks Block A / Fixed and fails on the old wiring.
- **(low) New deadlock paths.** With the project locked FOR UPDATE, the nightly sweeps (`create_followup_nudges`, `expire_mandates`: an event first, then a task naming the property — a foreign-key check, KEY SHARE) deadlocked with a call waiting for their chain lock. Reproduced ("deadlock detected"); fixed with FOR NO KEY UPDATE (0117's lesson); `price-list-version.test.ts` replays the sweep's order and passes. A writer that updates several of the same units in another order (the inherited-field sync, the contact merge) can still meet the id order; PostgreSQL then aborts one side (40P01), nothing of it is kept, and the actions ask for a retry — accepted and documented.
- (low) A replay never raised the bulk alert, so a reprice whose answer was lost server-side lost its alert. The replay now returns the changes read back from `price_history`, and the action raises it.
- (low) Tests that could not fail: the replay's creator check (both "another user" cases were refused by the request md5 alone — the tests now replay the admin's exact request; a mutant without the check fails both files), the event-count tripwire (a dropped `price_changed` line, history kept, is now refused and tested; the postflight and the restore pack now require both counts), a race barrier that waited on the chain lock rather than the operation key (a plain-version variant now waits on the transaction id itself), and regexes that required the `public.` prefix. The new e2e fixtures are removed in `afterEach`.
- (low) Two cross-tenant / insider limits, documented in the header and BACKLOG rather than fixed: another organisation's admin who knows a project's id can insert a version row against it (single-column `price_lists.project_id`) and so block its versions; the operation record is writable through `price_lists_update`.
Refuted: the operation record letting an insider make a genuine reprice a silent no-op (ids are random and minted at submit); the >1,000-unit finding (the page was already paged by then); two docs-timing points (the records land in their own commit, as for 0137/0138).

**Mutation.** Six SQL mutants committed to the isolated stack, both DB test files run against each, the real body restored after: stale check never fires (4 failures), replay ignores the request digest (3), units not locked (2), archived units back in the reviewed scope (17), rounding truncates instead of half-away (4), the creator check removed (2). The UPDATE's re-check against the computed-from price survives — an equivalent mutant while the units are locked; it is the second line if the lock is ever removed, and the "units not locked" run shows it doing exactly that.

**Measured locally (2026-10-05).** typecheck, lint: clean. Unit 3130/3130 (222 files). The disposable stack reset fresh from this branch's 140 migrations: the full DB suite 1309/1309 (59 files, the first run on that stack, 293 s). Desktop e2e against `next start` of this branch, pointed at the same stack: 305 tests — 303 passed, 1 skipped (`property-parties` skips itself here), and 1 failed only because `deal-close-outcomes.spec.ts` defaults its `DB_URL` to the shared stack, so its injected failure landed there; re-run with `DB_URL` on the disposable stack, that spec passed 7/7 (15.9 min). The new and changed tests: `supabase/tests/price-list-version.test.ts` (45), `price-uplift-actions.test.ts` (27), `lib/services/price-uplift.test.ts` (+7, now 22), `lib/utils/operation-id.test.ts` (5), `lib/actions/price-list-actions.test.ts` (29), `tests/e2e/price-uplift.spec.ts` (4: the original, plus 1,001 units through the real page, a stale review with Block A / Fixed, and an answer dropped after the commit). RED/GREEN: the action harness 23/26 RED on `2ef18a1`, 26/26 GREEN; the 1,001-unit e2e fails on the old unpaged page ("Repricing 1 unit" where there are two); the stale e2e fails on the old form wiring; the sweep-order test fails on a FOR UPDATE body.

**Deploy order.** Additive: hosted 0141 FIRST, then merge. The deployed `2ef18a1` app keeps its direct PATCH / INSERT path against 0141 unchanged (its rows leave the two new columns null; tested). The deployed app keeps writing duplicate `bulk_uplift` lines until the merge deploys, so record 0141's diagnostic row from a re-run AFTER the deploy. **Rollback:** the application first (to a release that does not call the function), then a forward migration dropping the function, the index, the pairing check and the two columns in one transaction (`supabase/tests/revert-0141.ts`). Rolling the database back first fails closed: the new actions get PGRST202 and say nothing was changed.

## T-media-upload-authz — a property-media upload is authorised BEFORE any privileged work, and an attempt that does not commit takes back what it wrote (2026-10-06; no migration; LANDED 2026-10-06 — PR #108, main `f4c940b`, deployed)

**The brief.** An external audit's priority 3, examined at `5ed1d6c` (= `origin/main` when this started, so the audited code was the current code): authorise property-media uploads before privileged work, and clean up failed uploads correctly. Taken as a hypothesis. Branch `fix/media-upload-authz` in its own worktree (`.worktrees/gnk-crm/media-upload-authz`); the main checkout's uncommitted #90 landing records were left alone. The offline-cache (T-sw-no-private-cache) and atomic-repricing (T-price-uplift-atomic) fixes are untouched.

**The permission model, read from the database (not substituted).** `properties_select` is organisation-wide (`org_id = current_org_id()`). `property_media_insert` (0002, restated by 0100) admits admin and listing_manager, or an `agent` whose `properties.assigned_agent_id = auth.uid()`, within the caller's organisation; `owner_portal` / `developer_portal` / `partner_portal` never. `require_aal2` is RESTRICTIVE on both tables and on `profiles`; `current_org_id()` / `current_role_gnk()` return NULL for a deactivated profile. Storage has NO policies on `storage.objects`: only the service role writes the `media` (public) and `documents` (private) buckets.

**Finding: CONFIRMED, reproduced before any change — and one consequence worse than reported.** `supabase/tests/media-upload-authz.test.ts` drives the REAL action against a disposable stack (ports 553xx, fresh from the 0001–0141 migrations) with real Storage, steering the session and service-role fetches to inject failures where they happen. Against `5ed1d6c` it failed 18 of 25:
- **Privileged work for a caller who may not upload.** A same-organisation agent who is not assigned READS the listing, so the action processed the image and made **7 service-role storage requests** (5 uploads, then the rejected-row cleanup's removals) before RLS refused the row.
- **Partial failure left siblings.** One refused, thrown, or stored-but-lost upload (original or any rendition) left **4 objects** behind and no row; a thrown upload escaped `Promise.all` before slower siblings settled. A two-file batch whose second file failed left **9 objects for 1 row**, and its error did not say the first file was saved.
- **A lost insert answer deleted a committed row's files.** The insert committed, its answer was lost, and the action's any-error cleanup removed all five objects: **a live `property_media` row with 0 objects** — a broken gallery entry and a portal-feed photo that 404s.
- **A failed `media_uploaded` event after the commit THREW**, so a saved upload looked failed (and a retry would duplicate it).
- An aal1 or deactivated session made no storage request, but the action THREW (`Profile not found…`) instead of returning a result — production strips thrown text.
Passing at `5ed1d6c` (the controls): admin / listing manager / assigned agent uploads, a floor plan, another organisation's admin (RLS hides the listing), and a reassignment while the upload was in flight (the old rejected-row cleanup handled that one). The unit harness `lib/actions/media-upload-attempt.test.ts` failed 28 of 35 against the old action for the same reasons.

**The fix (application only).**
- `lib/services/media-upload.ts` — `mayInsertPropertyMedia(profile, property)`: the insert policy said once in the application (same organisation; admin / listing manager; or the agent assigned). `putAttemptObjects`: uploads every object of an attempt and waits for EVERY request to settle (answered, refused or thrown); `upsert` stays false, so an attempt never overwrites. `discardAttemptObjects`: removes every path the attempt may have written — not only the ones that answered success, because an errored or thrown upload can still have stored its object — via the verified `removeObjectsOrFail`; an absent object counts as removed (so a repeat is harmless); a path the store refused as already present (409) is left alone; an unverified removal returns false and is reported. `insertDefinitelyRefused`: only an error WITH a code (SQLSTATE or PGRST) is a definite rejection — postgrest-js resolves a network failure as `code: ""` and does not retry POSTs. `reportMediaUpload`: console line + `Sentry.captureMessage`, shape only (ids, server-built paths; never a DB/storage message or a file name).
- `uploadPropertyMedia`, in order: `z.guid()` on the property id; every file of the batch checked (type, size) before anything is read or written; `getCurrentProfile` (an RLS read of `profiles`: signed-out, aal1 and deactivated sessions have none) caught into a RESULT; the property read through the session WITH its error checked (fail closed); `mayInsertPropertyMedia`; the gallery read with its error checked (an unread gallery would number from 0 and crown a second cover). Only then `createAdminClient`, the watermark, the pipeline and the uploads. One `attemptId` per file names every object AND the row (`id: attemptId` on the insert). The insert stays on the caller's SESSION — RLS keeps the last word (a reassignment or deactivation since the check is refused there, and the attempt is discarded). A coded insert error → discard. An uncoded one → read the row back by id: found → committed, carry on; not found or unreadable → keep the files, report `insert_unknown` with the paths, and tell the user "could not confirm whether it was saved — refresh the page before uploading it again". After a commit: the event in try/catch (a failure keeps row and files, is reported, and returns `warning`), `recomputeQuietly` instead of `recomputeQualityScore`, the site knock (never throws). A batch stops at its first failure and returns `saved` and "N of M saved, then …"; committed files stay and get their refresh.
- `MediaActionState` gains optional `saved` and `warning`; the media tab toasts `warning`. Its flow is otherwise unchanged (browser downscale, one file per request).

**Why this shape.**
- **An application predicate, not a database function.** The smallest change that refuses before privileged work and keeps one boundary: no migration, no deploy coupling, and the insert policy stays the final word. The cost is two statements of one rule, so the DB test holds them together: for admin, listing manager, assigned agent, same-org unassigned agent and another organisation's admin, `mayInsertPropertyMedia` and a real session insert give the same answer (aal1 is refused one step earlier, by the profile read). A policy change that is not mirrored fails that test. The alternative — a `SECURITY INVOKER` function used by both the policy and the action — is recorded in BACKLOG.
- **Discard every attempted path, not only the successes.** For an object store "failed" is not "absent": the answer, not the write, can be lost. The paths are server-built and carry a fresh uuid, so this reaches only the attempt that built them.
- **Never delete on an unknown insert outcome.** Not finding the row in a read-back is not proof that the insert will not commit (it may still be landing); a committed row pointing at deleted files is the worse failure. The price is a possible orphan, which is findable (below).
- **The event stays a follow-up, not a transaction partner.** Making the row and its `media_uploaded` line one transaction would need an RPC and a migration; the failure is reported to Sentry with the attempt id and the user is told. Recorded in BACKLOG.

**Limits (stated, not solved).** Storage and Postgres share no transaction: this is compensation, not rollback. (1) A process that dies between the uploads and the insert, or during the cleanup, leaves objects with no row. (2) A request the client gave up on (a thrown fetch) may still be written by the store AFTER the cleanup's removal; `Promise.all` over non-rejecting wrappers waits for every request the client still holds, which closes the race for slow uploads, but not for one the client abandoned. (3) An unknown insert outcome keeps the files; if the row never committed they are orphans, and if it did, the row exists without its `media_uploaded` event (the action stops before logging it). (4) A removal the store refuses is reported, not retried. All four are visible to one read-only query (row id = attempt id since this change; the join uses the row's own path columns, so pre-change rows — whose path id differs from the row id — are covered too):
```sql
select o.bucket_id, o.name, o.created_at
from storage.objects o
where o.bucket_id in ('media', 'documents')
  and o.name ~ '^properties/[0-9a-f-]{36}/(original/[0-9a-f-]{36}\.(jpg|png|webp)|[0-9a-f-]{36}_(thumb|card|full|jpeg)\.(webp|jpg))$'
  and not exists (
    select 1 from property_media m
    where o.name in (m.storage_path_original, m.path_thumb, m.path_card, m.path_full, m.path_jpeg))
order by o.created_at;
```
Sentry's `media_upload.cleanup` / `media_upload.insert_unknown` messages carry the attempt id and paths of each case. An object older than the longest upload (minutes) with no row is an orphan; remove it with the Storage API, never SQL (storage refuses SQL deletes). No automated sweep was added; no production object was listed, inspected or deleted.

**Measured locally (2026-10-06).** typecheck, lint: clean. Unit 3165/3165 (223 files) — `media-upload-attempt.test.ts` 35 (28 RED on `5ed1d6c`, 35 GREEN); two older fixtures updated (`media-upload-renditions.test.ts` used `"prop-1"`, which the guid check now refuses; `media-event-payload.test.ts`'s rejected-row fixture lacked the `42501` code PostgREST sends, and both mocks gained `recomputeQuietly`). DB: `media-upload-authz.test.ts` 25 (18 RED on `5ed1d6c`, 25 GREEN) and the full DB suite on the freshly reset disposable stack: 1334/1334 (60 files, 278 s). Browser: `tests/e2e/event-typed-text.spec.ts`'s photo upload through the real media tab, served by this branch's `next dev` pointed at the same stack: 3/3 (setup + the upload). The orphan query was proved on that stack: a planted object with no row is listed, then removed through the Storage API.

**Deploy order.** None to coordinate: no migration, no hosted change. Rolling the application back restores the old behaviour exactly (rows written by the new code differ only in having `id` = the attempt id in their paths, which nothing reads).

**Landing (2026-10-06, on the operator's "push it and land it").** The branch's first CI run (37527713722 on `297ab0d`) was red on `checks` only: an advisory published that day (GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w, sharp <0.35.5, high — its bundled librsvg) failed `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` on every branch; `rls` was already green. Fixed apart, as a lockfile-only PR [#109](https://github.com/KALAITSIDIS/gnk-crm/pull/109) (`npm audit fix --omit=dev --package-lock-only`: the sharp family only, 27 entries, sharp 0.35.4 → 0.35.5, libvips 1.3.3 → 1.3.4; media tests 27/27 on the new binary; CI green on `af72ee3`), merged as main `b94a71e` and deployed, then merged into the branch (`3030801`). CI on `3030801` green on checks, rls and e2e (run 37530703905) — the media change tested on sharp 0.35.5. PR [#108](https://github.com/KALAITSIDIS/gnk-crm/pull/108) merged 21:15:00Z as main `f4c940b`, pinned to `3030801` (standalone `gh pr merge … --merge --match-head-commit`). Vercel production `dpl_AVE9qFiH7gvr7h7rwJc64j13GSub` succeeded; merge CI green (run 37532521504); production `/login` 200, `/properties` unauthenticated 307 → `/login`. No production upload was made and no production object was listed or removed.

**Not done here** — BACKLOG "Media uploads — 2026-10-06 (T-media-upload-authz)".

## T-media-insert-outcome — a code on the media insert's error is not proof the row was refused; only an understood refusal deletes an attempt's files (2026-10-07; no migration)

**The brief.** An operator-supplied finding against `372ff5b` (= `origin/main` when this started): `insertDefinitelyRefused()` returned `Boolean(error?.code)`, so `uploadPropertyMedia` deleted an attempt's objects on ANY coded insert error, a committed row included. Taken as a hypothesis. Branch `fix/media-insert-outcome` in its own worktree; the main checkout's uncommitted HANDOFF / BACKLOG / DECISIONS edits were left alone. gnk-web untouched (no contract depends on this).

**Finding: CONFIRMED, on the real stack, by a genuine database answer.** The harness in `supabase/tests/media-upload-authz.test.ts` sent the insert POST TWICE (the replay is injected; nothing in production is known to replay a POST): the first committed, and the second was answered by the local database itself — HTTP 409, `23505` on `property_media_pkey`. The old action treated that code as a refusal and removed all five objects: **a committed `property_media` row with 0 objects** (`added: 0, committed: 1`; the scope test 9c then found 10 missing paths). With a SIMULATED coded answer after a real commit (`PGRST001`, `08006`) the old action did the same and never read the row back. The unit harness failed 37 cases on the old source (the action, the classifier table, the deal-close unknowns). An uncoded transport error (`code: ""`) was already handled — the control.

**What the codes actually mean (read from source, measured where possible — a 31-agent research workflow, every "definite" class challenged by skeptics).** Versions: postgrest-js / supabase-js 2.110.2; PostgREST v14.5 on the local stack and on hosted as recorded by `supabase link` on 2026-08-31 (not re-measured); v16.1 on CI's fresh stacks; PostgreSQL 17.6. PostgREST builds **PGRST111 / PGRST112** in its response AFTER the transaction ended — measured: HTTP 500 with the row committed. **57014 / 53xxx / 58xxx / XX000** can be reported for a COMMIT that went through (a cancel handled after CommandComplete, an out-of-memory in post-commit stats, a PANIC in the commit critical section). A lost COMMIT reply arrives as `code: ""` (measured on 14.5 and 16.1). **Class 08** comes from whatever sits in front of Postgres (libpq never synthesises one here). **PGRST001** was measured NOT to follow a commit on 14.5 / 16.1, but that rests on hasql internals — it stays unknown by policy, as do PGRST000 and every unclassified code. **23505** on this table can only be the attempt id's primary key (the only unique constraint; the id is a fresh uuid per attempt), so it means a row with THIS id exists.

**The fix.**
- `lib/services/rpc-outcome.ts` — `certainlyRolledBack(code: unknown)` is now an ALLOWLIST: PGRST002 / 003, 100–102, 105–108, 114, 115, 117, 118, 121–128, 200–205, 300–303 (raised before the transaction ran, or after PostgREST condemned it); SQLSTATE classes 0A, 21, 22, 23, 25, 2D, 40 (not 40003), 42, 44, 54, 55, P0 (raised while a statement runs or in pre-commit work). Everything else — no code, a non-string code, 08 / 53 / 57 / 58 / XX, PGRST000 / 001 / 103 / 111 / 112 / 116, never-raised 104 / 120, any future code — is unknown. The new set is a strict SUBSET of the old one: no caller can newly delete, or newly say "nothing changed", where it did not before.
- `lib/services/media-upload.ts` — `insertDefinitelyRefused` delegates to it, minus `23505` (read it back).
- `lib/actions/media.ts` — any answer that is not a definite refusal, and a "success" that names no row, is read back by the attempt id; only a read-back naming THIS attempt's id counts as saved (a gateway `{}`, or postgrest-js's `[]` for a 404 with an array body, is not a row — found by the review). Otherwise the files are kept, `media_upload.insert_unknown` is reported and the user reads "could not confirm". A definite refusal without a message no longer throws after its cleanup.

**Effect on the other callers (`close_deal` in deals.ts, `record_price_list_version` in units.ts).** For 57014, 53 / 58 / XX, 40003 and unclassified codes they now answer "could not confirm" instead of "nothing was changed". Both RPCs are idempotent (close_deal re-reads; 0141 replays by operation id), so the cost is a message, never data. `deal-won-close.test.ts` moved 57014 from its "definite" list to its unknowns (with PGRST001); `price-list-actions.test.ts` gained 57014 and XX000 rows.

**Kept as it was.** Authorisation before any privileged work; the insert on the caller's session (RLS the last word); 42501 a definite refusal that removes only its own attempt's objects (real RLS refusal mid-flight, DB test 4); private originals and floor plans; settled-upload cleanup; batch counts; the post-commit warning.

**Measured locally (2026-10-07).** Unit: `media-upload-attempt.test.ts` 76, `rpc-outcome.test.ts` (new) 83, `deal-won-close` / `price-list-actions` green; full unit suite green; tsc, eslint clean. Mutants: the old truthiness read-back (3 killed), the type guard removed (4 killed). DB, shared local stack (ledger 0140 — `price-uplift-actions` needs 0141 and runs on CI's fresh stack): `media-upload-authz.test.ts` 28/28 with the fix, 24/28 on the old source (5b, 5c, 5d, 9c); `deal-close-actions` + `deal-close` 123/123. Review: a 30-agent adversarial workflow (5 lenses, 2 skeptics per finding, a completeness critic over the eight acceptance criteria) — 5 findings upheld, all folded in (the read-back identity check; comment accuracy on PGRST001; numeric-code, range-edge, price-list 57014 and batch tests), 7 refuted.

**Limits (stated, not solved).** (1) Hosted PostgREST's version and the gateway / pooler path in front of it were not re-measured; nothing measured here shows a hosted POST replay. (2) 42501 stays definite although a file-permission PANIC inside the commit can carry it (needs a storage fault and a crash) — accepted. (3) Class 55 is definite because `property_media` has no deferred constraint, constraint trigger or NOTIFY; adding one would need it re-examined. (4) An unknown outcome that DID commit still has no `media_uploaded` line and no score refresh (BACKLOG, unchanged); a kept attempt that never committed is an orphan found by `T-media-upload-authz`'s query.

**Deploy order.** None: no migration, no hosted change; a revert restores the old behaviour exactly.
